sw.text: Nahitaji kupumzika siku moja au mbili.
alt: Lazima nipumzike siku moja au mbili.

en.text: I'm going to stay home today.
Please get well soon.

sw.note: Pona haraka is what you say to a sick friend.

en.text: How are you feeling now?

sw.note: -je at the end asks how.

en.text: Did you take your medicine?
Drink a lot of water.
I hurt my knee yesterday.

sw.note: goti langu liliumia = class 5 agreement.

en.text: I twisted my ankle.
I'm careful with what I eat.

alt: Huwa niko makini na chakula changu.
sw.note: ni-na-cho-kula = what-I-eat.

en.text: I don't smoke.

sw.note: si-vuti = I-do-not-pull, the verb for smoking.

en.text: I sleep early, that helps me a lot.
My health is good, thank God.

sw.text: Afya yangu ni nzuri, namshukuru Mungu.
alt: Afya yangu ni safi, Mungu ashukuriwe.

en.text: I go for a check-up once a year.

sw.text: Napima afya mara moja kwa mwaka.
alt: Huwa naenda kupima afya kila mwaka.

en.text: I want to build a house here.
I bought a piece of land.

sw.note: kiwanja = a plot; shamba = a farm or larger land.

en.text: The land is outside the town.

alt: Shamba liko nje kidogo ya mji.
sw.note: kiwanja kiko = class 7 agreement.

en.text: It's a quiet place, I like it.

sw.note: na-pa-penda = I-it-like, for a place.

en.text: We're starting the work next month.

sw.note: mwezi ujao = class 3 agreement.

en.text: How long will the building take?

sw.note: ujenzi utachukua = class 11 agreement.

en.text: How many workers do you need?

sw.note: vibarua wangapi: people take wa- agreement.

en.text: When can you start?
How much will the whole thing cost?
Can you give me a written price?
We're building the walls from earth.

sw.note: Rammed earth: kuta za udongo uliogandamizwa, shortened here.

en.text: The earth walls keep the house cool.

sw.text: Kuta za udongo hufanya nyumba iwe na ubaridi.
alt: Nyumba ya udongo haina joto ndani.

en.text: We're mixing the soil with lime.

sw.note: chokaa = lime.

en.text: We need more sand and water.
Where can we get the materials nearby?

sw.text: Tunaweza kupata vifaa wapi hapa karibu?
alt: Vifaa vya ujenzi vinauzwa wapi hapa?
sw.note: vifaa = class 8.

en.text: The builders are coming tomorrow.

sw.note: fundi = builder or skilled worker; plural mafundi.

en.text: The builder said it will take three months.

sw.note: miezi mitatu = class 4 number agreement.

en.text: Please show me the plan again.

sw.note: ramani = the drawing or plan.

en.text: I want big windows for the air.

sw.text: Nataka madirisha makubwa ili hewa iingie.
sw.note: madirisha makubwa = class 6 agreement.

en.text: The roof needs to be done before the rain.

sw.text: Paa linatakiwa kumalizika kabla ya mvua.
alt: Lazima tumalize paa kabla mvua haijanyesha.
sw.note: paa is class 5: linatakiwa.

en.text: We need to dig for the water first.
Is there water on the land?
How deep is the well?

sw.note: kisima kina kina = the well has depth.

en.text: We're putting the kitchen on this side.

sw.note: jiko = kitchen or cooking place.

en.text: I want one big room for working.

sw.text: Nataka chumba kimoja kikubwa cha kufanyia kazi.
alt: Nataka chumba kikubwa cha kazi yangu.
sw.note: chumba kimoja kikubwa = class 7 agreement.

en.text: Can you finish this part this week?

sw.text: Unaweza kumaliza sehemu hii wiki hii?

en.text: The work is going slowly.
They finished the floor yesterday.
It's looking really good so far.
I go and check the site every week.

alt: Kila wiki nakwenda kuona kazi inavyoendelea.

en.text: I want to do it properly, not fast.

sw.note: Haraka haraka haina baraka — the proverb behind this.

en.text: We'll plant some trees around the house.
One day this will be our home.

sw.text: Siku moja hapa patakuwa nyumbani kwetu.
alt: Siku moja hii itakuwa nyumba yetu.
sw.note: pa- is the place subject prefix: patakuwa.

en.text: It was blessed.
God bless you.

sw.note: a-ku-bariki = may-he-you-bless.

en.text: Thank God for today.

alt: Ahsante Mungu kwa siku ya leo.

en.text: We're blessed today.
It was a blessed morning.

alt: Asubuhi ya leo ilikuwa njema sana.

en.text: Congratulations, my friend.
I'm happy for you.
That's wonderful news.

sw.note: habari njema = class 10 agreement.

en.text: Happy birthday.

alt: Nakutakia heri ya siku yako ya kuzaliwa.

en.text: I wish you all the best.
May everything go well for you.

sw.note: li-ku-endee = may-it-for-you-go.

en.text: Safe travels, my friend.
Have a blessed day.
Thank you for everything.
I'm grateful for your help.

sw.note: msaada wako = class 3 agreement.

en.text: You've been very kind to me.
I'll never forget this.

sw.note: si-ta-li-sahau = I-will-not-it-forget, class 5.

en.text: Sorry for your loss.

sw.note: Pole kwa msiba is the set condolence phrase.

en.text: My thoughts are with your family.

sw.note: Swahili comforts with prayer: I pray for your family.

en.text: Be strong, we're with you.

sw.text: Uwe na nguvu, tuko pamoja nawe.

en.text: We're celebrating tonight.
I'm invited to a wedding.

sw.note: nime-alikwa = I-have-been-invited, the passive.

en.text: It was a beautiful ceremony.
Everyone came together for it.

sw.text: Watu wote walikusanyika kwa ajili yake.
alt: Watu wote walikuja kwa ajili hiyo.

en.text: We prayed together this morning.
Life is good right now.

sw.note: maisha ni mazuri = class 6 agreement.

en.text: I count my blessings every day.

alt: Kila siku nashukuru kwa baraka nilizo nazo.
sw.note: baraka zangu = class 10 possessive.

en.text: Everything happens for a reason.

sw.note: jambo lina = class 5 agreement.

en.text: I'm thankful for my health.

alt: Nina shukrani kwa afya niliyo nayo.

en.text: Peace be with you.
Enjoy the celebration.
See you at the party tonight.

sw.text: Tutaonana kwenye sherehe usiku wa leo.
sw.note: Tutaonana = his sign-off, see you.

en.text: That's something to be happy about.
Right now I'm just gathering some sentences.
I'm practising speaking.
We're going to translate all of these.

sw.note: tuta-zi-tafsiri = we-will-them-translate, class 10.

en.text: I'll say some more sentences when I'm finished.
Okay, so I have some more questions.

sw.note: maswali mengine = class 6 agreement.

en.text: I was thinking of some things to say in there.

sw.text: Nilikuwa nafikiria mambo ya kusema humo.

en.text: That's part of how I speak.

sw.text: Hiyo ni sehemu ya jinsi ninavyoongea.
sw.note: ni-na-vyo-ongea = the way I speak.

en.text: The sentences will be good.

sw.note: sentensi zitakuwa nzuri = class 10 agreement.

en.text: I want to learn Kiswahili first.
After that I want to learn a tribal language too.

sw.text: Baada ya hapo nataka kujifunza lugha ya kabila pia.

en.text: It's still going to be hard work.
I speak to my phone so it can hear my own sentences.

sw.text: Naongea na simu yangu ili isikie sentensi zangu mwenyewe.
alt: Nasema kwenye simu yangu ili inase sentensi zangu.

en.text: I've been speaking out loud for a day or two.

sw.text: Nimekuwa nikiongea kwa sauti siku moja au mbili.
alt: Ni siku mbili hivi naongea kwa sauti.
sw.note: kwa sauti = out loud.

en.text: I'm learning Kiswahili.
I'm still a beginner.
I practise a little every day.
How do you say this in Kiswahili?

sw.note: i-na-itwa-je = it-is-called-how.

en.text: What does that word mean?

alt: Maana ya neno hilo ni nini?
sw.note: neno hilo lina = class 5 agreement.

en.text: Can you repeat that, please?
Say it one more time, slowly.

sw.text: Sema tena mara moja, pole pole.

en.text: Did I say that correctly?
Please correct me when I'm wrong.

sw.note: ni-ki-kosea = when-I-err.

en.text: I know a few words only.

sw.note: maneno machache = class 6 agreement.

en.text: I understand more than I can speak.
I'm not afraid to make mistakes.

sw.note: si-ogopi = I-do-not-fear.

en.text: Speaking is the hard part for me.
I listen to the same sentences every day.

alt: Kila siku nasikiliza sentensi hizo hizo.
sw.note: sentensi zilezile = class 10 agreement.

en.text: I repeat out loud while I ride.

sw.text: Narudia kwa sauti nikiwa kwenye pikipiki.

en.text: I record myself speaking.

sw.note: ji- = myself.

en.text: I write down the words I forget.

sw.note: ninayosahau = which-I-forget, class 6 relative.

en.text: I want to speak with people, not just study.

sw.text: Nataka kuongea na watu, si kusoma tu.
alt: Sitaki kusoma tu, nataka kuongea na watu.

en.text: Please talk to me in Kiswahili.
Don't answer me in English.

sw.note: u-si-ni-jibu = you-not-me-answer.

en.text: I'll get better in a few months.

sw.text: Nitakuwa bora zaidi baada ya miezi michache.
alt: Miezi michache ijayo nitakuwa bora zaidi.
sw.note: miezi michache = class 4 agreement.

en.text: I study for thirty minutes every morning.

alt: Kila asubuhi nafanya masomo dakika thelathini.

en.text: Learning a language takes real work.

sw.note: ku-na-taka = it-requires, the verb noun takes ku-.

en.text: I'm going to keep going until I can speak.

sw.note: ni-weze = until I am able (subjunctive).

en.text: Oh wait, before I forget, I brought you some mangoes.

sw.note: kabla si-ja-sahau = before I forget.

en.text: I've been busy with the building work.

sw.text: Nimekuwa na shughuli nyingi za ujenzi.

en.text: The walls are finished, now we're putting on the roof.
I'll come on Saturday morning, God willing.

sw.note: Mungu akipenda = God willing, said after almost any plan.

en.text: Oh wait, do you have mangoes today?

sw.note: Ngoja kwanza = hold on a moment; good for reopening a talk.

en.text: Give me four, my fiancée really loves them.

sw.text: Nipe manne, mchumba wangu anayapenda sana.
alt: Naomba manne, mchumba wangu anayapenda sana.
sw.note: manne = four, the form for maembe; a-na-ya-penda = she loves them.

en.text: Two for today and two for tomorrow.

sw.text: Mawili ya leo na mawili ya kesho.
sw.note: mawili = two, the form that goes with maembe.

en.text: Oh, I forgot to buy water.
Cold, two bottles, please.
I've sent it to the same number.

sw.note: ileile = the very same (ile + ile).

en.text: No worries, I'll carry them in my hand.

sw.note: ni-ta-zi-beba = I-will-them-carry; zi stands for the bottles.

en.text: Yes, I'm building a house a little further down this road.

sw.text: Ndiyo, najenga nyumba mbele kidogo kwenye barabara hii.
alt: Ndiyo, najenga nyumba hapo mbele, kwenye barabara hii.

en.text: Yes, that's the one, we're still building.
Not yet, but I'm engaged.

sw.note: nina mchumba = I'm engaged (lit. I have a fiancee).

en.text: We haven't set the date yet.

sw.note: ha-tu-ja-panga = we have not yet set.

en.text: Me too. See you around, neighbour.
What's the problem, my friend?

sw.note: Tatizo and shida both mean problem; shida is more everyday.

en.text: I'll pick you up at six in the morning.

sw.text: Nitakupitia saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
alt: Nitakuja kukuchukua saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: ni-ta-ku-pitia = I-will-you-come by for. 6 a.m. = saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.

en.text: How much is it to fill the tank?
Please tell the driver to fill mine too.

sw.text: Tafadhali mwambie dereva ajaze langu pia.
alt: Naomba umwambie dereva ajaze langu pia.
sw.note: langu = mine, because tanki (tank) goes with la-: tanki langu.

en.text: Before you go, do you eat fish?

sw.note: kabla takes -ja-: kabla hujaondoka = before you leave.

en.text: Great, I'll buy fish at the market this afternoon.

sw.text: Safi, nitanunua samaki sokoni mchana huu.

en.text: No, just come.
Then let's say seven in the evening.

sw.note: saa moja usiku = seven in the evening.

en.text: I'll come and open the gate for you.

sw.note: ku-ku-fungul-i-a = to open for you.

en.text: See you at seven tonight.
Amen, you too.

sw.note: Amina is a common reply to Mungu akubariki.

en.text: No worries, tell me the price when you get here.

sw.note: u-ki-fika = when you arrive.

en.text: If I'm not there, give them to my fiancée.

sw.note: ni-si-po-kuwepo = if I am not around.

en.text: Thank you, see you on Saturday.
Now take me back home.

sw.note: ni-rudish-e = take me back (rudisha = bring back).

en.text: So the total is one hundred and fifty.

sw.text: Kwa hiyo jumla ni mia moja na hamsini.
alt: Sawa, jumla ni mia moja na hamsini.
sw.note: Kwa hiyo = so, therefore.

en.text: Then let's take the tarmac, I'm not in a hurry.

sw.note: Sina haraka = I'm not in a hurry (I have no hurry).

en.text: Drop me at the gate there, please.

sw.note: ni-shush-e = let me down (shuka = get down).

en.text: Oh, and my motorbike, where should I leave it?

sw.text: Na pikipiki yangu je, niiache wapi?
alt: Na pikipiki yangu je, niegeshe wapi?
sw.note: Na ... je? = and what about ...? ni-i-ache = should I leave it.

en.text: I'll be back before five in the evening.

sw.text: Nitarudi kabla ya saa kumi na moja jioni.
alt: Nitarudi kabla ya saa kumi na moja.
sw.note: saa kumi na moja jioni = five in the evening.

en.text: I won't be late, I promise.

sw.note: si-ta-chelewa = I-will-not-be-late.

en.text: Black tea, please.

sw.note: chai ya rangi = black tea.

en.text: Oh wait, where exactly shall we meet?
I've never been to your place, give me directions.

sw.note: si-ja-wahi = I have never.

en.text: Okay, I'll call you when I get to the market.

sw.note: ni-ki-fika = when I arrive.

en.text: I'll ask her if she's free.

sw.note: kuwa na nafasi = to be free (not uko huru).

en.text: It's still morning there.
Okay, I'll give her your greetings.

sw.note: ni-ta-m-pa = I-will-her-give.

en.text: What should I bring for your parents?

sw.note: ni-wa-letee = should I-them-bring for.

en.text: Let me call my mother now, good night.

sw.text: Ngoja nimpigie mama sasa, usiku mwema.
alt: Ngoja nimpigie mama sasa hivi, lala salama.

en.text: I usually come at seven in the morning, after I meditate.

sw.text: Huwa nakuja saa moja asubuhi, baada ya kutafakari.
alt: Kwa kawaida nakuja saa moja asubuhi, baada ya kutafakari.
sw.note: saa moja asubuhi = seven in the morning: the clock starts at dawn.

en.text: Deal, and you teach me pull-ups.
Okay, my brother, don't be late.

sw.note: u-si-chelew-e = don't be late: the negative ends in -e.

en.text: Come tomorrow at a quarter to six in the morning.

sw.text: Njoo kesho saa kumi na mbili kasoro robo alfajiri.
sw.note: 5:45 a.m. = saa kumi na mbili kasoro robo alfajiri.

en.text: Don't worry, we'll start with twenty minutes.
Yes, YouTube pays me every month.

sw.note: hu- = usually: YouTube hunilipa = YouTube pays me (regularly).

en.text: Can you give me his number?
The sound is still very low.
And if it's still low tomorrow?

alt: Na kesho ikiwa bado iko chini?
sw.note: -ki- = if: i-ki-endelea = if it goes on.

en.text: Okay, so do I pay the five hundred now?

sw.text: Sawa, basi nilipe ile mia tano sasa?
alt: Sawa, nikulipe zile mia tano sasa?

en.text: Thanks, this time I'll keep it away from water.

sw.text: Asante, safari hii nitaiweka mbali na maji.
alt: Asante, sasa nitaiweka mbali na maji.
sw.note: safari hii = this time (safari is also a trip).

en.text: Okay, I'll wear my old shoes.

sw.text: Sawa, nitavaa viatu vyangu vya zamani.

en.text: I'll take an umbrella, you never know.

sw.note: huwezi kujua = you never know (lit. you cannot know).

en.text: Save a big fish for me.

sw.note: ni-wek-e-e = put aside for me.

en.text: Should I take them before or after eating?

sw.text: Nimeze kabla au baada ya kula?
alt: Nimeze kabla ya kula au baada ya kula?
sw.note: kumeza = to swallow: people say meza vidonge for taking tablets.

en.text: And what if the fever doesn't go down?

sw.note: -sipo- = if not: i-sipo-shuka = if it does not go down.

en.text: Okay, if I'm not better tomorrow, I'll go to the clinic.

sw.text: Sawa, nisipopata nafuu kesho, nitakwenda kliniki.
alt: Sawa, kesho nisipopata nafuu, nitakwenda kliniki.
sw.note: kupata nafuu = to get better.

en.text: And the cement, how much is it per bag?

sw.text: Na saruji je, ni bei gani kwa mfuko?
alt: Na saruji je, mfuko ni bei gani?
sw.note: Na ... je? = and what about ...?

en.text: So I'll send you twenty thousand for everything.

sw.text: Basi nitakutumia elfu ishirini kwa kila kitu.
alt: Basi nitakutumia elfu ishirini kwa vyote.
sw.note: elfu ishirini = twenty thousand: elfu comes first.

en.text: When will the sand arrive?
Great, I'll come and check at seven in the morning.

sw.text: Safi, nitakuja kuangalia saa moja asubuhi.
alt: Safi, nitapita kuangalia saa moja asubuhi.

en.text: How are the mother and baby doing?

sw.note: wa-na-endelea-je = how are they getting on.

en.text: I'll come, God willing.

sw.note: Mungu akipenda = if God wills; people add it to plans.

en.text: Okay. Can I bring my fiancée with me?

sw.text: Sawa. Naweza kuja na mchumba wangu?
alt: Sawa. Naweza kuja pamoja na mchumba wangu?
sw.note: mchumba = fiancé or fiancée.

en.text: My fiancée will be very happy to hear this.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu atafurahi sana kusikia habari hii.
alt: Mchumba wangu atafurahi sana akisikia habari hii.

en.text: We're still planning it.

sw.note: tu-na-i-panga: i = it, the wedding (harusi).

en.text: May God protect the baby.

sw.note: a-m-linde = may he protect him or her.

en.text: Nobody, I learn by talking to people.

sw.text: Hakuna mtu, najifunza kwa kuongea na watu.
alt: Hakuna, najifunza kwa kuongea na watu.
sw.note: kwa + ku- verb = by doing: kwa kuongea = by speaking.

en.text: Only a few weeks.
I woke up early, meditated, then went to the gym.

sw.text: Niliamka mapema, nikatafakari, kisha nikaenda jimu.
alt: Niliamka mapema, nikatafakari, halafu nikaenda jimu.
sw.note: ni-ka- = and then I: it links the steps of a story.

en.text: Okay, see you tomorrow, teacher.
What time are the workers coming tomorrow?

sw.note: Kibarua = a day worker on a site; many of them = vibarua.

en.text: Welcome, guys, thanks for coming early.

sw.note: Karibuni, asanteni: the -ni ending speaks to the whole group.

en.text: No worries, your guys are already here.

sw.text: Hakuna shida, vijana wako wamefika tayari.
sw.note: Vijana (young men) is how people talk about a fundi's crew.

en.text: You're late today, my brother.
You told me seven in the morning.

sw.note: Saa moja asubuhi = seven in the morning; the clock starts at dawn.

en.text: We're slaking the lime today.

sw.note: Kuzima chokaa = to slake lime (literally, to put the lime out).

en.text: How long does the lime need to sit?

sw.text: Chokaa inahitaji kukaa kwa muda gani?
alt: Chokaa ikae muda gani kabla ya kuitumia?

en.text: Cover the lime so it doesn't dry out.
I don't want cement, only lime.

sw.note: Many fundis say simiti for cement.

en.text: I bought ten bags of lime this morning.

sw.text: Nilinunua mifuko kumi ya chokaa leo asubuhi.

en.text: How much is one bag of lime?

sw.text: Mfuko mmoja wa chokaa ni bei gani?
alt: Mfuko wa chokaa ni shilingi ngapi?

en.text: How much sand do you put in the lime?

sw.text: Mnaweka mchanga kiasi gani kwenye chokaa?

en.text: So do we start plastering today?

sw.note: Kupiga lipu = to plaster a wall; many fundis say kupiga plasta.

en.text: Start with this wall.
This plaster looks beautiful.
I'll wet the walls every morning.
Who will wet the walls on Sunday?
There's a crack in this wall.

sw.note: Ufa = a crack; many cracks = nyufa.

en.text: Why did the wall crack?
Can you fill that crack today?

sw.note: Proverb: Usipoziba ufa utajenga ukuta. Fill the crack or build a wall.

en.text: Tell the driver to dump the sand here.
So what do we do to stop it cracking again?

sw.text: Basi tufanye nini ili ukuta usipasuke tena?

en.text: I'll order a lorry of sand for tomorrow.

sw.text: Nitaagiza lori la mchanga lije kesho.

en.text: I brought them tea and mandazi.

sw.note: Mandazi = the fried dough eaten with tea all along the coast.

en.text: Let's take a break for tea.

sw.note: Chai ya saa nne = the ten o'clock tea break on every site.

en.text: Seven hundred shillings a day, is that okay?

sw.text: Shilingi mia saba kwa siku, ni sawa?

en.text: I'll pay everyone on M-Pesa on Friday.

sw.text: Nitawalipa wote kwa M-Pesa siku ya Ijumaa.
alt: Ijumaa nitawatumia wote pesa kwa M-Pesa.

en.text: Send me all the workers' M-Pesa numbers.

sw.text: Nitumie namba za M-Pesa za vibarua wote.

en.text: Did everyone get their money?
Where's the other trowel?

sw.note: Mwiko = a trowel; the same word also means a taboo.

en.text: Don't rush the work, do it well.
No problem, I'm up before five every day.

sw.text: Hakuna shida, naamka kabla ya saa kumi na moja kila siku.
sw.note: Saa kumi na moja alfajiri = five in the morning.

en.text: My respects, ma'am.

sw.note: Say Shikamoo to any older person, man or woman; the answer is Marahaba.

en.text: I came to pay the rent.

sw.note: Kodi = rent; the same word also means tax.

en.text: What date is the rent due?
How much is the rent a month?

sw.text: Kodi ni kiasi gani kwa mwezi?
alt: Kodi ya mwezi ni shilingi ngapi?

en.text: Can I pay the rent on M-Pesa?
I just sent this month's rent.

sw.text: Nimetuma kodi ya mwezi huu sasa hivi.

en.text: Please send me a receipt for the rent.
How much is the deposit?

sw.note: Many tenants just say deposit: Deposit ni kiasi gani?

en.text: Will I get my deposit back when I move out?

sw.note: ni-ta-rudish-iwa = I will be given back.

en.text: The roof is leaking in the bedroom.

sw.text: Paa linavuja kwenye chumba cha kulala.

en.text: Since the rain on Monday night.
What time will he come?
I'll be home all morning.
The lock on the back door is broken.

sw.text: Kitasa cha mlango wa nyuma kimeharibika.
sw.note: Kitasa = a door lock; kufuli = a padlock.

en.text: I can't lock the door at night.
The caretaker has another key.

sw.note: Many people just say caretaker.

en.text: Can you leave the key with the caretaker?
Do I pay for water separately?
The water tank has been leaking since Monday.

sw.text: Tanki la maji limekuwa likivuja tangu Jumatatu.

en.text: The neighbours play loud music every night.

sw.text: Majirani wanapiga muziki kwa sauti kubwa kila usiku.
alt: Jirani zangu hupiga muziki kwa sauti kubwa kila usiku.

en.text: Can you please talk to them?
Why is the rent going up?
Two thousand more is hard for me right now.

sw.text: Elfu mbili zaidi ni ngumu kwangu sasa hivi.

en.text: I've never paid the rent late.
I understand, but my house will be ready in about three months.

sw.text: Naelewa, lakini nyumba yangu itakuwa tayari baada ya miezi mitatu hivi.

en.text: I'll move out at the end of next month.
I'll give you one month's notice.
Please come and check the house before I leave.

sw.text: Tafadhali njoo ukague nyumba kabla sijaondoka.

en.text: I'll leave the keys with the caretaker.
This house has worked well for me.
There's something else.
If I pay the rent on Monday, is that okay?

sw.note: ni-ki-lipa = if I pay.

en.text: My bike is at the mechanic today.

sw.text: Leo pikipiki yangu iko kwa fundi.
alt: Pikipiki yangu iko kwa fundi leo.
sw.note: kwa fundi = at the mechanic's place; kwa + a person = at their place.

en.text: Can you pick me up at home at seven in the morning?

sw.text: Unaweza kunichukua nyumbani saa moja asubuhi?
sw.note: saa moja asubuhi = seven in the morning; the Swahili clock starts at dawn.

en.text: I'm waiting for you at the gate.

sw.note: na-ku-subiri = I-you-wait for.

en.text: Take me to the matatu stage, please.
Same price as always, right?

sw.text: Bei ni ileile kama kawaida, sivyo?
sw.note: sivyo? at the end = right? or isn't it?

en.text: Come and get me from the stage at five in the evening.

sw.text: Njoo unichukue kwenye stendi saa kumi na moja jioni.
alt: Uje unichukue kwenye stendi saa kumi na moja jioni.
sw.note: saa kumi na moja jioni = five in the evening, the eleventh hour after dawn.

en.text: I'll call you when I'm back from Kilifi.

sw.note: ni-ki-rudi = when I come back.

en.text: Is this one going to Kilifi?

sw.note: Hii = this one, the matatu; say gari hili if you call it gari.

en.text: How much is the fare to Kilifi?

sw.note: nauli = the fare for a ride.

en.text: I have one big bag.

sw.note: mzigo = luggage, a load; in a matatu any bag is mzigo.

en.text: Do I pay for the bag too?

sw.note: ku-lipia = to pay for something.

en.text: Can I sit in the front?
Okay, I'll sit by the window.
What time are we leaving?
We've been sitting here for half an hour now.

alt: Tumekaa hapa kwa nusu saa sasa.

en.text: You said that twenty minutes ago.

sw.note: zilizopita = that have passed: dakika ishirini zilizopita = twenty minutes ago.

en.text: I only have a thousand-shilling note.

sw.text: Nina noti ya elfu moja tu.

en.text: Okay, don't forget my change.

sw.note: u-si-sahau = you-don't-forget.

en.text: You haven't given me my change yet.

sw.note: hu-ja-ni-pa = you-not yet-me-give.

en.text: Drop me at the next stage.

sw.note: ku-shusha = to let down; the conductor lets you down at a stage.

en.text: Conductor, I'm getting off here.
Please tell me when we reach Mtwapa.

sw.note: tu-ki-fika = when we arrive.

en.text: This one is full, I'll wait for the next one.
Move over a little, please.
Can I pay the fare with M-Pesa?
I'm going to Mombasa, I'll be back in the evening.
Where are the matatus to Mombasa?

sw.note: Many matatus take za: matatu za Mombasa; one takes ya: matatu ya Mombasa.

en.text: What time is the last matatu back?

sw.text: Matatu ya mwisho ya kurudi ni saa ngapi?
alt: Gari la mwisho la kurudi ni saa ngapi?

en.text: No thanks, my laptop is in this bag.

sw.text: Hapana, asante, kompyuta yangu iko kwenye mkoba huu.

en.text: Is someone sitting here?
How long does it take to Kilifi?
I've got a lot of errands in town this morning.

sw.text: Nina shughuli nyingi mjini asubuhi hii.
alt: Leo asubuhi nina shughuli nyingi mjini.

en.text: All right, so first the bank, then the hardware shop.

sw.text: Haya, kwanza benki, halafu duka la vifaa.
alt: Haya, kwanza benki, kisha duka la vifaa.
sw.note: duka la vifaa = hardware shop; many people just say hardware.

en.text: I want to finish everything before twelve.

sw.text: Nataka kumaliza kila kitu kabla ya saa sita mchana.
alt: Nataka kumaliza yote kabla ya saa sita mchana.
sw.note: Swahili hours start at dawn: saa sita mchana is twelve noon.

en.text: Can you watch my bike for a bit?

sw.note: ku-i-angalia = to watch it: the i- stands for pikipiki.

en.text: Is there a hardware shop near here?

sw.text: Kuna duka la vifaa karibu na hapa?

en.text: I want a strong padlock for the gate.
I need one kilo of three-inch nails.

sw.text: Nahitaji kilo moja ya misumari ya inchi tatu.
alt: Nipe kilo moja ya misumari ya inchi tatu.
sw.note: Nails are sold by weight: kilo moja, kilo mbili.

en.text: Give me ten metres of wire too.

sw.text: Nipe pia mita kumi za waya.
alt: Na mita kumi za waya pia.

en.text: I also need ten iron sheets.

sw.note: bati = one iron sheet; mabati = iron sheets.

en.text: Do you have a two-inch paint brush?

sw.text: Una brashi ya rangi ya inchi mbili?

en.text: Can you cut me a key like this one?

sw.note: ku-ni-chong-e-a = to cut for me; kuchonga funguo = to cut keys.

en.text: This load is too big for my bike.

sw.text: Mzigo huu ni mkubwa mno kwa pikipiki yangu.
alt: Mzigo huu hautoshi kwenye pikipiki yangu.

en.text: How much do you charge for delivery?

sw.note: Mna- = you (plural): people speak to a shop as nyinyi.

en.text: Can you bring it this afternoon?
Yes, give me the till number.

alt: Ndiyo, namba ya till ni ipi?
sw.note: A shop's Lipa na M-Pesa number is called the till number.

en.text: Okay, I've paid, check your phone.
Please write it all on one receipt.

sw.text: Tafadhali andika vyote kwenye risiti moja.
alt: Tafadhali weka vyote kwenye risiti moja.

en.text: Tomorrow morning I'll wait for the truck at the plot.

sw.note: -ni on a place noun means at: kiwanja, kiwanjani.

en.text: I need to print ten pages.
Can I send it to you on WhatsApp?
How much is one page in colour?

sw.text: Ukurasa mmoja wa rangi ni bei gani?
alt: Ukurasa mmoja wa rangi ni shilingi ngapi?
sw.note: ukurasa (page) takes w-: ukurasa mmoja, ukurasa wa rangi.

en.text: I need two copies of my ID.

sw.text: Nahitaji nakala mbili za kitambulisho changu.
alt: Nahitaji fotokopi mbili za kitambulisho changu.

en.text: I've come to collect a parcel.

sw.note: Nimekuja keeps ku-: kuja is a one-syllable verb.

en.text: They sent me a message that it's arrived.

sw.note: ki- in kimefika agrees with kifurushi (parcel).

en.text: Is there anything to pay?
I want to buy my fiancée a kanga.

alt: Natafuta kanga ya kumpa mchumba wangu.
sw.note: ku-m-nunul-ia = to buy for her: -ia means for someone.

en.text: What does this kanga say?

sw.note: Every kanga has a printed saying; people read it before buying.

en.text: How much is one pair?

sw.note: doti = a pair of kanga, sold together as one piece.

en.text: Please wrap it nicely, it's a gift.
Will you open again after Friday prayers?

sw.text: Mtafungua tena baada ya sala ya Ijumaa?
alt: Mtafungua tena baada ya swala ya Ijumaa?
sw.note: Many coast shops close at midday on Friday for prayers.

en.text: I'll be back before you close.

sw.note: kabla + ha-...-ja-: kabla hamjafunga = before you close.

en.text: I've done everything, and it's not even eleven.

sw.text: Nimemaliza kila kitu, na bado haijafika saa tano.
sw.note: saa tano asubuhi = eleven in the morning.

en.text: I came to the beach early to buy fish.
What time do the boats come back?
Look, the boats are coming back right now.
Is that dhow coming from Lamu?

sw.note: Jahazi takes li-: jahazi lile, linatoka. Many dhows = majahazi.

en.text: How was the sea last night?
What fish did you get today?

sw.note: Mm- = you all: you are asking the whole crew.

en.text: Are these fish from this morning?

sw.text: Samaki hawa ni wa leo asubuhi?
sw.note: Fish are living things, so 'these' is hawa, not hizi.

en.text: I want two big changu.

sw.note: Changu is a favourite coast fish, like a snapper.

en.text: Do you have prawns today?

sw.note: Kamba here means prawns; it can also mean rope.

en.text: Keep two kilos of prawns for me tomorrow.

sw.text: Niwekee kilo mbili za kamba kesho.
alt: Kesho niwekee kilo mbili za kamba.
sw.note: ni-wek-e-e = keep for me.

en.text: How much is the octopus per kilo?

sw.text: Pweza ni bei gani kwa kilo?
alt: Kilo ya pweza ni bei gani?

en.text: Last week it was three hundred and fifty a kilo.

sw.text: Wiki iliyopita ilikuwa mia tatu na hamsini kwa kilo.

en.text: Weigh one kilo for me, please.
If I take two kilos, can we do seven hundred?

sw.text: Nikichukua kilo mbili, tufanye mia saba?
alt: Nikichukua kilo mbili, utanipa kwa mia saba?
sw.note: ni-ki-chukua = if I take.

en.text: These are fresh, I'll take them.

sw.note: wa- = them, for living things like fish.

en.text: Can you clean them for me?

sw.note: ku-ni-safish-ia = to clean for me.

en.text: Take out the scales and the insides, please.

sw.note: Some say utumbo for the insides; matumbo is the everyday word.

en.text: Don't cut off the head, I'll make soup.
What time will the tide come in today?

alt: Leo maji kujaa ni saa ngapi?
sw.note: Maji kujaa = high tide; maji kupwa = low tide.

en.text: The tide is out, the boats can't come in yet.

sw.text: Maji yamekupwa, mashua bado haziwezi kuingia.
sw.note: -pwa is a short verb, so it keeps ku-: ya-me-ku-pwa.

en.text: The sea is rough today.

sw.note: Kuchafuka = to get rough, said of the sea.

en.text: Do you go out to sea every night?
Good work, you were out at sea all night.

sw.text: Pole na kazi, mlikuwa baharini usiku kucha.
sw.note: Pole na kazi = a kind word to anyone who has worked hard.

en.text: Can I come out with you one day?

sw.text: Naweza kwenda nanyi baharini siku moja?
alt: Siku moja naweza kuja nanyi baharini?
sw.note: nanyi = na + nyinyi, with you all.

en.text: I'll pay for the boat's fuel.

sw.note: lip-ia = pay for something.

en.text: I can't swim very well.
Let me know when the wind drops.

sw.note: u-ki-pungua = when it drops; upepo takes u-.

en.text: Tonight my fiancée is making octopus in coconut.

sw.text: Leo usiku mchumba wangu atapika pweza wa nazi.
alt: Mchumba wangu atapika pweza wa nazi leo usiku.
sw.note: Pweza wa nazi = octopus cooked in coconut milk.

en.text: I'm going to grill this one at home.

sw.note: A fish takes m-: nitamchoma = I'll grill it.

en.text: How many of you go out in one boat?
Thank you, my brother, I'll come for the prawns tomorrow.

sw.text: Asante, ndugu yangu, nitakuja kuchukua kamba kesho.
alt: Asante, ndugu yangu, kesho nitakuja kuchukua kamba.

en.text: And peace be upon you.

sw.note: The reply to Assalamu alaykum.

en.text: I hear the call to prayer every morning.

sw.note: adhana = the call to prayer from the mosque, five times a day.

en.text: I usually wake up before the call to prayer.

sw.note: hu-amka = usually wake up; hu- marks a habit.

en.text: Don't worry, I like hearing it.
I meditate at the time of the dawn prayer.

sw.text: Natafakari wakati wa sala ya alfajiri.
alt: Mimi hutafakari wakati wa sala ya alfajiri.

en.text: What time are Friday prayers?

sw.text: Sala ya Ijumaa ni saa ngapi?
alt: Sala ya Ijumaa inaanza saa ngapi?

en.text: Sorry, I didn't know you were praying.
I respect all faiths.
Thank you for inviting me to church.
What time does the service start?
I'll come on Sunday at nine in the morning.

sw.note: saa tatu asubuhi = nine in the morning, the third hour after dawn.

en.text: What should I wear?
The service was long, but it was blessed.

sw.text: Ibada ilikuwa ndefu, lakini ilikuwa na baraka.

en.text: Ramadan starts this week, right?

alt: Ramadhani inaanza wiki hii, si ndiyo?

en.text: I wish you a good fast.
Are you fasting today?

sw.note: kufunga = to fast; the same verb means to close or lock.

en.text: No, but I won't eat in front of you.

sw.note: To a whole family, say mbele yenu.

en.text: What time do you break the fast?

sw.note: kufuturu = to break the fast at sunset; the meal is futari.

en.text: Thank you, I'd love to come.
What can I bring?
I'll bring some dates and juice.

sw.note: tende = dates; the fast is often broken with dates.

en.text: Should I take my shoes off here?
Has the moon been seen yet?

sw.note: Eid starts when the new moon is seen.

en.text: Is Eid tomorrow or the day after?

sw.text: Idi ni kesho au kesho kutwa?
sw.note: kesho kutwa = the day after tomorrow.

en.text: Happy Eid, my neighbour.

sw.note: Idi (Kenyans often write Idd) = Eid, the feast after Ramadan.

en.text: Same to you, my brother.
Merry Christmas to you and your family.

sw.text: Heri ya Krismasi kwako na familia yako.
alt: Krismasi njema kwako na familia yako.

en.text: When is the church harambee?

sw.note: harambee = a community fundraiser where everyone gives what they can.

en.text: I'll contribute two thousand shillings by M-Pesa.

sw.text: Nitachangia shilingi elfu mbili kwa M-Pesa.
alt: Nitatuma mchango wa shilingi elfu mbili kwa M-Pesa.

en.text: Please pray for me and my fiancée.

sw.text: Tafadhali tuombee mimi na mchumba wangu.
sw.note: tu-ombee = pray for us; Swahili says us, then names who.

en.text: I'll pray for all of you.
God willing, I'll be there.
How should I greet your father?
Should I shake your mother's hand?

sw.note: kumpa mtu mkono = to shake someone's hand. Some women greet men without one.

en.text: To be honest, I'm a little nervous.
Hello, may I come in?

sw.note: Call it at the door or gate. The answer is Karibu.

en.text: Should I take off my shoes?

sw.note: kuvua = to take off shoes or clothes.

en.text: I'm Ambi, your daughter's fiancé.

sw.text: Mimi ni Ambi, mchumba wa binti yenu.
sw.note: mchumba = fiancé or fiancée. Yenu (your, to all of them) is respectful.

en.text: I've come to introduce myself.

sw.note: ku-ji-tambulisha = to make yourself known.

en.text: I brought you a small gift.

sw.note: ni-me-wa-letea = I-have-you all-brought for.

en.text: It's sugar, tea leaves and flour.

sw.text: Ni sukari, majani ya chai na unga.
alt: Ni sukari, majani chai na unga.

en.text: Pleased to meet you, Uncle.
Oh, so you're her uncle.

sw.note: mjomba = mother's brother. Father's brother = baba mdogo or baba mkubwa.

en.text: Mama, you cook really well.

alt: Mama, chakula chako ni kitamu sana.

en.text: These chapatis are really soft.
Can I help you wash the dishes?
We've known each other for two years.

sw.note: tu-me-juana = we-have-known each other.

en.text: We met in Malindi.
I'm building our house near Malindi.

sw.text: Najenga nyumba yetu karibu na Malindi.

en.text: I sincerely want to marry your daughter.

sw.text: Nina nia ya dhati ya kumwoa binti yenu.
alt: Nia yangu ni kumwoa binti yenu.
sw.note: kuoa = a man marries; kuolewa = a woman is married. ku-mw-oa = to marry her.

en.text: I want to follow your customs and traditions.

sw.text: Nataka kufuata mila na desturi zenu.

en.text: I'll take good care of her.

sw.note: ni-ta-m-tunza = I-will-her-look after.

en.text: I promise to respect her always.
My parents send you their greetings.
I've asked an elder to represent me.

sw.note: In dowry talks, elders speak for each family, not the couple.

en.text: When should my elders come to discuss the dowry?

sw.text: Wazee wangu waje lini kuzungumzia mahari?
sw.note: mahari = the dowry, agreed by the elders of both families.

en.text: We'll leave the dowry to the elders.
Whatever the elders decide, I'll accept it.

sw.note: wa-taka-lo-amua = they-will-which-decide; ni-ta-li-kubali = I-will-it-accept.

en.text: Thank you for raising her so well.

sw.note: Asanteni = thank you, said to more than one person.

en.text: Thank you all for your hospitality.
With your permission, I'll head home now.

sw.note: A guest asks the elders' permission before leaving.

en.text: I'll come back with my elders.
Have we chosen a date yet?

sw.note: tu-me-sha-chagua = we-have-already-chosen.

en.text: Let's get married in December.

sw.note: kufunga ndoa = to get married (to tie the marriage).

en.text: Saturday is better for the guests, right?

sw.text: Jumamosi ni bora kwa wageni, sivyo?
sw.note: sivyo? at the end = right? (isn't it so?)

en.text: We want a small wedding.
Just close family and friends.

sw.text: Familia na marafiki wa karibu tu.
alt: Ndugu na marafiki wa karibu tu.

en.text: No more than a hundred guests.

sw.note: wa-si-zidi = let them not go over.

en.text: Okay, let's write the guest list tonight.

sw.text: Sawa, tuandike orodha ya wageni leo usiku.

en.text: Where will the wedding be?
Maybe at our new house, if it's ready.

sw.text: Labda kwenye nyumba yetu mpya, ikiwa tayari.

en.text: How much is the hall for one day?

sw.text: Ukumbi ni bei gani kwa siku moja?

en.text: We need to hire tents and chairs.
What's our budget for the food?

sw.text: Bajeti yetu ya chakula ni kiasi gani?

en.text: Let's have pilau and biryani.
Some guests don't eat meat.

sw.note: ha-wa-li = they don't eat (from kula).

en.text: How much is each plate?
The costs shouldn't go over our budget.
Let's not borrow money for the wedding.

sw.text: Tusikope pesa kwa ajili ya harusi.
alt: Tusichukue mkopo kwa ajili ya harusi.
sw.note: tu-si-kope = let's not borrow: a 'let's not' ends in -e.

en.text: Let's form a wedding committee.

sw.note: Kenyan weddings often have a committee that meets and collects contributions.

en.text: My friends want to contribute.

sw.note: kuchanga = to put money together; mchango = a contribution.

en.text: Send your contribution to the treasurer.

sw.text: Tuma mchango wako kwa mweka hazina.
sw.note: mweka hazina = treasurer (keeper of the treasury).

en.text: Thank you for your contribution.
On Friday I'm going to the tailor to be measured for a suit.

sw.text: Ijumaa nakwenda kwa fundi kupimwa suti.
alt: Ijumaa naenda kwa fundi kupimwa suti.
sw.note: fundi = any skilled worker; here the tailor.

en.text: The tailor needs two weeks to finish it.

sw.note: ku-i-maliza = to finish it (the suit).

en.text: Do you know a good photographer?

sw.note: mpiga picha = photographer (one who takes pictures).

en.text: The photographer wants twenty thousand shillings.

sw.text: Mpiga picha anataka shilingi elfu ishirini.

en.text: Let's send the invitation cards next week.

sw.text: Tutume kadi za mwaliko wiki ijayo.

en.text: We'll send invitations on WhatsApp too.
My parents are coming to the wedding.
My friend will be my best man.

sw.note: msimamizi = best man; the bride has her own msimamizi too.

en.text: It's our day, let's enjoy it.
I can't wait for the big day.

sw.text: Nasubiri siku hiyo kwa hamu kubwa.
sw.note: Kiswahili waits kwa hamu (with longing); siwezi kusubiri copies English.

en.text: I'd like a haircut, please.

sw.note: kunyoa = to cut or shave; kunyolewa = to be cut (get a haircut).

en.text: Who's the last one in the line?
How many people are ahead of me?
I'll wait, no problem.
I'll come back in twenty minutes.
Is it my turn now?
Short on the sides, leave a little on top.

sw.text: Nyoa fupi pembeni, juu uache kidogo.

en.text: Don't cut it too short, please.

sw.note: u-si-nyoe = you-don't-cut: a 'don't' ends in -e.

en.text: Just trim the beard a little.
Don't shave off my whole beard.
Please use a new blade.

sw.note: Ask for a new blade every time; barbers expect it.

en.text: Did you clean the clippers?

sw.note: mashine = the hair clippers at a Kenyan barbershop.

en.text: Do you have a generator?
I can't go home like this.
Can you finish it with scissors?
It's all good, I'll wait until the power comes back.

sw.text: Ni sawa tu, nitasubiri mpaka stima irudi.
sw.note: mpaka + i-rudi (not i-na-rudi) = until it comes back.

en.text: Let me look in the mirror.
You cut it really well, my brother.
How much for a haircut and the beard?

sw.text: Kunyoa nywele na ndevu ni bei gani?
alt: Nywele na ndevu ni pesa ngapi?

en.text: Last time I paid one hundred and fifty.

sw.text: Mara ya mwisho nililipa mia moja na hamsini.

en.text: Here's two hundred, keep the change.

sw.text: Chukua mia mbili, baki na chenji.
alt: Shika mia mbili, baki na chenji.

en.text: I come here every two weeks.

sw.text: Nakuja hapa kila baada ya wiki mbili.
sw.note: kila baada ya wiki mbili = every two weeks.

en.text: My fiancée is at the salon getting her hair braided.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu yuko saluni anasukwa nywele.
sw.note: kusuka = to braid; a-na-sukwa = she is being braided.

en.text: How long will she be?
I know braids take hours.
Is there a place to sit and wait?

sw.text: Kuna mahali pa kukaa na kusubiri?
sw.note: mahali takes pa-: mahali pa kukaa = a place to sit.

en.text: Tell her I'm waiting outside.
I'll come back to pick her up at four.

sw.note: saa kumi = the tenth hour after dawn: four in the afternoon.

en.text: How much do the braids cost?
I'll pay for her myself.

sw.note: ni-ta-m-lipia = I-will-her-pay for.

en.text: Your hair looks really beautiful.

sw.note: kupendeza = to look good; zi- matches nywele.

en.text: I've had a fever since last night.

sw.text: Nimekuwa na homa tangu jana usiku.
sw.note: Nimekuwa na homa = I have had a fever, and still do.

en.text: I woke up at two in the morning with a fever.

sw.text: Niliamka saa nane usiku nikiwa na homa.
sw.note: 2 a.m. = saa nane usiku. ni-ki-wa = while I was.

en.text: I was shivering all night.

sw.note: usiku kucha = the whole night long.

en.text: My whole body is aching.

sw.note: mwili takes u-: u-na-ni-uma = it-is-me-hurting.

en.text: I think it might be malaria.

sw.note: huenda = maybe, it could be.

en.text: I want to get tested for malaria.

sw.note: kupima malaria = to get tested for malaria.

en.text: It's my first time at this clinic.

sw.text: Ni mara yangu ya kwanza kuja kliniki hii.
alt: Hii ni mara yangu ya kwanza hapa.

en.text: Do you take SHA here?

sw.note: SHA is Kenya's public health cover; people say the letters.

en.text: I haven't joined SHA yet, I'll pay cash.

sw.text: Bado sijajiunga na SHA, nitalipa pesa taslimu.
alt: Sina SHA bado, nitalipa pesa taslimu.
sw.note: si-ja-jiunga = I-have-not-yet-joined.

en.text: How much is it to see the doctor?

sw.note: ku-mw-ona = to see him or her; mw- is for a person.

en.text: How much is the malaria test?

sw.text: Kipimo cha malaria ni shilingi ngapi?
sw.note: kipimo = a test; a ki- noun, so cha.

en.text: Where is the lab?
Will it hurt a lot?
When will the results be ready?

sw.note: majibu = results, a ma- noun, so ya-.

en.text: Okay, I'll wait outside.
The doctor wrote me a prescription.

sw.note: kumwandikia mtu dawa = to prescribe medicine for someone.

en.text: Do you have this medicine?
How much for the whole dose?

sw.note: dozi = the full course of a medicine.

en.text: How many tablets do I take each time?

sw.note: vidonge takes vi-: vingapi, viwili, vinne.

en.text: Do I take them in the morning or at night?
Please write it on the packet for me.

sw.note: ni-andik-ie = write-for-me.

en.text: I have to finish the whole dose, right?

sw.note: sivyo? at the end = right?

en.text: Does this medicine have any side effects?

sw.note: madhara = harm; for medicine, side effects.

en.text: When I take this medicine, I feel dizzy.

sw.note: ni-ki-meza = when-I-swallow.

en.text: When should I come back?
I'll come back on Friday to get tested again.

alt: Nitarudi siku ya Ijumaa kupimwa tena.
sw.note: kupimwa = to be tested; the -w- makes it passive.

en.text: Can I still go to the gym this week?

sw.text: Bado naweza kwenda jimu wiki hii?
alt: Naweza kuendelea na mazoezi wiki hii?

en.text: The fever has come down now.
My fiancée is taking good care of me.

sw.note: kuuguza = to nurse someone who is sick.

en.text: I sleep under a net every night.

sw.text: Nalala ndani ya chandarua kila usiku.
alt: Kila usiku nalala ndani ya chandarua.
sw.note: chandarua = mosquito net; plural vyandarua.

en.text: There's a hole in my net.

sw.note: chandarua is a ki- noun: changu, kina, kimetoboka.

en.text: Thank you so much, doctor.
I want to withdraw five thousand shillings.

sw.note: kutoa pesa = to withdraw; kuweka pesa = to deposit.

en.text: Do you have enough cash right now?

sw.text: Una pesa taslimu za kutosha sasa hivi?

en.text: How much do you have?
Okay, give me two thousand, then.
Is there another agent nearby?

sw.note: wakala is a person, so: wakala mwingine.

en.text: What's the charge to withdraw five thousand?

sw.text: Gharama ya kutoa elfu tano ni kiasi gani?
alt: Gharama ya kutoa elfu tano ni ngapi?

en.text: Here's my ID.

sw.note: hiki hapa = here it is, with ki- for kitambulisho.

en.text: Can I use my passport?
Please count it again.
This note is torn, please change it.

sw.note: i- in ibadilishe stands for noti (the note).

en.text: I'll come back when you have cash.
I sent money to the wrong number.

sw.text: Nimetuma pesa kwa namba isiyo sahihi.
sw.note: kimakosa = by mistake; you'll hear it a lot about M-Pesa.

en.text: I sent it yesterday evening.

sw.note: -zi- stands for pesa (money): pesa takes zi-.

en.text: I think I got one digit wrong.
How do I get my money back?

alt: Nifanye nini ili pesa zangu zirudi?

en.text: I've already called Safaricom.

sw.note: -mesha- = already: nimeshapiga, nimeshalipa.

en.text: They said the money will come back today.
How long before the money comes back?

sw.text: Pesa zitarudi baada ya muda gani?

en.text: Please send the money back, I made a mistake.
He still hasn't sent the money back.

sw.note: ha-ja- = not yet: hajarudisha, hazijaingia.

en.text: The money hasn't come in yet.
I got the message, but not the money.
The transaction is still pending.

sw.note: muamala (transaction) takes u-: haujakamilika.

en.text: Let me show you the message.
I've been charged twice.

sw.note: kukatwa pesa = to have money taken from your account.

en.text: It's come in now, thank you.
Is this the queue for deposits?

sw.text: Hii ndiyo foleni ya kuweka pesa?
alt: Foleni ya kuweka pesa ni hii?

en.text: I've been in this queue for half an hour.

sw.text: Nimesimama kwenye foleni hii kwa nusu saa.
alt: Nimekaa kwenye foleni hii nusu saa.

en.text: I want to deposit ten thousand shillings.
The ATM swallowed my card.

sw.note: People say the machine swallowed (imemeza) or ate (imekula) the card.

en.text: How do I get my card back?
I need a statement for the last three months.

sw.text: Nahitaji taarifa ya akaunti ya miezi mitatu iliyopita.
alt: Nahitaji statement ya miezi mitatu iliyopita.
sw.note: miezi (months) takes mi-: miezi mitatu iliyopita.

en.text: The meter is beeping, the units are almost finished.

sw.note: yuniti = the units on the prepaid meter.

en.text: I'm buying tokens on M-Pesa right now.

sw.text: Nanunua tokeni kwa M-Pesa sasa hivi.
alt: Nanunua stima kwa M-Pesa sasa hivi.
sw.note: Many people say kununua stima, to buy power.

en.text: I'll buy tokens for five hundred shillings.

sw.text: Nitanunua tokeni za shilingi mia tano.
alt: Nitanunua stima ya shilingi mia tano.

en.text: The token message hasn't come yet.

sw.note: ujumbe takes u-: ha-u-ja-fika = it-has-not-yet-arrived.

en.text: Let me put the token into the meter.
How many units did I get?
The units are running out so fast this month.

sw.text: Yuniti zinaisha haraka sana mwezi huu.
sw.note: yuniti takes zi- in the plural: zinaisha.

en.text: I thought my units had run out.
The power just went off.

sw.note: kukatika = to be cut; for power, to go off.

en.text: The power's been off since four in the afternoon.

sw.text: Stima imekatika tangu saa kumi jioni.
alt: Umeme umekatika tangu saa kumi jioni.
sw.note: 4 p.m. = saa kumi jioni.

en.text: When will the power come back?

sw.note: umeme is a u- noun: umeme utarudi.

en.text: I'm calling KPLC right now.

sw.note: People say KPLC or Kenya Power.

en.text: The power keeps going on and off today.

sw.note: Doubling the verb, katika-katika, means again and again.

en.text: The fridge is off, the food is going to spoil.
I'll use the light on my phone.

sw.note: tochi = torch; a phone has one too.

en.text: Good thing I charged the power bank last night.

sw.text: Bahati nzuri nilichaji power bank jana usiku.
sw.note: Bahati nzuri = luckily.

en.text: The home wifi has been down since yesterday.

sw.text: Wifi ya nyumbani imekatika tangu jana.

en.text: The internet light on the router is red.

sw.text: Taa ya intaneti kwenye ruta ni nyekundu.

en.text: Let me turn the router off and on again.

sw.text: Ngoja nizime ruta, kisha niiwashe tena.
sw.note: ni-i-washe = I-it-switch on; ruta takes i-.

en.text: The technician is coming at two in the afternoon.

sw.note: 2 p.m. = saa nane mchana.

en.text: I need to buy some data real quick.

sw.note: bando = data bundle, everyday slang.

en.text: How much is the weekly bundle?

sw.text: Kifurushi cha wiki ni shilingi ngapi?
alt: Bando la wiki ni shilingi ngapi?
sw.note: kifurushi = bundle, the word on the phone menu.

en.text: Can you turn on your hotspot for me?

sw.note: ku-ni-washia = to switch on for me.

en.text: Thanks, but the video is too big for a hotspot.

sw.text: Asante, lakini video ni kubwa mno kwa hotspot.
sw.note: mno = too much.

en.text: I have a video to upload tonight.

sw.text: Nina video ya kupakia leo usiku.
sw.note: video ya kupakia = a video to upload.

en.text: The laptop has twenty percent charge left.

sw.text: Chaji ya kompyuta imebaki asilimia ishirini.
alt: Kompyuta yangu imebaki na asilimia ishirini.
sw.note: asilimia = percent.

en.text: The video is stuck at ninety percent.
It's all good, the video can wait until the power comes back.

sw.text: Ni sawa tu, video inaweza kusubiri mpaka stima irudi.
sw.note: mpaka stima irudi = until the power comes back.

en.text: All right, let me start uploading the video again.

sw.text: Haya, ngoja nianze kupakia video tena.

en.text: I'll take my laptop to a café with wifi.

sw.text: Nitapeleka kompyuta yangu kwenye mgahawa wenye wifi.
sw.note: mgahawa takes w-: mgahawa wenye wifi.

en.text: I want to put solar on my new house.

sw.text: Nataka kuweka sola kwenye nyumba yangu mpya.
sw.note: sola = solar panels; kuweka sola = to install solar.

en.text: The power came back at seven in the evening.

sw.note: 7 p.m. = saa moja usiku; the clock counts from dawn.

en.text: It's starting to rain.

sw.note: Rain rains in Kiswahili: mvua inanyesha = it's raining.

en.text: The rain came suddenly today.
This rain is really heavy.

sw.note: Heavy rain is big rain: mvua kubwa.

en.text: Can I stand under your tarpaulin?

sw.text: Naweza kusimama chini ya turubai lako?
alt: Naweza kujikinga chini ya turubai lako?
sw.note: turubai takes li-: turubai lako, turubai linavuja.

en.text: Your tarpaulin is leaking here.
Okay, it's drier here.

sw.note: Places take pa-: hapa ni pakavu = it is dry here. Also said: hapa hakuna maji.

en.text: I didn't bring my raincoat.

sw.note: koti la mvua = raincoat, a coat for rain.

en.text: Do you sell umbrellas?

sw.note: mwavuli = umbrella; miavuli = umbrellas.

en.text: Watch out, it's slippery here.

sw.note: pa- in panateleza agrees with hapa (this spot).

en.text: My shoes are full of mud.
The tomatoes are wet, are they still good?

sw.note: zi- agrees with nyanya: zimelowa = they're wet.

en.text: Give me the dry ones, please.
Give me two heaps.

sw.note: fungu = a heap; tomatoes are often sold by the heap.

en.text: Put them in the bag so they don't get wet.

sw.note: zi-si-low-e = so they don't get wet.

en.text: Why has the price gone up today?

sw.note: Mbona? is another everyday why, often with surprise.

en.text: Yesterday it was fifty shillings.

sw.note: i- in ilikuwa agrees with bei (the price).

en.text: Is it because of the rain?
Are you packing up already?
If I take them all, how much?

alt: Nikichukua zote, utanipa kwa bei gani?
sw.note: -ki- = if: nikichukua = if I take.

en.text: Let me help you cover the vegetables.
Let's wait here until the rain stops.
It won't last long.
No worries, I'll wait on the shop's veranda.

sw.text: Hakuna shida, nitasubiri kwenye kibaraza cha duka.
sw.note: Old coast shops have a kibaraza, a veranda with a stone bench.

en.text: Wait, it's raining harder now.
It's still drizzling.

sw.note: manyunyu = light rain, drizzle.

en.text: The road home is flooded.

sw.text: Barabara ya kwenda nyumbani imejaa maji.
alt: Barabara ya kwenda nyumbani imefurika maji.

en.text: I left the bike at home because of the rain.

sw.text: Nimeacha pikipiki nyumbani kwa sababu ya mvua.

en.text: No boda wants to go in this rain.

sw.text: Hakuna boda anayetaka kwenda kwenye mvua hii.

en.text: I'll pay twice the fare, just take me home.

sw.text: Nitalipa nauli mara mbili, nipeleke nyumbani tu.

en.text: I'm soaking wet.

sw.note: chepechepe = dripping wet; it goes with kulowa.

en.text: The rain has eased, let's go now.
I got home without getting wet.
I was training on the beach all week.

sw.text: Wiki nzima nilikuwa nafanya mazoezi ufukweni.
alt: Wiki nzima nilikuwa nikifanya mazoezi ufukweni.

en.text: How much is the monthly membership now?

sw.text: Uanachama wa mwezi sasa ni bei gani?
alt: Ada ya mwezi sasa ni bei gani?

en.text: It was two thousand last month.

alt: Mwezi uliopita ilikuwa shilingi elfu mbili.

en.text: Okay, I'll pay for three months.

sw.note: mi- on the number matches miezi: miezi mitatu.

en.text: My membership ends on Friday.

alt: Uanachama wangu unaisha siku ya Ijumaa.

en.text: It's really hot in here today.

sw.text: Leo kuna joto sana humu ndani.

en.text: Can you switch on the fan, please?

sw.note: Kuwasha = switch on: a fan, a light, the stove.

en.text: Can we open the windows then?
It's too hot to train in the middle of the day.

sw.text: Kuna joto sana kufanya mazoezi mchana.

en.text: That's why I come at six in the morning.

sw.text: Ndiyo maana nakuja saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: Saa kumi na mbili asubuhi = six in the morning.

en.text: Coach, watch me and tell me if I'm doing it right.

sw.text: Kocha, niangalie uniambie kama nafanya sawa.

en.text: Is it right like this?
Is my back straight?
How low should I go?
How many sets should I do?

sw.note: ni-fany-e = should I do.

en.text: Twenty is a lot, but I'll try.
I can do ten pull-ups now.
Last month I could only do five.

sw.text: Mwezi uliopita niliweza kufanya tano tu.

en.text: Is anyone using these weights?

sw.note: Vyuma = weights, literally irons.

en.text: Can I borrow the skipping rope?
I'll bring it back in five minutes.

sw.note: i = it, for kamba (the rope).

en.text: Where can I put my things?
Can I shower here after training?

sw.text: Naweza kuoga hapa baada ya mazoezi?

en.text: I forgot my towel at home.
Sunday is my rest day.

sw.text: Jumapili ni siku yangu ya kupumzika.

en.text: My chest is sore from the push-ups.

sw.text: Kifua kinaniuma kwa sababu ya push-up.
sw.note: ki-na-ni-uma = it hurts me.

en.text: Today I can't even lift my arms.
I do my push-ups on the beach at sunrise.

sw.text: Nafanya push-up zangu ufukweni jua likichomoza.
sw.note: jua li-ki-chomoza = as the sun rises.

en.text: Training on the sand is harder.

sw.text: Ni vigumu zaidi kufanya mazoezi mchangani.

en.text: After training, I go into the sea.
Come and train with me on the beach tomorrow.
The gym is full, I'll come back later.
My bike needs a service.

sw.note: sevisi = a service, the everyday Kenyan word.

en.text: It was three months ago.
Use good oil, not cheap oil.

sw.text: Tumia oili nzuri, si ya bei rahisi.
sw.note: oili = engine oil; mafuta usually means fuel.

en.text: The back brakes are squeaking.

sw.note: ku-lia = to cry; a machine cries when it squeaks.

en.text: I want original parts, not fake ones.

sw.note: vipuri = spare parts; feki is the everyday word for fake.

en.text: Fake parts don't last.

sw.note: ha-vi-dumu = they don't last; vi- matches vipuri.

en.text: Can you tighten the chain?
What time will it be ready?
How much will the whole service cost?
Let me take it for a quick ride first.

sw.note: nayo = na + yo, with it (the bike).

en.text: That's more than you said.

sw.text: Hiyo ni zaidi ya bei uliyosema.

en.text: Thank you, the bike is like new now.

sw.text: Asante, pikipiki sasa ni kama mpya.

en.text: I think the chain is loose.

sw.note: ku-legea = to get loose; umelegea = it has got loose.

en.text: The back tyre has a puncture again.

sw.text: Tairi la nyuma limepata pancha tena.
sw.note: tairi takes li- words: tairi la nyuma limepata.

en.text: Can you fix the puncture right now?

sw.note: ku-ziba = to plug or patch a hole.

en.text: Should I change the spark plug?

sw.note: plagi = spark plug.

en.text: In the morning the bike is slow to start.

sw.note: ku-waka = to start (an engine), also to light up.

en.text: Is this part original?

sw.note: kipuri = one spare part; vipuri = spare parts.

en.text: How much is the original part?
I want to see the old spark plug.
Can you write down what you changed?

sw.note: ku-ni-andik-ia = to write for me.

en.text: How much for the labour?

sw.note: ufundi = the fundi's work, paid apart from the parts.

en.text: I'll pay with M-Pesa.
I'll bring it for a service every three months.

sw.text: Nitaileta kwa sevisi kila baada ya miezi mitatu.
sw.note: kila baada ya miezi mitatu = every three months.

en.text: Can you look at it today?
I need it back before the evening.
It still makes that noise.
The brakes are good now.
Please check the tyre pressure too.

sw.text: Tafadhali angalia upepo kwenye matairi pia.
sw.note: upepo = air in a tyre; the word also means wind.

en.text: Do you have that part here?
I always bring my bike here.

sw.text: Kila mara naleta pikipiki yangu hapa.

en.text: Okay, I'll be back at four in the afternoon.
The tank is empty again.
I ran out of water this morning.

sw.note: Kuishiwa na = to run out of (water, money, time).

en.text: I need a lorry of water today.
Hello, I got your number from my neighbour.

sw.text: Halo, nimepata namba yako kwa jirani yangu.

en.text: How much for ten thousand litres?

sw.text: Lita elfu kumi ni bei gani?

en.text: Five thousand is too much, can we do four thousand?

sw.text: Elfu tano ni ghali sana, tufanye elfu nne?

en.text: Okay, when can the lorry come?
Can it get here before twelve?

sw.text: Linaweza kufika kabla ya saa sita mchana?
sw.note: Saa sita mchana = twelve noon.

en.text: All right, two in the afternoon works for me.

sw.note: Saa nane mchana = two in the afternoon.

en.text: Call me when you reach the main road.
Thanks for coming so fast.
Okay, the tank is behind the house.

sw.text: Sawa, tanki liko nyuma ya nyumba.

en.text: My tank takes ten thousand litres.

sw.text: Tanki langu linachukua lita elfu kumi.
alt: Tanki langu ni la lita elfu kumi.

en.text: We said four thousand five hundred, right?

sw.text: Tulisema elfu nne na mia tano, sivyo?

en.text: Where does this water come from?
My borehole water is very salty.

sw.text: Maji ya kisima changu yana chumvi nyingi.
sw.note: Kisima = a well or a borehole.

en.text: Can you come again next Saturday?
If it rains, I won't need the lorry.
Thanks, my brother, see you on Saturday.
How much for one jerrycan?

sw.note: Dumu, plural madumu = a jerrycan, usually twenty litres.

en.text: Bring me ten jerrycans today.
Pour the water into the tank, please.
The salty water is just for laundry.

sw.text: Maji ya chumvi ni ya kufulia tu.

en.text: I boil all my drinking water.
The rain filled the tank last night.
I collect rainwater from the roof.

sw.text: Nakinga maji ya mvua kutoka kwenye paa.
sw.note: Kukinga maji = to catch water as it falls.

en.text: Rainwater is fresh, not salty.

sw.text: Maji ya mvua ni matamu, hayana chumvi.
sw.note: Maji matamu = fresh water (literally, sweet water).

en.text: The pump isn't working.
Maybe it's the power, let me check real quick.

sw.text: Labda ni stima, ngoja niangalie haraka.

en.text: Do you know anyone who fixes pumps?
Let's use the water carefully this week.

sw.text: Wiki hii tutumie maji kwa uangalifu.

en.text: When will the piped water come back?

sw.note: Maji ya bomba = piped water from the county.

en.text: Open the gate for me, please.

sw.note: fungua = open; fungulia = open for someone.

en.text: It's me, Ambi.
How are things at this hour?

sw.note: A friendly late-night greeting: news of these hours?

en.text: Yes, but the road was very muddy.

sw.text: Ndiyo, lakini barabara ilikuwa na matope mengi.
alt: Ndiyo, ila barabara ilikuwa na matope mengi.
sw.note: matope (mud) is a ma- word: matope mengi.

en.text: Help me push the bike inside.
Sorry to wake you up.

sw.note: ku-ku-amsha = to wake you.

en.text: I'll be home late tonight.
I'll be back at about ten at night.

sw.note: Swahili hours start at dawn: saa nne usiku = ten at night.

en.text: Don't lock the gate before I get back.

sw.note: kabla sijarudi = before I get back (kabla takes the not-yet form).

en.text: Lock the gate after I leave.

sw.note: ni-ki-sha-toka = once I have gone out.

en.text: I have a visitor coming this evening.

sw.note: a-na-ye-kuja = who is coming.

en.text: When he arrives, open the gate for him.

sw.note: a-ki-fika = when he arrives; m-fungulie = open for him.

en.text: Don't open for anyone you don't know.

sw.note: u-si-ye-m-jua = whom you don't know.

en.text: Did anyone come today?
Who was it?
Did he leave a message?
Did you feed the dog?

sw.note: mbwa is an animal, so it takes m-: u-me-m-pa = you gave him.

en.text: Why is the dog barking?

sw.note: kubweka = to bark.

en.text: Tie the dog up in the day and let him loose at night.

sw.text: Mfunge mbwa mchana na umfungue usiku.
sw.note: funga = tie or lock; fungua = untie or open.

en.text: Don't be scared, the dog is tied up.

sw.note: a-me-fung-wa = he has been tied.

en.text: Here's your pay for this month.

sw.text: Huu ni mshahara wako wa mwezi huu.
alt: Chukua mshahara wako wa mwezi huu.
sw.note: mshahara (pay) is an m-mi word: huu, wako.

en.text: Is ten thousand shillings a month okay with you?

sw.text: Shilingi elfu kumi kwa mwezi ni sawa kwako?
alt: Shilingi elfu kumi kwa mwezi zinakufaa?
sw.note: elfu kumi = ten thousand: the thousand comes first.

en.text: If you need something, just tell me.

sw.note: u-ki-hitaji = if you need.

en.text: I bought you new batteries for the torch.

sw.note: nunua = buy; nunulia = buy for someone.

en.text: I brought you some tea.

sw.note: leta = bring; letea = bring to someone.

en.text: It's raining, stay inside the hut.

sw.text: Mvua inanyesha, kaa ndani ya kibanda.
alt: Mvua inanyesha, jikinge ndani ya kibanda.
sw.note: kibanda = the watchman's small hut by the gate.

en.text: I'll buy you a raincoat this week.

sw.text: Nitakununulia koti la mvua wiki hii.
sw.note: koti la mvua = raincoat (coat of rain).

en.text: Here are the keys to the gate.

sw.note: ufunguo = one key; funguo = keys.

en.text: Don't give these keys to anyone.

sw.note: mtu yeyote = anyone at all.

en.text: Wake me up if you hear anything.

sw.note: ni-amsh-e = wake me.

en.text: Thank you for looking after the house.

sw.note: ku-i-linda = to guard it (nyumba takes i-).

en.text: Good night, see you in the morning.
I'd like to join your chama.

sw.note: chama = a savings group; it takes ki- words: chama chenu, chama hiki.

en.text: How many members do you have?

sw.note: mwanachama = a member; wanachama = members.

sw.text: Na Jumatatu lazima niwe Watamu saa moja asubuhi.
alt: Na Jumatatu natakiwa kuwa Watamu saa moja asubuhi.
sw.note: 7 a.m. = saa moja asubuhi.

en.text: Are you sure? It's very early.
Then I'll pay for your fuel.

sw.note: ku-lipia = to pay for; ni-ta-ku-lipia = I-will-you-pay for.

en.text: What time will you pick me up?

sw.note: u-ta-ni-pitia = you-will-me-come by for.

en.text: Thank you, brother. You're a true friend.

sw.text: Asante, kaka. Wewe ni rafiki wa kweli.
alt: Asante, ndugu yangu. Wewe ni rafiki wa kweli.

en.text: Yes, our power went out too, at eleven at night.

sw.text: Ndiyo, hata kwetu stima ilikatika saa tano usiku.
alt: Ndiyo, hata kwetu ilikatika saa tano usiku.
sw.note: 11 p.m. = saa tano usiku.

en.text: And the mosquitoes, did they bite you?

sw.note: wa-li-ku-uma = they-did-you-bite.

en.text: The power came back at five in the morning.

sw.text: Stima ilirudi saa kumi na moja alfajiri.
sw.note: 5 a.m. = saa kumi na moja alfajiri.

en.text: Is there water at your place? Ours has run out.

sw.note: kwako = at your place; kwetu = at our place.

en.text: The water lorry is coming at ten in the morning.

sw.text: Lori la maji linakuja saa nne asubuhi.
alt: Gari la maji linakuja saa nne asubuhi.
sw.note: 10 a.m. = saa nne asubuhi.

en.text: About one thousand five hundred shillings.

sw.text: Kama shilingi elfu moja na mia tano.
alt: Ni kama elfu moja na mia tano.

en.text: Okay. Are you going out this early?
Leave me the gate key, I'll let him in.

sw.note: ni-ta-m-fungulia = I-will-him-open for.

en.text: Yes, I really like fish.
Shall I bring you anything?
But I leave work at six in the evening.

sw.text: Lakini natoka kazini saa kumi na mbili jioni.

en.text: All right, I'll be there by seven.

sw.note: nitakuwa nimefika = I will have arrived.

en.text: Okay, I'll call you when I'm at the gate.
You sent five hundred, shall I give you back one hundred?

sw.text: Umetuma mia tano, nikurudishie mia moja?
sw.note: ni-ku-rudish-i-e = shall I return (it) to you.

en.text: Shall I bring you vegetables again on Saturday?
I'll get there at ten in the morning.

sw.note: saa nne asubuhi = ten in the morning.

en.text: All right, I'll give them to her.
Going back is one hundred, and the waiting is fifty.

sw.text: Kurudi ni mia moja, na kusubiri ni hamsini.
sw.note: Riders often add a little for waiting time.

en.text: Shall we take the tarmac, or the shortcut?

sw.text: Tupite lami au njia ya mkato?
sw.note: lami = tarmac; njia ya mkato = shortcut.

en.text: The shortcut is faster, but it's muddy.

sw.text: Njia ya mkato ni ya haraka zaidi, lakini ina matope.

en.text: If you need a boda again, call me, brother.

sw.note: kaka = brother; a friendly way to address a man.

en.text: Leave it here in front of my shop.

sw.text: Iache hapa mbele ya duka langu.
sw.note: i-ache = leave it; i stands for the motorbike.

en.text: Yes, I'll keep an eye on it until you come back.
You're welcome, what time will you be back?

sw.note: Karibu also answers thanks: you're welcome.

en.text: I close at six in the evening.

sw.text: Mimi nafunga saa kumi na mbili jioni.
sw.note: saa kumi na mbili jioni = six in the evening.

en.text: Shall I give you more rice?

sw.note: ni-ku-ongeze-e = shall I add for you.

en.text: Shall I bring you some tea?
Tea with milk, or black tea?

sw.text: Chai ya maziwa au chai ya rangi?
sw.note: chai ya rangi = black tea, literally tea of colour.

en.text: Yes, pay to the number there on the wall.

sw.text: Ndiyo, lipa kwa namba iliyo pale ukutani.
sw.note: Hotelis stick their M-Pesa pay number on the wall.

en.text: Come to my place, in Kakuyuni.
When you get to the market, call me and I'll come and get you.

sw.note: nije nikuchukue = so I come and fetch you.

en.text: Are you coming on your motorbike?
Come with your fiancée.
Okay, see you on Saturday.
Hello, love, how was your day?

sw.note: mpenzi = darling, my love.

en.text: Sorry. Have you eaten?
What are you doing tonight?
What time is it in Canada right now?

sw.text: Kanada sasa hivi ni saa ngapi?
alt: Huko Kanada ni saa ngapi sasa?

en.text: Greet your mother for me.
Do you miss them a lot?

sw.note: kukumbuka = to remember, and also to miss someone.

en.text: One day we'll go and visit them together.
She's fine. She's invited you for lunch on Sunday.

sw.text: Yuko salama. Amekualika chakula cha mchana Jumapili.
alt: Yuko sawa. Amekualika chakula cha mchana Jumapili.
sw.note: chakula cha mchana = lunch (the midday meal).

en.text: Come at one in the afternoon.

sw.note: 1 p.m. = saa saba mchana.

en.text: Just bring sugar and tea leaves.

sw.text: Leta sukari na majani ya chai tu.
sw.note: Sugar and tea leaves are a polite gift when you visit elders.

en.text: Seven is early for me, let's say eight.

sw.text: Saa moja ni mapema kwangu, tuseme saa mbili.
alt: Saa moja ni mapema kwangu, tufanye saa mbili.

en.text: Oh, so you meditate? For how long?

alt: Kumbe huwa unatafakari? Kwa muda gani?
sw.note: Kumbe = oh, so: surprise at something new.

en.text: Forty minutes? I can't even do five.

sw.text: Dakika arobaini? Mimi siwezi hata dakika tano.

en.text: Okay, but you'll have to teach me.

sw.note: itabidi = it will be necessary: you'll have to.

en.text: All right, see you at eight then.
I called you at six in the morning, but you didn't answer.

sw.text: Nilikupigia saa kumi na mbili asubuhi, lakini hukupokea.
alt: Nilikupigia simu saa kumi na mbili asubuhi, hukupokea.
sw.note: hu-ku-pokea = you did not pick up.

en.text: What time did you start today?
You sit for forty minutes without doing anything?

sw.text: Unakaa dakika arobaini bila kufanya chochote?
alt: Unakaa dakika arobaini bila kufanya kitu?

en.text: Do you do it every day?
Even when you're tired?

sw.note: u-ki-wa = when you are.

en.text: What's the most important thing?

sw.note: lipi goes with jambo; kipi goes with kitu.

en.text: Don't your legs hurt?

sw.note: ha-i-ku-umi = they do not hurt you (miguu, legs).

en.text: Can I try it with you one day?

sw.text: Naweza kujaribu pamoja nawe siku moja?
alt: Siku moja naweza kujaribu pamoja nawe?

en.text: So early? Okay, I'll try.
What do you do on that laptop all day?

sw.text: Unafanya nini kwenye kompyuta hiyo siku nzima?
alt: Kwenye kompyuta hiyo unafanya nini siku nzima?

en.text: YouTube? Do they pay you for that work?
So who is your boss?

sw.text: Kwa hiyo bosi wako ni nani?
sw.note: kwa hiyo = so, therefore.

en.text: What time do you start in the morning?
Three videos in one day?
So why are you still working?

alt: Sasa kwa nini bado unafanya kazi?
sw.note: mbona = why, said with surprise.

en.text: My son repairs computers in Malindi town.

sw.text: Kijana wangu anatengeneza kompyuta mjini Malindi.
sw.note: kijana wangu = my son (literally, my young man).

en.text: I'll send you his number this evening.
Don't wear yourself out, rest a little.

sw.note: u-si-ji-choshe = you-don't-yourself-tire.

en.text: Try making a call and see.
It's the speaker, it's still a little damp.

sw.text: Ni spika, bado ina unyevu kidogo.
alt: Ni spika, bado ina maji kidogo.

en.text: Put it in dry rice overnight.

sw.text: Iweke kwenye mchele mkavu usiku mzima.
alt: Iweke ndani ya mchele usiku mzima.

en.text: Bring it back, I'll change the speaker for free.

alt: Ilete hapa, nitaweka spika mpya bure.

en.text: Go at four in the afternoon, the tide will be out.

sw.text: Nenda saa kumi jioni, maji yatakuwa yamekupwa.
alt: Nenda saa kumi jioni, wakati wa maji kupwa.
sw.note: maji kupwa = low tide; maji kujaa = high tide.

en.text: Wear shoes, the rocks are sharp.
Come back early, it might rain this evening.

sw.text: Urudi mapema, mvua inaweza kunyesha jioni.
alt: Rudi mapema, huenda mvua ikanyesha jioni.

en.text: If you stop by tomorrow, I'll have fresh fish.

sw.text: Ukipitia hapa kesho, nitakuwa na samaki wabichi.
sw.note: samaki wabichi = fresh fish: wa- agrees with animals.

en.text: Then come early, before seven in the morning.

sw.text: Basi njoo mapema, kabla ya saa moja asubuhi.
alt: Basi uje mapema, kabla ya saa moja asubuhi.

en.text: That's one hundred and fifty shillings.

sw.text: Ni shilingi mia moja na hamsini.

en.text: Yes, pay by till, the number is there on the wall.

sw.text: Ndiyo, lipa kwa till, namba iko hapo ukutani.
alt: Ndiyo, lipa kwa till namba iliyo ukutani.
sw.note: A till is the shop's own M-Pesa number for paying.

en.text: Then go to the clinic and get tested for malaria.

sw.note: On the coast, fever with a headache means a quick malaria test.

en.text: But today we need to buy sand and cement.

sw.text: Lakini leo tunahitaji kununua mchanga na saruji.
alt: Ila leo lazima tununue mchanga na saruji.

en.text: A lorry of sand is ten thousand shillings.

sw.text: Lori la mchanga ni shilingi elfu kumi.
alt: Lori la mchanga ni elfu kumi.

en.text: Eight hundred a bag, and we need ten bags.

sw.text: Mia nane kwa mfuko, na tunahitaji mifuko kumi.

en.text: That's enough, what's left is for transport.

sw.text: Hizo zinatosha, zitakazobaki ni za usafiri.
sw.note: pesa takes zi-: hizo zinatosha = that money is enough.

en.text: Okay, I'll send you a photo of the receipt.
Tomorrow morning, before we start work.

alt: Kesho asubuhi, kabla ya kuanza kazi.
sw.note: kabla ha-tu-ja-anza = before we start.

en.text: True, it's been a long time. I have big news.

sw.text: Kweli, siku nyingi. Nina habari kubwa.

en.text: My wife gave birth last night.

sw.note: kujifungua = to give birth, the polite word.

en.text: Thank you. It's a girl.

sw.note: mtoto wa kike = a girl; mtoto wa kiume = a boy.

en.text: They're both fine, thank God.
On Saturday we're having a small celebration at home.

sw.text: Jumamosi tutakuwa na sherehe ndogo nyumbani.

en.text: Come at four in the afternoon.

sw.note: 4 p.m. = saa kumi jioni.

en.text: And you, when is your wedding?

sw.text: Na nyinyi je, harusi yenu ni lini?
sw.note: nyinyi, yenu = you, your, for a couple or a group.

en.text: May God give you children too.

sw.note: a-wa-jalie = may he grant you (plural).

en.text: Amen. Thank you, see you on Saturday.
How long have you been learning?
Only a few weeks? Well done, you're working hard.

alt: Wiki chache tu? Hongera, unajaribu sana.

en.text: Then tell me what you did today, in Kiswahili.

sw.text: Basi niambie ulichofanya leo, kwa Kiswahili.
alt: Basi nieleze ulichofanya leo, kwa Kiswahili.
sw.note: u-li-cho-fanya = what you did: -cho- means what.

en.text: Very good, I understood everything.
Come every day and we'll practise together.

alt: Pitia hapa kila siku, tuongee Kiswahili.

en.text: The lime needs to sit for two weeks.
Sorry I'm late, the bike had a flat tyre.

sw.text: Samahani kwa kuchelewa, pikipiki ilipata pancha.

en.text: Good morning, boss, the guys are here.

sw.text: Habari za asubuhi, bosi, vijana wamefika.

en.text: The lime is hot, don't touch it.

sw.note: Slaking makes lime boil hot; keep hands and eyes away.

en.text: The lime has sat two weeks, it's ready.

sw.text: Chokaa imekaa wiki mbili, iko tayari.

en.text: Yes, the guys are mixing the lime right now.

sw.text: Ndiyo, vijana wanachanganya chokaa sasa hivi.

en.text: One pan of lime, three pans of sand.

sw.text: Karai moja ya chokaa, karai tatu za mchanga.
sw.note: Karai = the metal pan every site uses to carry mortar.

en.text: Yes, only lime, like you wanted.
This wall has a crack, we'll fill it first.

sw.text: Ukuta huu una ufa, tutauziba kwanza.

en.text: The sun was very strong, the wall dried fast.

sw.text: Jua lilikuwa kali sana, ukuta ulikauka haraka.

en.text: Wet the walls morning and evening.

sw.text: Nyunyizia kuta maji asubuhi na jioni.

en.text: It's ten o'clock, the guys want tea.

sw.text: Ni saa nne, vijana wanataka chai.
sw.note: Saa nne = ten o'clock, four hours after dawn.

en.text: Thank you for the tea, boss.
There's only a little sand left.
The workers are asking about their pay.
My trowel has gone missing.
Send it to my number, as usual.

sw.text: Tuma kwa namba yangu kama kawaida.

en.text: I'll send you the receipt in the evening.
Tell me, what is it?
I'll send the fundi tomorrow morning.
He'll come at nine in the morning.

sw.note: Saa tatu asubuhi = nine in the morning.

en.text: From next month, the rent will go up by two thousand.

sw.text: Kuanzia mwezi ujao, kodi itapanda kwa elfu mbili.

en.text: Then let the rent stay the same until you move out.

sw.text: Basi kodi ibaki ilivyo mpaka utakapohama.
sw.note: u-taka-po-hama = when you move out.

en.text: Give me one month's notice before you move out.

sw.text: Nipe notisi ya mwezi mmoja kabla hujahama.

en.text: Rent is paid on the first of every month.

sw.text: Kodi inalipwa tarehe mosi kila mwezi.
sw.note: Tarehe mosi = the first day of the month.

en.text: The rent is ten thousand a month.

sw.text: Kodi ni elfu kumi kwa mwezi.

en.text: The deposit is one month's rent.

sw.text: Amana ni kodi ya mwezi mmoja.
sw.note: Many landlords just say deposit.

en.text: The keys are with the caretaker.
Leave the keys with me when you go out.
The water bill is separate.
Water only comes on Tuesday and Friday.

sw.text: Maji yanatoka Jumanne na Ijumaa tu.

en.text: Please don't be late paying the rent.
Where's your bike today?
I'm at the gate, come out.
I'll be at the stage at five in the evening.

sw.text: Nitakuwa kwenye stendi saa kumi na moja jioni.
sw.note: saa kumi na moja jioni = five in the evening.

en.text: Kilifi, Kilifi, two more people!

sw.note: bado watu wawili = two more people; a matatu leaves when it is full.

en.text: Yes, get in, we're leaving right now.

sw.note: Conductors say sasa hivi even while the matatu is still filling.

en.text: Kilifi is two hundred.
The bag is fifty shillings extra.
Sit at the back, the front is taken.
We'll leave when it's full.

sw.note: gari takes li- words: gari likijaa, gari limejaa.

en.text: We're leaving right now, don't worry.
Your fare, brother.
I'll give you your change when we get there.
Here's your change, seven hundred and fifty.

sw.text: Hii hapa chenji yako, mia saba na hamsini.

en.text: Let's put your bag on the roof.

sw.text: Tuweke mzigo wako juu ya gari.

en.text: Move over a little, brother.
This one is full, take the next one.
Welcome, brother, how can I help you?
This one is very strong, it's eight hundred shillings.

sw.text: Hii ni imara sana, ni shilingi mia nane.

en.text: I'll let you have it for seven hundred.
Anything else?
Nails are two hundred shillings a kilo.

sw.text: Misumari ni shilingi mia mbili kwa kilo.

en.text: How will you carry these iron sheets?

sw.note: -ya- in utayabeba stands for mabati.

en.text: Don't worry, we can deliver it for you.
Transport is one thousand shillings.
The truck is out, we'll bring it tomorrow morning.

sw.note: gari takes li-: gari limetoka, gari liko wapi?
