en.text: The number is up there on the wall.
Park it there in the shade.

sw.note: kivuli = shade; kivulini = in the shade.

en.text: Colour is thirty shillings a page.

sw.text: Rangi ni shilingi thelathini kwa ukurasa.

en.text: Show me your ID.
Sign here.
This one says patience brings blessings.

sw.note: Subira huvuta heri is an old saying, often printed on kanga.

en.text: We close at six today.

sw.text: Leo tunafunga saa kumi na mbili jioni.

en.text: You're up early today, my friend.
We've just come back from the sea.
The wind was strong, but we caught fish.

sw.text: Upepo ulikuwa mkali, lakini tulipata samaki.

en.text: We have changu, kolekole and octopus.

sw.note: Kolekole = a large coast fish, good for grilling.

en.text: There are no prawns today, come tomorrow.
Okay, I'll keep them for you.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-wek-e-a = I will keep for you.

en.text: A kilo of octopus is four hundred shillings.

sw.text: Kilo ya pweza ni shilingi mia nne.
alt: Pweza ni mia nne kwa kilo.

en.text: Okay, take them for seven hundred.
Cleaning is fifty shillings, wait a little.

sw.text: Kusafisha ni shilingi hamsini, subiri kidogo.

en.text: We go back out to sea at nine tonight.

sw.note: Saa tatu usiku = nine at night on the Swahili clock.

en.text: You're welcome to come, but wait for the wind to drop.
Done, I've already cleaned them.

sw.note: ni-me-sha-wa-safisha = I-have-already-them-cleaned.

en.text: How are you going to cook them?
In the kusi season the sea gets rough.

sw.note: Kusi = the season of strong south winds in the middle of the year.

en.text: Look at the eyes, these are fresh.

sw.note: Clear eyes mean a fresh fish.

en.text: The boats arrive at six in the morning.

sw.text: Mashua zinafika saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: Saa kumi na mbili asubuhi = six in the morning.

en.text: Did the dawn call to prayer wake you up?
Today is the first day of Ramadan.

sw.text: Leo ni siku ya kwanza ya Ramadhani.

en.text: Are you fasting too?
Thank you, you're a good neighbour.
We break the fast at half past six in the evening.

sw.text: Tunafuturu saa kumi na mbili na nusu jioni.
sw.note: saa kumi na mbili na nusu jioni = half past six in the evening.

en.text: Come and break the fast with us this evening.
Don't bring anything, just come.
We pray first, then we eat.

sw.note: On the coast you also hear kuswali for kusali, to pray.

en.text: Come at six, before the call to prayer.

sw.text: Njoo saa kumi na mbili, kabla ya adhana.

en.text: Pray for us, my brother.
Friday prayers are at one in the afternoon.

sw.text: Sala ya Ijumaa ni saa saba mchana.
sw.note: saa saba mchana = one in the afternoon.

en.text: Come to church with us on Sunday.
Just wear decent clothes.

sw.note: nguo za heshima = modest clothes, literally clothes of respect.

en.text: Eid is tomorrow if the moon is seen.
What religion are you?
We have a harambee at church on Saturday.
Greet my father first, then my mother.
Come inside and sit down.
Thank you very much, my son.

sw.note: mwanangu = my child; elders say it warmly to young people.

en.text: All right, tell us about yourself.
Where do your parents live?
How long have you known each other?
This is my uncle, my mother's brother.

sw.text: Huyu ni mjomba wangu, kaka yake mama.

en.text: Wash your hands, the food is ready.

sw.note: kunawa = to wash hands or face. A jug and basin often come to you.

en.text: Eat, don't be shy.

sw.note: kuona haya = to feel shy.

en.text: No, just sit, you're our guest.

sw.text: Hapana, keti tu, wewe ni mgeni wetu.

en.text: Where will you live after the wedding?

sw.note: m-ta-ishi = you (both) will live.

en.text: The dowry is a matter for the elders.
Bring your elders, and we'll talk.
Take good care of our daughter.
Welcome to our family.
Greet your parents for us.
Shall we choose the wedding date today?
A Saturday or a Sunday?
My mother wants a big wedding.
So how many people should we invite?
My aunts have to be invited.

sw.note: shangazi = a father's sister.

en.text: Where should we hold the wedding?
And what about the food?

sw.note: Na ... je? = and what about ...?

en.text: The cook wants five hundred shillings a plate.

sw.text: Mpishi anataka shilingi mia tano kwa sahani.

en.text: Your friends said they'll contribute.
And what about the photographer?
Yes, I know one.
The committee will meet on Sunday at four in the afternoon.

sw.text: Kamati itakutana Jumapili saa kumi jioni.
sw.note: saa kumi = the tenth hour after dawn: four in the afternoon.

en.text: So far we've collected fifty thousand.
Come back on Friday to try it on.

sw.note: u-i-jaribu = you-it-try (the suit).

en.text: That date is already booked.
I heard you're getting married, congratulations.

sw.note: kuoa = a man marries; kuolewa = a woman gets married.

en.text: Welcome, boss, have a seat.
There are two people ahead of you.

sw.note: wawili = two (people); the number changes to match the noun.

en.text: All right, it's your turn.
How do you want your hair cut?
Shall I do your beard too?
Don't worry, this is a new blade.

sw.note: wembe takes huu for 'this'.

en.text: Yes, I've cleaned it.

sw.note: ni-me-i-safisha = I-have-it-cleaned (the clippers).

en.text: The power's gone off, sorry.
Don't worry, the power will be back soon.
Yes, I'll finish it with scissors.
Look in the mirror, is it okay?

sw.note: ji-angalie = look at yourself.

en.text: It's one hundred and fifty with the beard.

sw.text: Ni mia moja na hamsini pamoja na ndevu.

en.text: Thanks, boss, come again.
About half an hour more.
Braiding is two thousand five hundred.

sw.text: Kusuka ni elfu mbili na mia tano.

en.text: I'm almost done, wait for me.
Is this your first time here?

sw.text: Ni mara yako ya kwanza kuja hapa?

en.text: Will you pay with SHA or cash?

sw.text: Utalipa kwa SHA au pesa taslimu?
alt: Utatumia SHA au utalipa pesa taslimu?

en.text: What else are you feeling?
Your temperature is thirty-nine.

sw.text: Joto lako ni thelathini na tisa.
alt: Joto lako ni nyuzi thelathini na tisa.
sw.note: joto is a li- noun: joto lako.

en.text: We'll test you for malaria first.

sw.note: tu-ta-ku-pima = we-will-you-test.

en.text: Go to the lab for a blood test.

sw.note: u-ka-pimwe = go and be tested.

en.text: Let me prick your finger.

sw.note: kuchoma = to prick; also used for an injection.

en.text: No, just a little.
The results will be ready in twenty minutes.

sw.text: Majibu yatakuwa tayari baada ya dakika ishirini.
alt: Majibu yatatoka baada ya dakika ishirini.

en.text: You have malaria, but it's not too serious.

sw.text: Una malaria, lakini si kali sana.

en.text: You don't have malaria, it's just a cold.
Take four tablets twice a day, for three days.

sw.text: Meza vidonge vinne mara mbili kwa siku, kwa siku tatu.
sw.note: Meza = swallow; many people say kunywa dawa for any medicine.

en.text: Take them after eating.
Yes, finish it even if you feel better.

alt: Ndiyo, imalize yote hata ukipata nafuu.
sw.note: i-malize = it-finish; i- stands for dozi.

en.text: You might feel a little dizzy.
If you don't feel better in three days, come back.

sw.text: Usipopata nafuu baada ya siku tatu, rudi.
sw.note: u-sipo-pata = if you don't get.

en.text: I don't have enough cash right now.

sw.text: Sina pesa taslimu za kutosha sasa hivi.
sw.note: Agents call their cash float: sina float = I've no cash.

en.text: I only have two thousand.
Try the agent next to the chemist.

sw.text: Jaribu wakala aliye karibu na kemisti.

en.text: The charge is about thirty shillings.
I need your ID number.

sw.note: Agents write each customer's ID number in a book.

en.text: Count your money here in front of me.

sw.text: Hesabu pesa zako hapa mbele yangu.

en.text: Sorry, take this new one.
What else can I help you with?
When did you send it?
Forward that message to Safaricom.
What did they say?
Don't worry, it'll come back.
Take a ticket and sit over there.
Deposits are at counter number three.

sw.text: Kuweka pesa ni kaunta namba tatu.

en.text: Come tomorrow with your ID to collect it.

sw.text: Njoo kesho na kitambulisho chako uichukue.
sw.note: u-i-chukue = so you collect it; i- stands for kadi (card).

en.text: The system is slow today.
Hello, may I come in?

sw.note: Hodi is called at the door; answer Karibu.

en.text: Is the power off at your place too?
No, the power is off in the whole area.

sw.note: eneo takes li-: eneo lote.

en.text: I don't know, they're fixing the transformer.
I already called, they said by nine tonight.

sw.text: Nimeshapiga simu, wamesema kufikia saa tatu usiku.
sw.note: 9 p.m. = saa tatu usiku. nime-sha- = I have already.

en.text: Does your laptop have any charge?
Shall I turn on my hotspot for you?

sw.note: ni-ku-washi-e = shall I switch on for you.

en.text: The café in town has a generator and wifi.

sw.text: Mgahawa wa mjini una jenereta na wifi.

en.text: I put in solar last year.

sw.note: mwaka jana = last year.

en.text: A small solar kit is about fifty thousand shillings.

sw.text: Sola ndogo ni kama shilingi elfu hamsini.
sw.note: elfu hamsini = fifty thousand; elfu comes first.

en.text: Look, the power is back.
Okay, I'll leave you to your work.
Give me your meter number.
There's a power fault in your area.

sw.text: Kuna hitilafu ya umeme katika eneo lenu.
sw.note: hitilafu = a fault; eneo takes li-: eneo lenu.

en.text: Turn off the router, then turn it on again.
The problem is outside, not in your house.

sw.text: Tatizo liko nje, si ndani ya nyumba yako.
sw.note: tatizo takes li-: tatizo liko.

en.text: Come in here, under the tarpaulin.
The rain is getting heavy, I'm packing up now.
One heap is seventy shillings today.

sw.text: Leo fungu moja ni shilingi sabini.

en.text: The trucks didn't come because of the rain.

sw.text: Magari hayakuja kwa sababu ya mvua.
sw.note: ha-ya-ku-ja = they did not come (ya- for magari).

en.text: They're fine, it's only rainwater.

sw.text: Ni nzuri, ni maji ya mvua tu.

en.text: Take them all for two hundred.
Move over to this side, it's leaking there.
How will you get home?
Wait a little, it will stop soon.
The rain has eased, you can go now.
Everything gets expensive when it rains.

sw.text: Kila kitu kinapanda bei mvua ikinyesha.

en.text: The road from the farms is cut off.

sw.note: imekatika: a road broken or washed out by rain.

en.text: Mind the mud there.
Nobody is going out in this rain.
The water is too deep, the bike will stall.

sw.text: Maji ni mengi sana, pikipiki itazima.

en.text: You're soaking wet, come and dry off.
Your membership has run out.
It's two thousand five hundred shillings now.

sw.text: Ni shilingi elfu mbili na mia tano sasa.
alt: Sasa ni elfu mbili na mia tano.

en.text: Yes, the price of electricity has gone up.
Pay on M-Pesa, then show me the message.

sw.text: Lipa kwa M-Pesa, kisha unionyeshe ujumbe.
sw.note: The message = the M-Pesa text that proves you paid.

en.text: Sorry, the fan is broken.
Yes, go ahead and open them.

sw.note: ya = them, for madirisha (windows).

en.text: Show me your push-ups.
Straighten your back, then go down slowly.

sw.text: Nyoosha mgongo, kisha ushuke pole pole.

en.text: Good, but don't hold your breath.

sw.note: kuzuia pumzi = to hold your breath; u-si-zuie = don't hold it.

en.text: Do five sets of twenty push-ups.

sw.text: Fanya seti tano za push-up ishirini.

en.text: You'll manage, start slowly.
Take it, I'm done.
We open at five in the morning.

sw.text: Tunafungua saa kumi na moja alfajiri.
sw.note: Saa kumi na moja alfajiri = five in the morning.

en.text: Don't train tomorrow, rest.
Spread your hands a little wider.
Write your name here.
Welcome, brother. What's wrong with it today?

sw.text: Karibu, kaka. Ina shida gani leo?

en.text: When was the last service?
The oil is worn out, it's very black.

sw.note: imechoka = is tired; old oil is tired oil.

en.text: The brake pads are worn out, we have to change them.

alt: Pedi za breki zimeisha, lazima tuzibadilishe.
sw.note: tu-zi-badilishe: zi = them, the brakes.

en.text: The original ones are eight hundred, the fake ones three hundred.

sw.text: Za halisi ni mia nane, za feki ni mia tatu.
sw.note: feki = fake; fundis say it all the time.

en.text: True, and the chain is loose too.
Yes, I'll tighten it right now.

sw.note: ni-ta-u-kaza: u = it, the chain (mnyororo).

en.text: It will be ready at four in the afternoon.

sw.note: saa kumi jioni = four in the afternoon; the clock counts from dawn.

en.text: The service is two thousand, with the oil.

sw.text: Sevisi ni elfu mbili, pamoja na oili.

en.text: The total is three thousand two hundred.

sw.text: Jumla ni elfu tatu na mia mbili.

en.text: The spark plug was worn out, I changed it too.
Bring it back in three months.
There's a nail in the back tyre.

sw.text: Kuna msumari kwenye tairi la nyuma.

en.text: Labour is five hundred, you'll buy the parts yourself.

sw.text: Ufundi ni mia tano, vipuri utanunua mwenyewe.

en.text: What do you think of it now?

sw.note: u-na-i-ona-je = you-are-it-seeing-how.

en.text: Take it for a ride and see.
Hello, boss, the water lorry is here.

sw.text: Habari, bosi, lori la maji limefika.

en.text: The lorry can't reach the gate, the road is narrow.

sw.text: Lori haliwezi kufika getini, njia ni nyembamba.

en.text: We'll run a long hose from the road.

sw.note: Mpira = a ball, and also a rubber hose.

en.text: How many litres does your tank take?
Then one lorry is enough.
Yes, you'll pay when the tank is full.
It's fresh piped water, not borehole water.

sw.text: Ni maji matamu ya bomba, si ya kisima.

en.text: Your tank is full to the top.
God willing, it will rain next week.

sw.text: Mungu akipenda, mvua itanyesha wiki ijayo.
sw.note: Mungu akipenda = God willing, said about any plan ahead.

en.text: Call me one day before.
This year the rain is late.
How many litres do you need?
Ten thousand litres is five thousand shillings.

sw.text: Lita elfu kumi ni shilingi elfu tano.

en.text: One jerrycan is thirty shillings.
I'll bring the jerrycans on the handcart.

sw.note: Mkokoteni = the wooden handcart used for water and goods.

en.text: Don't drink the borehole water, it's salty.

sw.text: Usinywe maji ya kisima, yana chumvi.

en.text: Who is that?
Welcome home, boss.

sw.note: Watchmen often call the owner bosi.

en.text: Did you get home safely?
Someone came looking for you.

sw.note: ku-ku-tafuta = to look for you.

en.text: He said he's your fundi.
He said he'll come back tomorrow morning.
Okay, I'll open for him.

sw.note: ni-ta-m-fungulia = I will open for him.

en.text: Boss, the torch batteries are finished.
Thank you, now I'll see well at night.
Go and sleep, I'm here.

sw.note: u-ka-lale = go and sleep: ka- means go and.

en.text: Good night, boss.
Nobody came today.
The dog only barks at strangers.

sw.note: hu- = usually: hu-wa-bwekea = usually barks at them.

en.text: Should I open the gate?
Can you pay me a bit early this month?

sw.text: Unaweza kunilipa mapema kidogo mwezi huu?

en.text: The hut leaks when it rains.

sw.note: mvua ikinyesha = when it rains.

en.text: Welcome to our chama.
The joining fee is five hundred shillings.

sw.text: Ada ya kujiunga ni shilingi mia tano.

en.text: Every member contributes two thousand shillings a month.

sw.text: Kila mwanachama anachanga shilingi elfu mbili kwa mwezi.

en.text: We meet on the last Sunday of every month.

sw.text: Tunakutana Jumapili ya mwisho ya kila mwezi.

en.text: The meeting starts at three in the afternoon.
If you're late, the fine is two hundred shillings.

sw.text: Ukichelewa, faini ni shilingi mia mbili.

en.text: Send it to my number, I'm the treasurer.

sw.text: Tuma kwa namba yangu, mimi ndiye mweka hazina.

en.text: Your turn is in December.
Why do you need it early?

sw.note: -zi- stands for pesa, the money.

en.text: Talk to the chairperson at the meeting.

sw.note: mwenyekiti = chairperson, literally the owner of the chair.

en.text: See you on Sunday, don't be late.

sw.note: u-si-chelewe = don't be late; it ends in -e.

en.text: We have twelve members.

sw.note: wawili = two, for people.

en.text: The interest is ten percent.
Did you send your contribution?
Rules are rules.
My father passed away last night.
Thank you, we're coping.

sw.note: The usual answer to pole: tumeshapoa, we have already eased.

en.text: He was very fond of you.
Thank you, put them in the kitchen.
He'll be buried today after the midday prayer.

sw.text: Atazikwa leo baada ya sala ya adhuhuri.

en.text: We Muslims bury on the same day.

sw.note: A Muslim burial is quick, usually the same day.

en.text: Yes, we'll leave at half past twelve.

sw.text: Ndiyo, tutaondoka saa sita na nusu mchana.
sw.note: saa sita na nusu mchana = half past twelve.

en.text: Send it to my uncle's number, he's keeping the money.

sw.text: Tuma kwa namba ya mjomba wangu, ndiye anayeshika pesa.

en.text: Amen, thank you for coming to comfort us.
We need more chairs for the guests.
Have you heard? The old man next door has passed away.
The burial is on Saturday at his home in Marafa.

sw.note: kwao = at their home; many families bury at the family's home place.

en.text: Thank you, you're like a brother to us.

sw.text: Asante, wewe ni kama ndugu yetu.

en.text: God's work has no mistakes.

sw.note: A common saying at funerals: we accept what God has done.

en.text: Come in and sit, have some tea.
Men sit outside, women sit inside.
My respects.

sw.note: Children greet every adult this way; answer Marahaba.

en.text: We're fine.

sw.note: The answer to Hamjambo?

en.text: It was good, we played football.
Yes, we've already finished.

sw.note: tu-me-sha-maliza = we have already finished.

en.text: Please lend us your ball so we can play.

sw.note: Tunaomba = we ask (for): the polite way to ask.

en.text: We'll be careful.
This is a young coconut.

sw.note: dafu = a green coconut for drinking; nazi = a ripe one.

en.text: That's not how you say it.

sw.note: ha-i-semwi = it is not said.

en.text: Your Kiswahili is funny.

sw.note: ki-na-chekesha = it makes people laugh.

en.text: We'll teach you every day.
We'll bring it back before dark.

sw.note: tu-ta-u-rudisha: u- stands for mpira (the ball).

en.text: Do you have sweets today?
Thank you for the sweets.
Please give us a ride on the bike.
Are the children bothering you?
If they bother you, send them home.

sw.note: wa-ki-ku-sumbua = if they bother you.

en.text: Welcome, a table for how many?

sw.note: Karibuni = welcome, to more than one person.

en.text: Have you booked?
Come this way, sit here.

sw.note: -ni makes an order plural: njoo, njooni; kaa, kaeni.

en.text: What would you like to drink?
What will you have today?
Yes, we have prawns, octopus and grilled fish.

sw.text: Ndiyo, tuna kamba, pweza na samaki wa kuchoma.

en.text: And what will your partner have?

sw.note: Mwenzako = your companion, the person with you.

en.text: The food will be ready in twenty minutes.

sw.text: Chakula kitakuwa tayari baada ya dakika ishirini.

en.text: Is everything okay with the food?
Here is your bill.
Sorry, I'll correct it right now.

sw.note: ni-ta-i-rekebisha: i = it, the bill.

en.text: Thank you both, come again.

sw.note: Asanteni, karibuni: the -ni ending speaks to both of you.

en.text: Swimming for the day is two thousand five hundred shillings.

sw.text: Kuogelea kwa siku ni shilingi elfu mbili na mia tano.

en.text: It includes lunch and a towel.

sw.text: Inajumuisha chakula cha mchana na taulo.
alt: Ni pamoja na chakula cha mchana na taulo.

en.text: Sorry for the wait, here is your food.

sw.text: Samahani kwa kuchelewa, chakula hiki hapa.
sw.note: Chakula hiki hapa = here is the food.

en.text: The wifi password is on the menu.

sw.text: Nywila ya wifi iko kwenye menyu.
alt: Password ya wifi iko kwenye menyu.
sw.note: Nywila = password; many people just say password.

en.text: Stop there, park at the side.
Fine, thanks. Where are you heading?
Your licence, please.
Is this motorbike yours?
Show me the insurance sticker.
Where is your reflector jacket?

sw.text: Jaketi yako ya reflekta iko wapi?
alt: Jaketi yako ya kuakisi mwanga iko wapi?

en.text: Fasten your helmet properly.
Your back light isn't working.
Fix it before tonight.
Everything is in order, you can go.

sw.text: Kila kitu kiko sawa, unaweza kwenda.

en.text: Ride carefully.
It's just a routine check.

sw.note: ukaguzi = an inspection, from ku-kagua, to inspect.

en.text: Where are you coming from now?
Bring your licence to the station tomorrow.

sw.note: Leta = bring (never lete).

en.text: Take off your helmet, please.
Do you have your ID?
My phone is new.

sw.note: simu yangu … mpya: N nouns take y- and an n-/m- adjective.

en.text: This house is small, but it's nice.

sw.text: Nyumba hii ni ndogo, lakini ni nzuri.
sw.note: hii … ndogo … nzuri: an N singular agrees as hii and n-.

en.text: These houses are all new.

sw.note: nyumba is one or many; the plural shows on hizi and zote.

en.text: The road to the beach is long.

sw.text: Barabara ya kwenda ufukweni ni ndefu.
sw.note: barabara ya … ndefu: ya- and n- for an N noun.

en.text: The phone fell and broke.

sw.note: i-li-anguka, i-ka-vunjika: simu takes i- on the verb.

en.text: My clothes got dirty at the building site.

sw.note: nguo zangu zi-me-: the plural takes z- and zi-.

en.text: I bought two bottles of water.

sw.note: chupa mbili za: an N plural takes za for of.

en.text: Where's the charger? I can't see it.

sw.note: chaja iko … si-i-on-i: -i- is the object for an N noun.

en.text: I've sent the photos, did you get them?

sw.note: u-me-zi-pata = have you got them: -zi- for picha (many).

en.text: The news is good today.

sw.note: habari … nzuri: N adjectives take n-.

en.text: Those bananas are sweet.

sw.note: ndizi zile: the plural shows on zile.

en.text: My motorbike is at the fundi's.

sw.note: pikipiki yangu iko: y- and i- for an N noun.

en.text: I'll take another way back home.

sw.note: njia nyingine: an N noun takes ny-ingine.

en.text: All the lights have been switched off.

sw.note: taa zote zi-me-zim-w-a: the plural shows on zote and zi-.

en.text: The tea is still hot.

sw.note: chai … ya moto: ya for an N noun.

en.text: Which cap do you want, this one or that one?

sw.text: Unataka kofia ipi, hii au ile?
sw.note: kofia ipi, hii, ile: which, this and that for an N noun.

en.text: The medicine I was given is finished.

sw.note: dawa ni-li-yo-pewa: -yo- (which) agrees with dawa.

en.text: In three weeks I'll be in Nairobi.

sw.text: Baada ya wiki tatu nitakuwa Nairobi.
sw.note: wiki tatu: numbers after an N noun keep their plain form.

en.text: The bills this month are big.

sw.text: Bili za mwezi huu ni kubwa.
sw.note: bili za … kubwa: kubwa takes no prefix with N nouns.

en.text: My dream is to build a big house.

sw.text: Ndoto yangu ni kujenga nyumba kubwa.
sw.note: ndoto yangu … nyumba kubwa: y- and a bare kubwa for N.

en.text: My key isn't here, did you take it?

sw.note: ha-u-po, u-me-u-chukua: U nouns take u- as subject and as object.

en.text: The wall is long, but it isn't finished.

sw.note: ukuta … mrefu … ha-u-ja-: U takes m- adjectives and u-.

en.text: The walls are tall now.

sw.note: kuta … ndefu: the plural of ukuta agrees like N.

en.text: This song is really beautiful.

sw.note: wimbo huu … mzuri: huu and m- for a U singular.

en.text: I like her songs.

sw.note: nyimbo zake: the plural of wimbo takes z-.

en.text: The power has gone again.

sw.note: umeme u-me-katika: u- on the verb.

en.text: Sleep won't come to me.

sw.note: ha-u-ni-ji-i = it doesn't come to me: usingizi takes u-.

en.text: Your message reached me, thank you.

sw.note: ujumbe wako u-me-ni-fikia: w- and u- for ujumbe.

en.text: The wind this morning was cold.

sw.text: Upepo wa asubuhi hii ulikuwa wa baridi.
sw.note: upepo wa … u-li-kuwa wa: w- and u- for upepo.

en.text: The truth is, I'm tired.

sw.note: ukweli = the truth: a U noun with no plural.

en.text: Their love is strong.

sw.note: upendo wao u-na: w-ao and u-na for upendo.

en.text: Porridge in the morning is good for me.

sw.text: Uji wa asubuhi ni mzuri kwangu.
sw.note: uji wa … mzuri: U takes w- and m-.

en.text: One wall is enough for today.

sw.note: ukuta mmoja u-na-tosha: m-moja and u- for U.

en.text: Where have you put the keys?

sw.note: u-me-zi-weka: -zi- for funguo, the plural of ufunguo.

en.text: Show me another page.

sw.note: ukurasa mwingine: U takes mw-ingine.

en.text: All the pages are torn.

sw.note: kurasa zote zi-: the plural of ukurasa agrees like N.

en.text: The beach is long and empty in the morning.

sw.text: Ufuo ni mrefu na mtupu asubuhi.
sw.note: ufuo … mrefu … mtupu: U adjectives take m-.

en.text: That illness is serious.

sw.note: ugonjwa huo … mbaya: huo and m- for U.

en.text: Her face lit up when she saw the ring.

sw.text: Uso wake ulijaa furaha alipoona pete.
sw.note: uso wake u-li-jaa: w- and u- for uso.

en.text: My advice is that you rest early.

sw.note: ushauri wangu: w-angu for a U noun; u-pumzik-e = that you rest.

en.text: Running in the morning helps me.

sw.note: kukimbia … ku-na-ni-saidia: a verb used as a noun takes ku- on the verb.

en.text: Meditating every day has changed my life.

sw.text: Kutafakari kila siku kumebadilisha maisha yangu.
sw.note: ku-me-badilisha: kutafakari is the subject, so ku-.

en.text: Swimming in the ocean is good for the body.

sw.text: Kuogelea baharini ni kuzuri kwa mwili.
sw.note: kuogelea … kuzuri: an adjective after a ku- noun takes ku-.

en.text: The way I speak Kiswahili keeps getting better every day.

sw.text: Kuongea kwangu Kiswahili kunazidi kuwa bora kila siku.
sw.note: kuongea kwangu ku-na-zidi: kwangu and ku- agree with the ku- noun.

en.text: Eating too much at night isn't good.

sw.note: kula kwingi … kuzuri: kw- and ku- agree with kula.

en.text: Waking up early was hard at first.

sw.note: ku-li-kuwa ku-gumu: the verb and the adjective both take ku-.

en.text: Her singing is lovely.

sw.note: kuimba kwake ku-na-pendeza: kwake and ku- for kuimba.

en.text: Walking on the beach calms me down.

sw.note: ku-na-ni-tuliza = it calms me: ku- because kutembea is the subject.

en.text: Building with lime takes time.

sw.note: kujenga … ku-na-chukua: ku- for the verb-noun subject.

en.text: Learning Kiswahili isn't hard if you practise.

sw.text: Kujifunza Kiswahili si kugumu ukifanya mazoezi.
sw.note: kujifunza … kugumu: the adjective takes ku-.

en.text: All this travelling has worn me out.

sw.note: kusafiri kote huku ku-me-: kote, huku and ku- all agree.

en.text: Working like this without rest isn't good.

sw.text: Kufanya kazi huku bila kupumzika si kuzuri.
sw.note: huku = this, for a ku- noun; kuzuri agrees too.

en.text: Sleeping with the fan on helps me.

sw.note: kulala … ku-na-ni-saidia: ku- for kulala.

en.text: My cooking still isn't very good.

sw.text: Kupika kwangu bado si kuzuri sana.
sw.note: kupika kwangu … kuzuri: kw- and ku- for kupika.

en.text: Her laughing made everyone laugh.

sw.note: ku-li-wa-chekesha: ku- as subject, -wa- them, -esha makes it happen.

en.text: The dogs' barking woke me up.

sw.note: kubweka kwa mbwa ku-li-ni-amsha: kwa (of) and ku- agree with kubweka.

en.text: Riding in the rain made me really tired.

sw.note: ku-li-ni-chosha = it tired me: ku- for kuendesha.

en.text: All that talking was for nothing.

sw.note: kote kule ku-li-kuwa: all three agree with kuongea.

en.text: Does getting up early bother you?

sw.note: ku-na-ku-sumbua: the first ku- is the subject, the second is you.

en.text: Coming here was a good idea.

sw.note: kuja … ku-li-kuwa: ku- for the verb-noun subject.

en.text: It's hot here, let's sit in the shade.

sw.note: hapa pana = here there is, at this very spot: pa-.

en.text: Is the fundi here? Yes, he's here.

sw.note: yupo = he is here: -po for a definite spot.

en.text: Put the bag there, by the door.

sw.text: Weka begi pale, karibu na mlango.
sw.note: pale = there, a spot you can point at.

en.text: This is a good place to build a house.

sw.text: Hapa ni mahali pazuri pa kujenga nyumba.
sw.note: mahali pazuri pa: mahali agrees with pa- (pazuri, pa).

en.text: Wait for me right there, I'm coming.

sw.note: hapo hapo = right there.

en.text: There's a mosquito on the table.

sw.note: mezani pana = on the table there is: a surface takes pa-.

en.text: It's cold over there in Canada now.

sw.note: kule … kuna = over there, there is: ku- for a general area.

en.text: Things are good here on the coast.

sw.note: huku = around here, a general area.

en.text: How are things at your place?

sw.note: ku-ko-je = how is it there: ku- for a place in general.

en.text: Where are you? I'm at the market.

sw.note: uko, niko: -ko for where you are, somewhere around.

en.text: There are lots of people on the beach today.

sw.note: ufukweni kuna = at the beach there are: ku- for an area.

en.text: What's in the fridge?

sw.note: mna = there is, inside: mu- for inside.

en.text: It's hot in the room.

sw.note: chumbani mna = in the room there is.

en.text: Is anyone inside? Yes, he's in there.

sw.note: yumo = he is inside: -mo for inside.

en.text: There's nothing in here.

sw.note: humu = in here; hamna = there isn't, inside.

en.text: The keys are in the bag.

sw.note: zimo = they are inside: funguo takes zi-, -mo for inside.

en.text: Here or there? Here is better.

sw.text: Hapa au pale? Hapa ni pazuri zaidi.
sw.note: hapa … pazuri: a spot takes pa- on the adjective.

en.text: Is there a shop near here?

sw.note: kuna = there is (somewhere around).

en.text: Put everything in there.

sw.note: humo = in there: -mo for inside.

en.text: Where I live there are lots of coconut trees.

sw.note: ni-na-po-ishi = where I live; kuna = there are.

en.text: I'm reading a book about Kenya.

sw.note: ni-na-soma = I-now-read: who, then when, then the verb.

en.text: You speak Kiswahili well.

sw.note: u-na-ongea = you-now-speak.

en.text: She cooked pilau yesterday.

sw.note: a-li-pika = she-past-cook.

en.text: We've finished the foundation.

sw.note: tu-me-maliza = we-done-finish: -me- for what is done.

en.text: Will you all come to the wedding?

sw.note: m-ta-kuja = you all-will-come.

en.text: They arrived at eight.

sw.note: wa-li-fika = they-past-arrive; saa mbili = eight o'clock.

en.text: I usually wake up before five.

sw.text: Mimi huamka kabla ya saa kumi na moja.
sw.note: hu-amka = usually wake: hu- fills both slots.

en.text: The book has arrived.

sw.note: ki-me-fika = it-done-arrive: kitabu is KI, so ki-.

en.text: The car will be ready tomorrow.

sw.note: li-ta-kuwa = it-will-be: gari is JI-MA, so li-.

en.text: The phone is ringing.

sw.note: i-na-lia = it-now-ring: simu is N, so i-.

en.text: The photos came out well.

sw.note: zi-me-toka = they-done-come out: picha (many) takes zi-.

en.text: The wall fell down last night.

sw.note: u-li-anguka = it-past-fall: ukuta takes u-.

en.text: The mangoes are ripening.

sw.note: ya-na-iva = they-now-ripen: maembe take ya-.

en.text: When I arrive, I'll phone.

sw.note: ni-ki-fika, ni-ta-piga = I-when-arrive, I-will-make (the call).

en.text: We're going to the beach, are you all coming?

sw.note: tu-na-kwenda, m-na-kuja: the who slot changes, the when slot stays.

en.text: He hasn't arrived yet.

sw.note: ha-ja-fika = he-not yet-arrive: the negative has its own slots.

en.text: We'll see.

sw.note: tu-ta-ona = we-will-see.

en.text: My fiancée is sleeping, speak quietly.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu analala, ongea kwa sauti ya chini.
sw.note: a-na-lala = she-now-sleep.

en.text: The builders started work at seven.

sw.note: wa-li-anza = they-past-start; saa moja = seven o'clock.

en.text: The food will get cold.

sw.note: ki-ta-poa = it-will-cool: chakula is KI.

en.text: Can you hear me well?

sw.note: u-na-ni-sikia = you-now-me-hear: the object sits right before the verb.

en.text: I saw you at the market yesterday.

sw.note: ni-li-ku-ona = I-past-you-see.

en.text: I'll call her after work.

sw.note: ni-ta-m-pigia = I-will-her-call.

en.text: I've already told him.

sw.note: ni-me-sha-mw-ambia: mw- for him before a vowel.

en.text: The fundi told us to wait.

sw.note: a-li-tu-ambia = he-past-us-tell.

en.text: I'll pay them on Friday.

sw.note: ni-ta-wa-lipa = I-will-them-pay.

en.text: I bought a book, and now I'm reading it.

sw.note: ni-na-ki-soma = I'm reading it: -ki- for kitabu.

en.text: I've found my things.

sw.note: ni-me-vi-pata = I've found them: -vi- for vitu.

en.text: The car is dirty, I'll wash it.

sw.note: ni-ta-li-osha = I'll wash it: -li- for gari.

en.text: I bought mangoes and ate them all.

sw.note: ni-ka-ya-la = and I ate them: -ya- for maembe.

en.text: My old motorbike? I sold it last year.

sw.text: Pikipiki yangu ya zamani? Niliiuza mwaka jana.
sw.note: ni-li-i-uza = I sold it: -i- for pikipiki.

en.text: The keys? I've put them on the table.

sw.note: ni-me-zi-weka = I've put them: -zi- for funguo.

en.text: The wall? We'll build it tomorrow.

sw.note: tu-ta-u-jenga = we will build it: -u- for ukuta.

en.text: I'm learning Kiswahili with my teacher.

sw.note: na-ji-funza = I teach myself: -ji- is self, so kujifunza = to learn.

en.text: Look after yourself on the road.

sw.note: ji-tunz-e = look after yourself.

en.text: Have you seen my fiancée? I'm looking for her.

sw.note: u-me-mw-ona, na-m-tafuta: -mw- and -m- for her.

en.text: Help me, please.

sw.note: ni-saidi-e = help me: a request with the object -ni-.

en.text: Don't disturb them, they're sleeping.

sw.note: u-si-wa-sumbu-e = don't disturb them.

en.text: Take us to the beach.

sw.note: tu-pelek-e = take us: -tu- us.

en.text: I love this house and I'll look after it well.

sw.text: Naipenda nyumba hii na nitaitunza vizuri.
sw.note: na-i-penda, ni-ta-i-tunza: -i- for nyumba.

en.text: Cook for me today, I'm tired.

sw.note: pik-i-a = cook for: -i- adds for someone.

en.text: I'll read it to you.

sw.note: som-e-a = read to: -e- after o.

en.text: I'm writing my parents a letter.

sw.note: andik-i-a = write to.

en.text: The video was watched a thousand times.

sw.note: tazam-w-a = be watched: -w- makes it done-to.

en.text: I've been invited to a wedding.

sw.note: alik-w-a = be invited.

en.text: The glass has broken.

sw.note: vunj-ik-a = get broken: -ik- says it happened, with no doer.

en.text: Your Kiswahili is easy to understand.

sw.note: elew-ek-a = be understandable: -ek- after e.

en.text: It's not possible today, maybe tomorrow.

sw.note: wez-ek-an-a = be possible: ha-i-…-i is its negative.

en.text: We love each other.

sw.note: pend-an-a = love each other: -an- makes it go both ways.

en.text: Let's help each other.

sw.note: saidi-an-e = help each other.

en.text: We understand each other now.

sw.note: elew-an-a = understand each other.

en.text: Show me how to do it.

sw.note: on-yesh-a = make see, show: -esh- causes it.

en.text: The fundi made me late today.

sw.note: chelew-esh-a = make late.

en.text: The heat woke me up early.

sw.note: am-sh-a = make wake: amka becomes amsha.

en.text: Put the baby to sleep.

sw.note: la-z-a = make sleep: lala becomes laza.

en.text: Open the door, I'll close it later.

sw.note: fung-u-a = undo the closing: -u- reverses the verb.

en.text: Unfold the map.

sw.note: kunj-u-a = unfold: -u- reverses kunja (fold).

en.text: We showed each other photos from home.

sw.note: on-yesh-an-a = show each other: two endings stacked.

en.text: Her mother cooked for me.

sw.note: pik-i-w-a = be cooked for: the applied, then the passive.

en.text: The door can be opened from outside.

sw.note: fung-u-k-a = can be opened: the reversive plus the stative.

en.text: My fiancée helps me a lot.

sw.note: mchumba wangu: a person (M-WA) takes w-angu.

en.text: My builders are coming tomorrow at seven.

sw.text: Mafundi wangu watakuja kesho saa moja.
sw.note: mafundi wangu: people take wangu, one or many.

en.text: My plan is to finish the house this year.

sw.text: Mpango wangu ni kumaliza nyumba mwaka huu.
sw.note: mpango wangu: an M-MI singular also takes w-angu.

en.text: My wall has a crack.

sw.note: ukuta wangu u-na: U nouns take w-angu and u-.

en.text: My house isn't finished yet.

sw.note: nyumba yangu: N nouns take y-angu.

en.text: My plans have changed this week.

sw.note: mipango yangu i-me-: an M-MI plural takes y-angu and i-.

en.text: My mangoes are ripe now.

sw.note: maembe yangu ya-me-iva: MA plurals take y-angu and ya-.

en.text: Where's my chair? Someone has taken it.

sw.text: Kiti changu kiko wapi? Mtu amekichukua.
sw.note: kiti changu … a-me-ki-chukua: KI takes ch-angu, and -ki- as the object.

en.text: My food is getting cold.

sw.note: chakula changu ki-na-poa: ch- and ki- for chakula.

en.text: My book is on the table.

sw.note: kitabu changu kiko: ch-angu and ki-ko.

en.text: My question is simple.

sw.note: swali langu: a JI-MA singular takes l-angu.

en.text: My idea is to build with lime.

sw.text: Wazo langu ni kujenga kwa chokaa.
sw.note: wazo langu: wazo is JI-MA, so l-angu.

en.text: My watermelon is bigger than yours.

sw.text: Tikiti langu ni kubwa kuliko lako.
sw.note: tikiti langu … lako: JI-MA takes l- for mine and yours.

en.text: My keys are on the motorbike.

sw.note: funguo zangu ziko: U plurals take z-angu and zi-.

en.text: My flip-flops broke at the beach.

sw.note: ndala zangu zi-me-katika: an N plural takes z-angu and zi-.

en.text: All my videos are on the laptop.

sw.text: Video zangu zote ziko kwenye kompyuta.
sw.note: video zangu zote ziko: z-angu, z-ote, zi-ko.

en.text: My shoes are at the door.

sw.note: viatu vyangu viko: a VI plural takes vy-angu and vi-.

en.text: Where are my things? I put them here.

sw.text: Vitu vyangu viko wapi? Niliviweka hapa.
sw.note: vitu vyangu … ni-li-vi-weka: vy- and -vi- for vitu.

en.text: Many of my books are in English.

sw.text: Vitabu vyangu vingi ni vya Kiingereza.
sw.note: vitabu vyangu vingi vya: VI plural all the way through.

en.text: Your motorbike is new, mine is old.

sw.text: Pikipiki yako ni mpya, yangu ni ya zamani.
sw.note: yako … yangu: pikipiki is N, so y- for yours and mine.

en.text: Come to my place on Saturday.

sw.note: kwangu = at my place: ku- for a place in general.

en.text: My place is far from town.

sw.note: kwangu = my place, where I live.

en.text: At my home we eat together.

sw.note: nyumbani kwangu: nyumbani is a place, so kw-angu.

en.text: For me, meditating in the morning is the best.

sw.text: Kwangu mimi, kutafakari asubuhi ni bora.
sw.note: kwangu mimi = as for me: my side of it.

en.text: My reading has improved a lot.

sw.note: kusoma kwangu ku-me-: a verb used as a noun agrees with ku-.

en.text: There's sand in my shoe.

sw.note: kiatuni mwangu = inside my shoe: -ni plus mw-angu for inside.

en.text: My phone is in my pocket.

sw.note: mfukoni mwangu = in my pocket: inside takes mw-angu.

en.text: In my room there's a big fan.

sw.note: chumbani mwangu mna = in my room there is: mw- and mna for inside.

en.text: In my heart, I know this is home.

sw.text: Moyoni mwangu najua hapa ni nyumbani.
sw.note: moyoni mwangu = in my heart: inside, so mw-angu.

en.text: I have lots of ideas in my head.

sw.note: kichwani mwangu = in my head.

en.text: This is my spot at the gym.

sw.note: pangu = my spot: pa- for one definite place.

en.text: Nobody sits in my place when I'm meditating.

sw.note: mahali pangu: mahali takes p-angu.

en.text: My place by the window is the best.

sw.text: Mahali pangu karibu na dirisha ni pazuri zaidi.
sw.note: mahali pangu … pazuri: mahali agrees with pa-.

en.text: Sorry, that's my seat.

sw.note: hapo ni pangu = that spot is mine.

en.text: My spot under the mango tree is cool.

sw.text: Mahali pangu chini ya mwembe pana baridi.
sw.note: mahali pangu … pana: pa- all the way through.

en.text: Is it far to your place?

sw.note: kwako = at your place: ku- with -ako.

en.text: Let's meet at his place.

sw.note: kwake = at his place; tu-kutan-e = let's meet.

en.text: What's in your bag?

sw.note: begini mwako mna = inside your bag there is.

en.text: Come to our place for dinner.

sw.text: Karibu kwetu kwa chakula cha jioni.
sw.note: kwetu = at our place.

en.text: This is your spot, sit here.

sw.note: pako = your spot: pa- with -ako.

en.text: If anyone asks, I'm at the gym.

sw.note: mtu yeyote = anyone: a person takes y-eyote.

en.text: Don't tell anyone yet.

sw.note: usi-mw-ambi-e mtu yeyote = don't tell anyone: -mw- and yeyote for the person.

en.text: Do you need anything from the market?

sw.note: chochote = anything: kitu is KI, so ch-ochote.

en.text: I didn't eat anything this morning.

sw.note: si-ku-la chochote = I didn't eat anything.

en.text: Anything you need, just let me know.

sw.note: chochote u-na-cho-hitaji = anything you need: -cho- agrees too.

en.text: Ask me any question.

sw.note: swali lolote: JI-MA takes l-olote.

en.text: Anything can happen on the road.

sw.note: lolote = anything at all (jambo lolote), with li- on the verb.

en.text: I can work from anywhere with my laptop.

sw.text: Naweza kufanya kazi popote nikiwa na kompyuta yangu.
sw.note: popote = anywhere: pa- for places.

en.text: Sit anywhere, you're welcome.

sw.note: popote = anywhere at all.

en.text: Call me any time.

sw.note: wakati wowote = any time: wakati takes w-owote.

en.text: Anyone who wants to help is welcome.

sw.note: watu wowote = any people: plural people take w-owote.

en.text: Do you have any news from home?

sw.note: habari zozote = any news: an N plural takes z-ozote.

en.text: I don't have any money on me right now.

sw.note: pesa zozote: pesa takes z-, so zozote.

en.text: Either way, we'll finish on Friday.

sw.note: vyovyote vile = either way, whatever happens.

en.text: Any tools will do.

sw.note: vifaa vyovyote vi-ta-faa: VI all the way through.

en.text: No problem at all.

sw.note: shida yoyote: shida is an N singular, so y-oyote.

en.text: I'll drink any water, I'm very thirsty.

sw.text: Nitakunywa maji yoyote, nina kiu sana.
sw.note: maji yoyote: MA takes y-oyote.

en.text: I've looked, but I can't find my keys anywhere.

sw.text: Nimetafuta, lakini sioni funguo zangu kokote.
sw.note: kokote = anywhere around: ku- for places in general.

en.text: Is anyone home?

sw.note: yeyote on its own = anyone (a person).

en.text: Wherever you go on the coast, you'll see coconut trees.

sw.note: popote u-ta-ka-po-kwenda = wherever you go.

en.text: Every morning I sit for forty minutes.

sw.text: Kila asubuhi nakaa kwa dakika arobaini.
sw.note: kila asubuhi = every morning: kila comes first and never changes.

en.text: Everyone at the gym knows me now.

sw.note: kila mtu = everyone: the verb stays singular (a-na-ni-jua).

en.text: Every time I come here, it's full.

sw.note: kila ni-ki-ja = every time I come: kila with -ki-.

en.text: Each fundi gets one thousand a day.

sw.text: Kila fundi anapata elfu moja kwa siku.
sw.note: kila fundi a-na-: kila keeps the noun and the verb singular.

en.text: I check everything twice.

sw.note: kila kitu = everything.

en.text: Some guy called me but didn't say his name.

sw.text: Mtu fulani alinipigia lakini hakusema jina lake.
sw.note: mtu fulani = a certain person, someone.

en.text: There's a certain place in Watamu where the fish is very good.

sw.text: Kuna mahali fulani Watamu ambapo samaki ni wazuri sana.
sw.note: mahali fulani = a certain place: fulani never changes.

en.text: Some day I'll take you to Jamaica.

sw.note: siku fulani = some day.

en.text: So-and-so said the price has gone up.

sw.note: fulani on its own = so-and-so.

en.text: Some of my friends live in Nairobi.

sw.text: Baadhi ya rafiki zangu wanaishi Nairobi.
sw.note: baadhi ya = some of; the verb agrees with the friends (wa-).

en.text: Some of the walls are already finished.

sw.note: baadhi ya kuta zi-me-sha-: the verb agrees with kuta.

en.text: Some people don't like the heat.

sw.note: baadhi ya watu ha-wa-pend-i = some people don't like.

en.text: I've watched some of the videos, not all of them.

sw.text: Nimeangalia baadhi ya video, si zote.
sw.note: baadhi ya video … si zote: zote agrees with video.

en.text: Another day, maybe tomorrow.

sw.note: siku nyingine: an N noun takes ny-ingine.

en.text: Give me another one, this one is broken.

sw.note: nyingine … hii: both agree with the N noun (a bottle, say).

en.text: Some people say the coast is too hot.

sw.text: Wengine wanasema pwani kuna joto sana.
sw.note: wengine = some (people), others.

en.text: Let's go to another beach today.

sw.note: ufuo mwingine: U nouns take mw-ingine.

en.text: I have other plans this weekend.

sw.note: mipango mingine: an M-MI plural takes m-ingine.

en.text: Every single day, same time, same posture.

sw.text: Kila siku, saa ileile, mkao uleule.
sw.note: kila siku = every day; ileile, uleule = the very same.

en.text: The other builders will come later.

sw.note: mafundi wengine: people take w-engine.

en.text: When I finish the video, I'll come to the beach.

sw.note: ni-ki-maliza = when I finish: -ki- after the person.

en.text: If you get a chance, let's go to the gym together.

sw.note: u-ki-pata = if you get: the same -ki- means if.

en.text: When the fundi comes, tell him to wait for me.

sw.note: a-ki-ja = when he comes: kuja drops its ku- after -ki-.

en.text: When we finish building, we'll throw a party.

sw.note: tu-ki-maliza = when we finish.

en.text: If you all want, we can go to Watamu on Sunday.

sw.note: m-ki-taka = if you (all) want.

en.text: When they leave, lock the gate.

sw.note: wa-ki-ondoka = when they leave.

en.text: If it rains, I won't ride the motorbike.

sw.note: i-ki-nyesha = if it rains: mvua takes i-, then -ki-.

en.text: When my phone rings, tell me.

sw.note: i-ki-lia = when it rings: simu takes i-.

en.text: When the money comes in, I'll pay you.

sw.note: zi-ki-ingia = when it comes in: pesa takes zi-.

en.text: If the food runs out, we'll cook more.

sw.note: ki-ki-isha = if it runs out: chakula's ki-, then -ki- for if.

en.text: When the car is ready, let me know.

sw.note: li-ki-wa = when it is: gari takes li-.

en.text: I found her cooking when I arrived.

sw.note: a-ki-pika = cooking: after a past verb, -ki- means while.

en.text: I was meditating when you called.

sw.note: ni-li-kuwa ni-ki-tafakari = I was meditating: -ki- for the ongoing part.

en.text: I saw him riding on the beach road.

sw.text: Nilimwona akiendesha kwenye barabara ya ufukweni.
sw.note: a-ki-endesha = riding, as I saw him.

en.text: If you don't come, it's all good.

sw.note: u-si-po-kuja = if you don't come: -sipo- is the if-not of -ki-.

en.text: If I don't pay today, the builders won't come tomorrow.

sw.note: ni-si-po-lipa = if I don't pay; ha-wa-ta-kuja = they won't come.

en.text: When I'm tired, I go to bed early.

sw.note: ni-ki-choka = when I'm tired; hu-lala = I sleep, as a habit.

en.text: When you're in Malindi, call me.

sw.note: u-ki-wa = when you are: kuwa drops its ku- after -ki-.

en.text: God willing, we'll get married.

sw.note: a-ki-penda = if he wills: Mungu akipenda = God willing.

en.text: When the sun comes up, I'll be sitting on the beach.

sw.note: li-ki-chomoza = when it rises: jua takes li-.

en.text: This message was written by my teacher.

sw.text: Ujumbe huu uliandikwa na mwalimu wangu.
sw.note: u-li-andik-w-a na = it was written by: -w- after a consonant.

en.text: The chapatis are being cooked right now, wait a little.

sw.text: Chapati zinapikwa sasa hivi, subiri kidogo.
sw.note: zi-na-pik-w-a = they are being cooked: pika → pikwa.

en.text: I got paid for the video yesterday.

sw.note: ni-li-lip-w-a = I was paid: lipa → lipwa.

en.text: The house will be painted after the rains.

sw.text: Nyumba itapakwa rangi baada ya mvua.
sw.note: i-ta-pak-w-a = it will be painted: paka → pakwa.

en.text: I'm loved by my fiancée.

sw.note: na-pend-w-a = I am loved: penda → pendwa.

en.text: The food was eaten before I arrived.

sw.note: ki-li-l-iw-a = it was eaten: la → liwa, her -iw- rule.

en.text: We were given mango seedlings by the elders.

sw.text: Tuligawiwa miche ya miembe na wazee.
sw.note: tu-li-gaw-iw-a = we were given a share: gawa → gawiwa, her -iw- rule.

en.text: Kenya was ruled by the British for many years.

sw.text: Kenya ilitawaliwa na Waingereza kwa miaka mingi.
sw.note: i-li-tawal-iw-a = it was ruled: tawala → tawaliwa.

en.text: The builders were given two mangoes each.

sw.text: Mafundi waligawiwa maembe mawili kila mmoja.
sw.note: wa-li-gaw-iw-a = they were handed out a share: gawa → gawiwa.

en.text: This fish should be eaten today.

sw.note: ku-l-iw-a = to be eaten: kula → kuliwa.

en.text: These shoes have only been worn once.

sw.text: Viatu hivi vimevaliwa mara moja tu.
sw.note: vi-me-va-liw-a = they have been worn: vaa → valiwa, her -liw- rule.

en.text: The watermelon was bought at the market.

sw.note: li-li-nunu-liw-a = it was bought: nunua → nunuliwa.

en.text: The food has been prepared, come and let's eat.

sw.note: ki-me-anda-liw-a = it has been prepared: andaa → andaliwa.

en.text: I was chosen to speak at the wedding.

sw.note: ni-li-chagu-liw-a = I was chosen: chagua → chaguliwa.

en.text: The gate is opened at six in the morning.

sw.text: Geti hufunguliwa saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: hu-fungu-liw-a = it is opened, as a rule: fungua → funguliwa.

en.text: I was raised in Canada.

sw.note: ni-li-le-lew-a = I was raised: lea → lelewa, her -lew- rule.

en.text: My friend got married last year.

sw.note: a-li-o-lew-a = she got married: oa → olewa, said of the woman.

en.text: The money was taken out of my account.

sw.note: zi-li-to-lew-a = it was taken out: toa → tolewa.

en.text: I was met at the airport by my fiancée.

sw.text: Nilipokelewa uwanja wa ndege na mchumba wangu.
sw.note: ni-li-poke-lew-a = I was received: pokea → pokelewa.

en.text: Two fishermen were rescued last night.

sw.note: wa-li-oko-lew-a = they were rescued: okoa → okolewa.

en.text: Are you up already? Let's go to the gym.

sw.note: u-me-sha-amka = have you already woken up? -sha- adds already.

en.text: I didn't wake up early today, I went to bed at twelve.

sw.text: Sikuamka mapema leo, nililala saa sita usiku.
sw.note: si-ku-amka = I didn't wake up; saa sita usiku = twelve at night on the Swahili clock.

en.text: We woke up to heavy rain here in Malindi today.

sw.text: Leo tumeamkia mvua kubwa hapa Malindi.
sw.note: amk-i-a = wake up to: the -i- ending adds to or for.

en.text: I haven't gone to bed yet, I'm uploading a video right now.

sw.text: Bado sijalala, napakia video sasa hivi.
sw.note: si-ja-lala = I haven't slept yet: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: Don't sleep without the net, there are lots of mosquitoes here.

sw.text: Usilale bila chandarua, kuna mbu wengi hapa.
sw.note: u-si-lal-e = don't sleep: -si- and the -e ending. Mbu takes wengi, like people do.

en.text: If I sleep during the day, I can't get to sleep at night.

sw.note: ni-ki-lala = if I sleep; si-pat-i usingizi = I can't get to sleep (I don't get sleep).

en.text: The power went off in the night, and the heat woke me up.

sw.note: li-ka-ni-amsha = and it woke me: -ka- is the next event, -ni- is me. Joto takes li-.

en.text: I was woken up by the neighbour's rooster at three in the morning.

sw.text: Niliamshwa na jogoo wa jirani saa tisa usiku.
sw.note: ni-li-amsh-w-a = I was woken: passive -w-, the doer after na. Saa tisa usiku = three a.m.

en.text: Don't worry, I'll wake you up when I get up.

sw.note: amka = wake up; amsha = wake someone up. ni-ta-ku-amsha = I will wake you.

en.text: When I get up, I make the bed first.

sw.note: kutandika kitanda = to make the bed; na-tandika = I make it.

en.text: I've made the bed for you, sleep well.

sw.note: ni-me-ku-tandik-i-a = I have made it for you: -ku- you, -i- for.

en.text: The bed hasn't been made yet, give me five minutes.

sw.text: Kitanda hakijatandikwa bado, nipe dakika tano.
sw.note: ha-ki-ja-tandik-w-a = it hasn't been made yet: kitanda takes ki-, passive -w-.

en.text: I want to go for a dip in the ocean this evening.

sw.text: Nataka kwenda kuoga baharini leo jioni.
sw.note: kuoga baharini = to bathe in the sea: on the coast, a dip in the ocean.

en.text: Let me shower real quick, then let's head out.

sw.note: ngoja ni-og-e = let me shower: after ngoja the verb takes -e.

en.text: There's no water to shower with today, the tank is empty.

sw.text: Hakuna maji ya kuogea leo, tanki ni tupu.
sw.note: ku-og-e-a = to shower with: the -e- ending adds with or for.

en.text: I've only washed my face, I haven't showered yet.

sw.note: kunawa = to wash the face or hands; kuoga = to wash the whole body.

en.text: Is there soap for washing hands here?

sw.text: Kuna sabuni ya kunawia mikono hapa?
alt: Kuna sabuni ya kunawa mikono hapa?
sw.note: ku-naw-i-a = to wash with: sabuni ya kunawia = soap to wash with.

en.text: When you finish the lime work, wash your hands before you eat.

sw.text: Mkimaliza kazi ya chokaa, naweni mikono kabla ya kula.
sw.note: naw-eni = wash, all of you: -eni speaks to many; m-ki-maliza = when you all finish.

en.text: I'm completely worn out, I carried bags of lime all day.

sw.text: Nimechoka kabisa, nilibeba mifuko ya chokaa siku nzima.
sw.note: ni-me-choka = I'm tired: the -me- form says the state you are in now.

en.text: I'm not tired yet, let's do one more set.

sw.text: Sijachoka bado, tufanye seti moja tena.
sw.note: si-ja-choka = I'm not tired yet: Kiswahili says I haven't got tired yet.

en.text: If you get tired, tell me so we can rest.

sw.note: u-ki-choka = if you get tired; tu-pumzik-e = so that we rest.

en.text: All right, so on Sunday I'm going to rest, I won't do any work.

sw.text: Haya, basi Jumapili nitapumzika, sitafanya kazi yoyote.
sw.note: ni-ta-pumzika = I will rest; si-ta-fanya = I won't do.

en.text: Let's rest for ten minutes, then carry on.

sw.text: Tupumzike kwa dakika kumi, halafu tuendelee.
sw.note: tu-pumzik-e = let's rest: tu- plus the -e ending.

en.text: The builders need shade to rest in at midday.

sw.text: Mafundi wanahitaji kivuli cha kupumzikia mchana.
sw.note: ku-pumzik-i-a = to rest in: kivuli cha kupumzikia = shade to rest in.

en.text: What should I wear to my friend's wedding?

sw.text: Nivae nini kwenye harusi ya rafiki yangu?
sw.note: ni-va-e = should I wear? A question in the -e form asks what to do.

en.text: I'm not going to wear a suit, it's too hot here on the coast.

sw.text: Sitavaa suti, kuna joto sana hapa pwani.
sw.note: si-ta-vaa = I won't wear: si- with -ta- is the negative future.

en.text: Don't wash this shirt, it's only been worn once.

sw.text: Usilifue shati hili, limevaliwa mara moja tu.
sw.note: li-me-va-liw-a = it has been worn: her -liw- rule. Shati takes li-, so u-si-li-fu-e = don't wash it.

en.text: I want to learn to fish in the ocean.

sw.note: kuvua samaki = to fish; kuvua viatu = to take off shoes: one verb, two meanings.

en.text: Please take your shoes off here, the floor's just been cleaned.

sw.text: Tafadhali vua viatu hapa, sakafu imesafishwa sasa hivi.
sw.note: vua = take off: a command is the bare verb; i-me-safish-w-a = it has been cleaned.

en.text: Were these fish caught this morning?

sw.note: wa-me-vu-liw-a = they have been caught: her -liw- rule. Samaki takes wa-, like people.

en.text: We're getting ready for the wedding, there's a lot to do.

sw.text: Tunajiandaa kwa harusi, kuna mengi ya kufanya.
sw.note: tu-na-ji-andaa = we are getting ourselves ready: -ji- means self.

en.text: Get ready real quick, we're leaving in ten minutes.

sw.text: Jiandae haraka, tunaondoka baada ya dakika kumi.
sw.note: ji-anda-e = get yourself ready: a -ji- verb's command ends in -e.

en.text: I'm not ready yet, wait for me a bit.

sw.note: si-ja-ji-andaa = I'm not ready yet: I haven't got myself ready.

en.text: A button's come off, can you sew it on for me?

sw.note: ku-ni-shon-e-a = to sew for me: -ni- me, -e- for.

en.text: My wedding suit is being made by a tailor in Malindi.

sw.text: Suti yangu ya harusi inashonwa na fundi wa Malindi.
sw.note: i-na-shon-w-a = it is being sewn: suti takes i-, passive -w-.

en.text: I sewed on the button myself yesterday.

sw.note: ni-li-shona = I sewed; mwenyewe = by myself.

en.text: She's combing her hair, she'll be ready in five minutes.

sw.text: Anachana nywele, atakuwa tayari baada ya dakika tano.
sw.note: a-na-chana nywele = she's combing her hair; a-ta-kuwa = she will be.

en.text: I haven't combed my hair, I've only just woken up.

sw.note: si-ja-chana = I haven't combed yet; ni-me-amka sasa hivi = I've only just woken up.

en.text: My fiancée combed my hair for me before the photos.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu alinichania nywele kabla ya picha.
sw.note: a-li-ni-chan-i-a = she combed for me: -ni- me, -i- for.

en.text: I got a haircut yesterday, what do you think?

sw.note: ni-li-nyo-lew-a = I was shaved, I got a haircut: her -lew- rule for o verbs.

en.text: Just trim it a little for me, don't shave it all off.

sw.note: u-si-nyo-e = don't shave: -si- and the -e ending. Zote agrees with nywele (hair).

en.text: If I shave every day, my skin itches.

sw.note: ni-ki-nyoa = if I shave; i-na-ni-washa = it itches me: -ni- me.

en.text: You look really nice today, where are you going?

sw.note: u-me-pendeza = you look nice: Kiswahili says you have become pleasing.

en.text: This colour doesn't look good, let's choose another one.

sw.note: ha-i-pendez-i = it doesn't look good: rangi takes i-, the negative ends in -i.

en.text: Our house will look beautiful when we coat it with white lime.

sw.text: Nyumba yetu itapendeza tukiipaka chokaa nyeupe.
sw.note: tu-ki-i-paka = when we coat it: the -i- after -ki- stands for nyumba.

en.text: These shoes don't fit me, they're too small.

sw.text: Viatu hivi havinifai, ni vidogo sana.
sw.note: ha-vi-ni-fa-i = they don't fit me: viatu takes vi-, -ni- me.

en.text: This dress really suits you, buy it.

sw.note: li-na-ku-faa = it suits you; li-nunu-e = buy it: gauni takes li-.

en.text: It would be better if we left early, the sun will be strong at midday.

sw.text: Ingefaa tuondoke mapema, jua litakuwa kali mchana.
sw.note: i-nge-faa = it would be right: -nge- makes would; tu-ondok-e = that we leave.

en.text: I'm going to clean the house before my fiancée gets here.

sw.text: Nitasafisha nyumba kabla mchumba wangu hajafika.
sw.note: ni-ta-safisha = I will clean; kabla ha-ja-fika = before she arrives: kabla takes the not-yet form.

en.text: The builders cleared the plot yesterday, today we're starting to build.

sw.text: Mafundi walisafisha kiwanja jana, leo tunaanza kujenga.
sw.note: wa-li-safisha = they cleaned: kusafisha kiwanja = to clear a plot.

en.text: Can you clean my motorbike for me? I'll pay you two hundred.

sw.text: Unaweza kunisafishia pikipiki? Nitakulipa mia mbili.
sw.note: ku-ni-safish-i-a = to clean for me: -ni- me, -i- for.

en.text: Let me sweep real quick, there's sand everywhere.

sw.text: Ngoja nifagie haraka, kuna mchanga kila mahali.
sw.note: ngoja ni-fagi-e = let me sweep: after ngoja the verb ends in -e.

en.text: I sweep the yard every morning before I meditate.

sw.text: Nafagia uwanja kila asubuhi kabla ya kutafakari.
sw.note: na-fagia = I sweep, short for ninafagia; kabla ya ku-tafakari = before meditating.

en.text: Don't step there, I haven't finished sweeping.

sw.note: si-ja-maliza ku-fagia = I haven't finished sweeping yet; u-si-kanyag-e = don't step.

en.text: I'm going to wash my gym clothes today, they're really dirty.

sw.text: Nitafua nguo zangu za jimu leo, zimechafuka sana.
sw.note: kufua = to wash clothes, not dishes; ni-ta-fua = I will wash them.

en.text: There's a lady who washes my clothes for me every Saturday.

sw.text: Kuna mama anayenifulia nguo kila Jumamosi.
sw.note: a-na-ye-ni-fu-li-a = who washes for me: -ye- is who, -ni- me, -lia for.

en.text: If it rains, I won't do the washing today.

sw.note: i-ki-nyesha = if it rains; si-ta-fua = I won't wash.

en.text: Hang the clothes in the sun, they'll dry quickly.

sw.note: anika = hang out to dry: a command is the bare verb; zi-ta-kauka = they will dry.

en.text: The clothes are out on the line, and the rain's coming!

sw.text: Nguo zimeanikwa nje, na mvua inakuja!
sw.note: zi-me-anik-w-a = they have been hung out: nguo takes zi-, passive -w-.

en.text: I didn't hang the clothes out yesterday, now they smell.

sw.note: si-ku-anika = I didn't hang them out: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: When I finish meditating, I roll up my mat.

sw.note: kukunja = to fold or roll up; ni-ki-maliza = when I finish.

en.text: Fold this shirt for me, I'll put it in the bag.

sw.text: Nikunjie shati hili, nitaliweka kwenye begi.
sw.note: ni-kunj-i-e = fold it for me; ni-ta-li-weka = I will put it: li- stands for shati.

en.text: I've folded all the clothes, only the sheets are left.

sw.text: Nimekunja nguo zote, zimebaki shuka tu.
sw.note: ni-me-kunja = I have folded; zi-me-baki = they are left over.

en.text: I want to wash the motorbike, it's covered in mud.

sw.note: nataka ku-osha = I want to wash; i-me-jaa = it is full: pikipiki takes i-.

en.text: No worries, I'll wash the dishes, you rest.

sw.text: Hakuna shida, nitaosha vyombo, wewe pumzika.
sw.note: ni-ta-osha = I will wash; pumzika = rest: a command is the bare verb.

en.text: Wash these two cups for me, the guests have arrived.

sw.text: Nioshee vikombe hivi viwili, wageni wamefika.
sw.note: ni-osh-e-e = wash them for me: -e- for, the last -e asks. Vikombe takes hivi viwili.

en.text: Where did you put my charger?

sw.note: u-li-weka = you put: -li- marks the past.

en.text: Save some food for me, I'll be back at eight tonight.

sw.text: Niwekee chakula, nitarudi saa mbili usiku.
sw.note: ni-wek-e-e = keep it for me: -e- for, the last -e asks. Saa mbili usiku = eight p.m.

en.text: The bags of lime have been put in the store so they don't get rained on.

sw.text: Mifuko ya chokaa imewekwa stoo ili isinyeshewe.
sw.note: i-me-wek-w-a = they have been put: mifuko takes i-; i-si-nyeshew-e = so they don't get rained on.

en.text: Don't throw those bottles away, I'll use them for the plants.

sw.text: Usitupe chupa hizo, nitazitumia kwa mimea.
sw.note: u-si-tup-e = don't throw away; ni-ta-zi-tumia = I will use them: zi- stands for chupa.

en.text: Where does the rubbish get thrown around here?

sw.note: hu-tup-w-a = it gets thrown, as a rule: hu- habit, -w- passive.

en.text: Throw me the keys, I'm at the gate.

sw.note: ni-tup-i-e = throw them to me: -i- to, -ni- me, -e asks.

en.text: I want to learn to cook coconut rice.

sw.text: Nataka kujifunza kupika wali wa nazi.
sw.note: nataka ku-jifunza ku-pika = I want to learn to cook; wali wa nazi = coconut rice.

en.text: All right, so today I'm going to cook dinner for my fiancée.

sw.text: Haya, basi leo nitampikia mchumba wangu chakula cha jioni.
sw.note: ni-ta-m-pik-i-a = I will cook for her: -m- her, -i- for.

en.text: This fish has been cooked in coconut, it's really tasty.

sw.text: Samaki huyu amepikwa kwa nazi, ni mtamu sana.
sw.note: a-me-pik-w-a = it has been cooked: samaki takes a- and huyu, like a person.

en.text: I was cutting a mango and I cut my finger.

sw.note: ni-li-kuwa na-kata = I was cutting; ni-ka-ji-kata = and I cut myself: -ji- is self.

en.text: Cut this pineapple into small pieces for me.

sw.note: ni-kat-i-e = cut it for me: -i- for, -e asks. Vipande takes vidogo.

en.text: This knife doesn't cut, it's gone blunt.

sw.note: ha-ki-kat-i = it doesn't cut: kisu takes ki-, the negative ends in -i.

en.text: I'll fry the fish in just a little oil.

sw.text: Nitakaanga samaki kwa mafuta kidogo tu.
sw.note: ni-ta-kaanga = I will fry; kwa mafuta = with oil.

en.text: These days I don't eat fried food.

sw.text: Siku hizi sili vyakula vya kukaanga.
sw.note: vyakula vya ku-kaanga = fried foods; si-l-i = I don't eat: kula drops ku- in the negative.

en.text: Fry two eggs for me, please.

sw.note: ni-kaang-i-e = fry for me: -i- for, -e asks. Mayai takes mawili.

en.text: I'm boiling cassava, we'll eat it with tea.

sw.note: tu-ta-i-la = we will eat it: -i- stands for mihogo and takes the place of ku-.

en.text: Has this water been boiled? I want to drink it.

sw.note: ya-me-chemsh-w-a = it has been boiled: maji takes ya-; ku-ya-nywa = to drink it.

en.text: I didn't boil any water today, I'll buy bottled.

sw.text: Sikuchemsha maji leo, nitanunua ya chupa.
sw.note: si-ku-chemsha = I didn't boil; ya chupa = the bottled kind.

en.text: Have you eaten yet? I've brought you some fish.

sw.note: u-me-sha-kula = have you already eaten? One-syllable kula keeps ku- after -me-.

en.text: When I come back from the gym, I eat eggs and bananas.

sw.text: Nikitoka jimu, nakula mayai na ndizi.
sw.note: ni-ki-toka = when I come from; na-kula = I eat: kula keeps ku- after na-.

en.text: The whole cake's been eaten! You didn't even leave me a piece?

sw.text: Keki yote imeliwa! Hukuniachia hata kipande?
sw.note: i-me-liw-a = it has been eaten: kula becomes liwa; hu-ku-ni-achi-a = you didn't leave for me.

en.text: I've peeled the oranges, have some.

sw.note: ni-me-menya = I have peeled; chukua = take: a command is the bare verb.

en.text: Peel this mango for me, I don't know how to peel it properly.

sw.text: Nimenyee embe hili, sijui kulimenya vizuri.
sw.note: ni-meny-e-e = peel it for me; ku-li-menya = to peel it: li- stands for embe.

en.text: The pineapple's been peeled and cut, it's in the fridge.

sw.text: Nanasi limemenywa na kukatwa, liko kwenye friji.
sw.note: li-me-meny-w-a = it has been peeled: nanasi takes li-, passive -w-.

en.text: I've never tasted this fruit, what's it called?

sw.note: si-ja-wahi ku-onja = I have never tasted; li-na-it-w-a-je = how is it called?

en.text: Let me taste it first before adding salt.

sw.text: Ngoja nionje kwanza kabla ya kuongeza chumvi.
sw.note: ngoja ni-onj-e = let me taste: after ngoja the verb ends in -e.

en.text: If you taste this chilli, you'll cry!

sw.note: u-ki-onja = if you taste; u-ta-lia = you will cry.

en.text: My fiancée has made me tea and mahamri.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu ameniandalia chai na mahamri.
sw.note: a-me-ni-anda-li-a = she has prepared for me: -ni- me, -lia for.

en.text: The wedding food will be prepared by cooks from here in Malindi.

sw.text: Chakula cha harusi kitaandaliwa na wapishi wa hapa Malindi.
sw.note: ki-ta-anda-liw-a = it will be prepared: chakula takes ki-; her -liw- rule.

en.text: I haven't made anything, shall we go and eat at a restaurant today?

sw.text: Sijaandaa chochote, twende tukale hotelini leo?
sw.note: si-ja-andaa = I haven't prepared; tu-ka-l-e = and let's eat: kula drops ku- in the -e form.

en.text: I'm really thirsty, I want to drink cold water.

sw.text: Nina kiu sana, nataka kunywa maji baridi.
sw.note: nina kiu = I'm thirsty (I have thirst); nataka ku-nywa = I want to drink.

en.text: I drink three litres of water every day because of the heat.

sw.text: Nakunywa lita tatu za maji kila siku kwa sababu ya joto.
alt: Ninakunywa lita tatu za maji kila siku kwa sababu ya joto.
sw.note: na-kunywa = I drink: a one-syllable verb keeps ku- in the present.

en.text: We drank two coconuts at the beach yesterday.

sw.note: tu-li-kunywa = we drank; dafu is a young coconut, madafu two or more.

en.text: I'm completely full, I can't eat any more.

sw.note: ni-me-shiba = I'm full: Kiswahili says I have become full.

en.text: Fill up the tank for me, please.

sw.note: ni-jaz-i-e = fill it for me: -i- means for, and the -e ending asks.

en.text: I've spilled coffee on my laptop!

sw.note: ni-me-mwaga = I've spilled: kumwaga is to pour out or to spill.

en.text: I didn't order this, I ordered mango juice.

sw.text: Sikuagiza hii, niliagiza juisi ya embe.
sw.note: si-ku-agiza = I didn't order: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: I've taken two tablets, but my head still hurts.

sw.text: Nimemeza vidonge viwili, lakini kichwa bado kinauma.
sw.note: kumeza vidonge = to take tablets: in Kiswahili you swallow them.

en.text: Let my body cool down first, then I'll shower.

sw.text: Ngoja mwili upoe kwanza, halafu nitaoga.
sw.note: ngoja mwili u-po-e = let the body cool down: mwili takes u-, and ngoja takes the -e form.

en.text: If I drink coffee at night, I don't sleep.

sw.note: ni-ki-nywa = if I drink: kunywa drops ku- after -ki-; si-lal-i = I don't sleep.

en.text: I'm not full yet, add a bit more rice for me.

sw.note: si-ja-shiba = I'm not full yet: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: Eat something, you won't get full on tea alone.

sw.text: Kula kitu, hutashiba kwa chai tu.
sw.note: kula = eat (the command); hu-ta-shiba = you won't get full: hu- is you-not, -ta- the future.

en.text: Guys, don't spill water on the floor, someone will fall.

sw.note: m-si-mwag-e = don't spill, all of you: m- speaks to many.

en.text: Shall I fill your bottle for you?

sw.note: ni-ku-jaz-i-e = shall I fill it for you? The -e form offers; -ku- you, -i- for.

en.text: All right, I'll order tea and mandazi for the fundis.

sw.text: Haya, nitawaagizia mafundi chai na maandazi.
sw.note: ni-ta-wa-agiz-i-a = I'll order for them: -wa- them, -i- for.

en.text: My tea's gone cold, but it's all good, I'll drink it like that.

sw.text: Chai yangu imepoa, lakini ni sawa tu, nitainywa hivyo hivyo.
sw.note: ni-ta-i-nywa = I'll drink it: the object -i- (for chai) takes the place of ku-.

en.text: If I swallow a tablet without water, it gets stuck in my throat.

sw.text: Nikimeza kidonge bila maji, kinakwama kooni.
sw.note: ni-ki-meza = if I swallow; ki-na-kwama = it gets stuck: kidonge takes ki-.

en.text: I don't spit out watermelon seeds, I just swallow them.

sw.text: Mimi sitemi mbegu za tikiti, nazimeza tu.
sw.note: si-tem-i = I don't spit: the negative ends in -i; na-zi-meza = I swallow them.

en.text: The waiter spilled soda on my shirt.

sw.note: a-li-ni-mwag-i-a = spilled on me: -ni- me, -i- on.

en.text: When the laptop cools down, I'll upload the video.

sw.note: i-ki-poa = when it cools down: kompyuta takes i-.

en.text: The doctor told me to drink a lot of water.

sw.note: a-li-ni-agiza = told me to; ni-nyw-e = that I drink: the -e form follows.

en.text: Don't spit it out, just swallow it, it's good medicine.

sw.text: Usiiteme, imeze tu, ni dawa nzuri.
sw.note: u-si-i-tem-e = don't spit it out; i-mez-e = swallow it: -i- stands for dawa.

en.text: Have the water drums been filled yet?

sw.note: ya-mesha-jaz-w-a = they've already been filled: mapipa takes ya-, passive -w-.

en.text: Are these tablets taken before or after eating?

sw.text: Vidonge hivi vinamezwa kabla au baada ya kula?
sw.note: vi-na-mez-w-a = they are swallowed: passive -w-; vidonge takes vi-.

en.text: I'm going to buy a watermelon for a hundred shillings.

sw.text: Nitanunua tikiti maji kwa shilingi mia moja.
sw.note: ni-ta-nunua = I will buy.

en.text: He went to buy mangoes for them.

sw.note: Her sentence: ku-wa-nunul-i-a = to buy for them; alienda is common in Kenya (textbook: alikwenda).

en.text: I'll buy you a young coconut real quick.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-nunul-i-a = I will buy for you.

en.text: These mangoes were bought this morning.

sw.note: ya-li-nunu-liw-a = they were bought: her -liw- rule; maembe takes ya-.

en.text: Are you selling peanuts today?

sw.note: u-na-uza = you are selling.

en.text: Sell me three for two hundred.

sw.note: ni-uz-i-e = sell to me: -i- for, -e asks.

en.text: The plot next to mine has been sold.

sw.text: Kiwanja kilicho karibu na changu kimeuzwa.
sw.note: ki-me-uz-w-a = it has been sold: kiwanja takes ki-.

en.text: Let me choose the ripe tomatoes myself.

sw.note: ngoja ni-chagu-e = let me choose; zi-li-zo-iva = the ones that are ripe.

en.text: I don't want to choose, you pick for me.

sw.note: ni-chagul-i-e = choose for me: -l- joins the vowels.

en.text: My friend has been chosen to lead the choir.

sw.note: a-me-chagu-liw-a = has been chosen: her -liw- rule.

en.text: Can you weigh these for me?

sw.note: ku-ni-pim-i-a = to weigh for me.

en.text: Measure the room before we buy the carpet.

sw.note: pima = measure; kabla ha-tu-ja-nunua = before we buy (the not-yet form).

en.text: The plot was measured last week.

sw.note: ki-li-pim-w-a = it was measured.

en.text: Bring it down a bit for me, it's for my fiancée.

sw.text: Nipunguzie kidogo, ni ya mchumba wangu.
sw.note: ni-punguz-i-e = lower it for me.

en.text: If you lower the price, I'll take two.

sw.note: u-ki-punguza = if you lower.

en.text: The price hasn't been lowered, it's still two hundred and fifty.

sw.text: Bei haijapunguzwa, bado ni mia mbili na hamsini.
sw.note: ha-i-ja-punguz-w-a = it hasn't been lowered yet.

en.text: Add one more, please.

sw.note: ongeza = add: the bare verb is a command.

en.text: The seller has added one more for me.

sw.note: a-me-ni-ongez-e-a = he has added for me.

en.text: Prices have gone up this month.

sw.note: zi-me-ongez-ek-a = they have gone up: -ek- happens by itself.

en.text: I'll carry the bags, you carry the water.

sw.note: ni-ta-beba = I will carry; u-beb-e = you carry (subjunctive).

en.text: Can you carry this for me to the motorbike?

sw.text: Unaweza kunibebea hiki mpaka kwenye pikipiki?
sw.note: ku-ni-beb-e-a = to carry for me: -e- after e.

en.text: If I carry all this, my back will hurt.

sw.note: ni-ki-beba = if I carry; u-ta-ni-uma = it will hurt me.

en.text: Count the change before you go.

sw.note: hesabu = count: a loan's command is the bare verb.

en.text: I didn't count the money, I trust you.

sw.note: si-ku-hesabu = I didn't count; na-ku-amini = I trust you.

en.text: I want to pay with M-Pesa, is that okay?

sw.text: Nataka kulipa kwa M-Pesa, ni sawa?
sw.note: nataka ku-lipa = I want to pay; ni sawa? = is that okay?

en.text: All right, I've paid all the fundis today.

sw.note: ni-me-wa-lipa = I've paid them: -wa- them sits right before the root.

en.text: Don't worry, I'll pay the fare for you.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-lip-i-a = I'll pay for you: -ku- you, -i- for.

en.text: I've already sent you the money, now how much is this?

sw.text: Nimeshakutumia pesa, sasa hii ni bei gani?
sw.note: ni-mesha-ku-tumia = I've already sent you: kutumia is kutuma with -i-, send to.

en.text: I sent money to the wrong number, what should I do?

sw.text: Nilituma pesa kwa namba isiyo sahihi, nifanye nini?
sw.note: ni-li-tuma = I sent; ni-fany-e nini? = what should I do? The -e form asks.

en.text: I'll send the fundi the money for the lime this evening.

sw.text: Nitamtumia fundi pesa za chokaa leo jioni.
sw.note: ni-ta-m-tumia = I'll send him: -m- him, and kutumia means send to.

en.text: I haven't received the money yet, which number have you sent it to?

sw.text: Sijapokea pesa bado, umetuma kwa namba gani?
sw.note: si-ja-pokea = I haven't received yet: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: When you receive the money, let me know.

sw.note: u-ki-pokea = when you receive; ni-julish-e = let me know (inform me).

en.text: Receive my parcel for me, I'm on my way.

sw.note: ni-pokel-e-e = receive it for me: kupokea takes -le- before the -e- that means for.

en.text: I'll withdraw money at the agent before going to the market.

sw.text: Nitatoa pesa kwa wakala kabla ya kwenda sokoni.
sw.note: ni-ta-toa pesa = I'll take out money: kutoa also means to withdraw.

en.text: I didn't withdraw money yesterday, the agent didn't have enough cash.

sw.text: Sikutoa pesa jana, wakala hakuwa na pesa za kutosha.
sw.note: si-ku-toa = I didn't take out; ha-ku-wa na = he didn't have (he wasn't with).

en.text: How much should I withdraw for you?

sw.note: ni-ku-tol-e-e = should I take out for you? -ku- you, -le- joins, the -e asks.

en.text: I've kept back a little money to get through the month.

sw.text: Nimebakisha pesa kidogo za kumaliza mwezi.
sw.note: ni-me-bakisha = I've left some over: kubakisha is to make some remain.

en.text: Don't spend it all, keep a little back.

sw.note: u-si-zi-tumi-e = don't spend them: zi- stands for pesa; bakisha = leave some.

en.text: If I keep back five thousand every week, I'll have money for the wedding.

sw.text: Nikibakisha elfu tano kila wiki, nitakuwa na pesa za harusi.
sw.note: ni-ki-bakisha = if I keep back; ni-ta-kuwa na = I'll have (I will be with).

en.text: I keep money in M-Shwari, not in M-Pesa.

sw.text: Nahifadhi pesa kwenye M-Shwari, si kwenye M-Pesa.
sw.note: na-hifadhi = I keep, I save; M-Shwari is the savings side of M-Pesa.

en.text: Keep this money for me until Monday.

sw.note: ni-hifadhi-e = keep it for me: kuhifadhia is keep for, and the -e asks.

en.text: All the receipts have been saved on my phone.

sw.text: Risiti zote zimehifadhiwa kwenye simu yangu.
sw.note: zi-me-hifadh-iw-a = they have been kept: loan verbs take -iwa; risiti takes zi-.

en.text: I don't like borrowing money from friends.

sw.note: si-pend-i ku-kopa = I don't like to borrow; kukopa kwa = to borrow from.

en.text: I borrowed five thousand from a neighbour, I'll pay him back on Friday.

sw.text: Nilikopa elfu tano kwa jirani, nitamrudishia Ijumaa.
sw.note: ni-li-kopa = I borrowed; ni-ta-m-rudish-i-a = I'll give it back to him.

en.text: I don't want to borrow again, I want to build without debt.

sw.text: Sitaki kukopa tena, nataka kujenga bila deni.
sw.note: sitaki ku- = I don't want to; nataka ku- = I want to.

en.text: I lent the fundi three thousand last month.

sw.text: Nilimkopesha fundi elfu tatu mwezi uliopita.
sw.note: ni-li-m-kopesha = I lent him: kukopesha is to make someone borrow, to lend.

en.text: I won't lend to him again until he pays me.

sw.note: si-ta-m-kopesha = I won't lend him; mpaka a-ni-lip-e = until he pays me.

en.text: You owe me five hundred shillings, but no worries.

sw.text: Nakudai shilingi mia tano, lakini hakuna shida.
sw.note: na-ku-dai = I claim from you: Kiswahili says I claim you, English says you owe me.

en.text: I owe the mama mboga three hundred, I'll pay her tomorrow.

sw.text: Nadaiwa na mama mboga mia tatu, nitamlipa kesho.
sw.note: na-dai-w-a = I owe: the passive of kudai, I am claimed, means to owe.

en.text: I want to travel to Jamaica one day.

sw.note: nataka + ku-verb = I want to do it.

en.text: I don't want to travel at night.

sw.note: si-tak-i = I don't want: the negative ends in -i.

en.text: I'm going to travel to Nairobi on Friday.

sw.note: ni-ta-safiri = I-will-travel; kwenda here means to.

en.text: I'm on my way, I'll arrive in twenty minutes.

sw.text: Niko njiani, nitafika baada ya dakika ishirini.
sw.note: ni-ta-fika = I-will-arrive.

en.text: I've arrived, I'm at the gate.

sw.note: ni-me-fika = I have arrived: -me- is for what has just happened.

en.text: When I get to Nairobi, I'll send you a message.

sw.note: ni-ki-fika = when I arrive; ni-ta-ku-tumia = I-will-you-send.

en.text: Where have we got to now?

sw.note: fik-i-a = to reach: the -i- ending points at the place.

en.text: When I arrived, I was welcomed with food.

sw.note: ni-li-po-fika = when I arrived; karibish-w-a = be welcomed (passive -w-).

en.text: What time does the Mombasa bus leave?

sw.text: Basi la Mombasa linaondoka saa ngapi?
sw.note: basi is a JI-MA noun, so li-na-ondoka = it leaves.

en.text: The bus left at five in the morning.

sw.text: Basi liliondoka saa kumi na moja alfajiri.
sw.note: saa kumi na moja alfajiri = five a.m.: the Swahili clock starts at dawn.

en.text: We'll leave early so we don't get stuck in traffic.

sw.text: Tutaondoka mapema ili tusikwame kwenye foleni.
sw.note: tu-si-kwame = so we don't get stuck: the negative subjunctive after ili.

en.text: Let's go now, we're running late.

sw.note: twende = tu-ende: let's go (subjunctive).

en.text: I didn't go to the gym yesterday, I was tired.

sw.note: si-kw-enda = I didn't go; many people say sikuenda.

en.text: Come to Malindi, you'll really like it.

sw.note: njoo = come: the one irregular command of kuja.

en.text: My fiancée came from Mombasa yesterday.
