sw.text: Mchumba wangu alikuja jana kutoka Mombasa.
sw.note: a-li-kuja: one-syllable verbs keep ku- in the past.

en.text: I'll come and pick you up at eight.

sw.note: saa mbili = eight o'clock; ku-ku-chukua = to-you-pick up.

en.text: I didn't come back yesterday because the road was bad.

sw.text: Sikurudi jana kwa sababu barabara ilikuwa mbaya.
sw.note: si-ku-rudi = I didn't come back: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: I'll be back in two weeks.

sw.note: ni-ta-rudi = I will come back.

en.text: Sorry I'm late, the boda didn't come on time.

sw.text: Samahani nimechelewa, boda haikufika kwa wakati.
sw.note: ni-me-chelewa = I'm late: Kiswahili says I have become late.

en.text: Don't be late, the plane leaves at ten.

sw.note: u-si-chelewe = don't be late; saa nne = ten o'clock.

en.text: We were told the bus would be late.

sw.note: tu-li-ambi-w-a = we were told (passive -w-).

en.text: If we leave now, we'll make it on time.

sw.note: kuwahi = to be in time; tu-ki-ondoka = if we leave.

en.text: Have you ever been to Lamu?

sw.note: u-me-wahi + ku-verb = have you ever done it?

en.text: I've never flown in a small plane.

sw.note: si-ja-wahi = I have never: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: I want to take a boda to Watamu, how much is it?

sw.text: Nataka kupanda boda mpaka Watamu, ni shilingi ngapi?
sw.note: kupanda boda = to take a boda: kupanda is to get on, to board.

en.text: I ride my own motorbike, I don't take bodas much.

sw.text: Naendesha pikipiki yangu mwenyewe, sipandi boda sana.
sw.note: na-endesha = I ride, I drive; si-pand-i = I don't get on: the negative ends in -i.

en.text: Drop me off there at the corner, please.

sw.note: ni-shush-e = drop me off: kushusha is to let someone down, to drop off.

en.text: Stop for a bit, I want to buy water.

sw.note: simama = stop, stand: the bare verb is a command.

en.text: Don't cross now, a lorry's coming!

sw.note: u-si-vuk-e = don't cross; lori takes li-, so li-na-kuja = it is coming.

en.text: I'll get off there at the chemist.

sw.text: Nitashukia pale kwenye duka la dawa.
sw.note: ni-ta-shuk-i-a = I'll get off at: the -i- ending points at the place.

en.text: When you get on the back, hold on tight.

sw.note: u-ki-panda = when you get on; shika = hold on (a command).

en.text: I dropped my fiancée off at the market this morning.

sw.note: ni-li-m-shusha = I dropped her off: -m- her sits right before the root.

en.text: Get off on this side, the exhaust pipe is hot.

sw.text: Shuka upande huu, bomba la moshi lina joto.
sw.note: shuka = get off (a command); bomba la moshi = the exhaust pipe.

en.text: If you turn right, you'll see a big mosque.

sw.note: u-ki-geuka = if you turn; u-ta-ona = you will see.

en.text: We crossed the Kilifi bridge on the motorbike yesterday.

sw.text: Tulivuka daraja la Kilifi kwa pikipiki jana.
sw.note: tu-li-vuka = we crossed: kuvuka takes what you cross as its object, daraja.

en.text: The bike's suddenly stopped, I don't know what's wrong with it.

sw.text: Pikipiki imesimama ghafla, sijui ina shida gani.
sw.note: i-me-simama = it has stopped: pikipiki takes i-; si-ju-i = I don't know.

en.text: I won't ride at night again, the road is really dark.

sw.text: Sitaendesha usiku tena, barabara ina giza sana.
sw.note: si-ta-endesha = I won't ride: the -ta- of the future stays in the negative.

en.text: I'll stop by the market real quick on my way back.

sw.note: ni-ta-pit-i-a = I'll pass by: -i- points at the place; ni-ki-rudi = on my way back.

en.text: I haven't taken a matatu since last month, I use my motorbike.

sw.text: Sijapanda matatu tangu mwezi uliopita, natumia pikipiki yangu.
sw.note: si-ja-panda = I haven't got on: -ja- means not yet, not since.

en.text: I didn't get off at Malindi, I slept all the way to Mombasa!

sw.note: si-ku-shuka = I didn't get off: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: Let's turn round and go back, we've passed his house.

sw.note: tu-geuk-e tu-rud-i = let's turn and go back; tu-me-i-pita = we've passed it (-i- for nyumba).

en.text: Let's cross over there at the zebra crossing, it's safer.

sw.text: Tuvukie pale kwenye zebra, ni salama zaidi.
sw.note: tu-vuk-i-e = let's cross at: -i- points at the place, and the -e suggests.

en.text: We've missed the ferry, let's wait for the next one.

sw.note: tu-me-pit-w-a na = we've missed it: we were passed by it (passive -w-).

en.text: The police stopped me and checked my licence.

sw.note: wa-li-ni-simam-ish-a = they stopped me: -ish- makes someone else stop.

en.text: My arm hurts, can you ride the bike home for me?

sw.text: Mkono unaniuma, unaweza kuniendeshea pikipiki mpaka nyumbani?
sw.note: ku-ni-endesh-e-a = to ride for me: -ni- me, -e- for.

en.text: We were dropped off on the way because the bus broke down.

sw.text: Tulishushwa njiani kwa sababu basi liliharibika.
sw.note: tu-li-shush-w-a = we were dropped off: passive -w-; basi takes li-.

en.text: When I turned left, I saw a cow in the middle of the road.

sw.text: Nilipogeuka kushoto, nikaona ng'ombe katikati ya barabara.
sw.note: ni-li-po-geuka = when I turned; ni-ka-ona = and then I saw.

en.text: If you pass through Malindi, give me a call.

sw.note: u-ki-pita = if you pass; ni-pig-i-e simu = call me: -i- for, and the -e asks.

en.text: I want to take you to Watamu on Saturday.

sw.note: ku-ku-peleka = to take you: the second ku- means you.

en.text: Please take the builders some tea, it's ten o'clock.

sw.text: Tafadhali wapelekee mafundi chai, ni saa nne.
sw.note: wa-pelek-e-e = take to them: -e- means to, and the last -e asks.

en.text: I won't take the motorbike to that mechanic again, he made it worse.

sw.text: Sitaipeleka pikipiki kwa fundi yule tena, aliiharibu zaidi.
sw.note: si-ta-i-peleka = I won't take it: -i- stands for pikipiki.

en.text: Bring the sand over here, the fundi is waiting.

sw.note: leteni = bring, all of you: -eni turns a command to a group.

en.text: I'm bringing you some cold water right now.

sw.note: na-ku-let-e-a = I'm bringing to you: -e- means to or for.

en.text: Twenty bags of lime have been delivered to the plot.

sw.text: Mifuko ishirini ya chokaa imeletwa kiwanjani.
sw.note: i-me-let-w-a = they have been brought: mifuko takes i-.

en.text: I was picked up at the bus station by my friend.

sw.text: Nilichukuliwa na rafiki yangu kwenye stendi.
sw.note: ni-li-chuku-liw-a = I was picked up: her -liw- rule; the doer comes after na.

en.text: I'm not taking your money, it's a gift.

sw.note: si-chuku-i = I'm not taking: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: Don't take me the wrong way, I was only joking.

sw.note: u-si-ni-chukul-i-e = don't take me (wrongly): -si- don't, -ni- me.

en.text: Tomorrow morning I'll go to the chief about the land.

sw.text: Kesho asubuhi nitamwendea chifu kuhusu kiwanja.
sw.note: ni-ta-mw-endea = I will go to him: -endea is going to someone.

en.text: I went to another fundi, and he gave me a better price.

sw.text: Nilimwendea fundi mwingine, akanipa bei nzuri zaidi.
sw.note: ni-li-mw-endea = I went to him; a-ka-ni-pa = and he gave me.

en.text: If you have a problem, go to our neighbour, he's a good man.

sw.text: Ukipata shida, mwendee jirani yetu, ni mtu mzuri.
sw.note: mw-endee = go to him: the person sits inside the command.

en.text: I'll walk you to the main road.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-sindikiza = I'll walk with you part of the way.

en.text: Don't bother seeing me off, I'll take a boda.

sw.note: u-si-ji-sumbue = don't trouble yourself; ku-ni-sindikiza = to see me off.

en.text: Yesterday I saw my fiancée off at the airport.

sw.text: Jana nilimsindikiza mchumba wangu mpaka uwanja wa ndege.
sw.note: ni-li-m-sindikiza = I saw her off: -m- is her.

en.text: All right, the money has been returned to my M-Pesa.

sw.text: Haya, pesa zimerudishwa kwenye M-Pesa yangu.
sw.note: zi-me-rudish-w-a = it has been sent back: pesa takes zi-.

en.text: When you're done, bring the keys back here.

sw.note: rudisha = give back: rudi (come back) + -ish- = make it come back.

en.text: Mama, you haven't given me my change back.

sw.note: hu-ja-ni-rudish-i-a = you haven't given back to me: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: Don't give him all the money, give him half first.

sw.text: Usimpe pesa zote, mpe nusu kwanza.
sw.note: u-si-m-pe = don't give him; m-pe = give him: kupa drops its ku-.

en.text: I was given this shirt by my fiancée.

sw.text: Shati hili nilipewa na mchumba wangu.
sw.note: ni-li-pew-a = I was given: in the passive kupa becomes kupewa.

en.text: If you give me his number, I'll call him right now.

sw.text: Ukinipa namba yake, nitampigia sasa hivi.
sw.note: u-ki-ni-pa = if you give me: with -ni- in place, ku- drops.

en.text: I'll give you an answer tomorrow morning.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-patia = I will give you: her own example was kukupatia.

en.text: Yesterday you didn't give me a receipt, please give it to me today.

sw.text: Jana hukunipatia risiti, naomba unipatie leo.
sw.note: hu-ku-ni-patia = you didn't give me; u-ni-pati-e = that you give me.

en.text: We were given a really nice room in Watamu.

sw.note: tu-li-pati-w-a = we were given: the passive of patia.

en.text: I'm looking for the land office, where is it?

sw.text: Natafuta ofisi ya ardhi, iko wapi?
sw.note: na-tafuta = I'm looking for: the short form of ninatafuta.

en.text: Find me a boda, I'm late.

sw.note: ni-tafut-i-e = find for me: -i- for, and -e asks.

en.text: I looked for my helmet everywhere, I didn't find it.

sw.text: Nilitafuta helmeti yangu kila mahali, sikuipata.
sw.note: si-ku-i-pata = I didn't find it: -ku- for the negative past, -i- the helmet.

en.text: Show me where to park the motorbike.

sw.note: ni-onyesh-e = show me: a request with -ni- inside.

en.text: I'll show you my land on Saturday.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-onyesha = I will show you: -ku- is you.

en.text: I was shown the way by a fisherman.

sw.note: ni-li-onyesh-w-a = I was shown: the doer comes after na.

en.text: Excuse me, can you direct me to the market?

sw.note: ku-ni-elekeza = to direct me: -ni- is me.

en.text: If you direct me well, I'll get there myself.

sw.note: u-ki-ni-elekeza = if you direct me: -ki- if, -ni- me.

en.text: We were given the wrong directions, and we ended up in Kilifi instead of Watamu.

sw.text: Tulielekezwa vibaya, tukafika Kilifi badala ya Watamu.
sw.note: tu-li-elekez-w-a = we were directed; tu-ka-fika = and then we got to.

en.text: Follow me, I'll show you the way.

sw.note: ni-fuat-e = follow me: a request with -ni- inside.

en.text: I'm at the bus station, I've come to pick you up.

sw.note: ku-ku-fuata = to come for you: in Kenya kufuata also means to pick up.

en.text: A dog followed me from the beach all the way home.

sw.text: Mbwa alinifuata kutoka ufukweni mpaka nyumbani.
sw.note: a-li-ni-fuata = it followed me: animals take a- like people.

en.text: Don't be a stranger, my friend.

sw.note: u-si-pote-e = don't get lost: people say it for don't be a stranger.

en.text: I got lost the first time I came to Malindi.

sw.text: Nilipotea mara ya kwanza nilipokuja Malindi.
sw.note: ni-li-potea = I got lost; ni-li-po-kuja = when I came.

en.text: I won't get lost again, I've put the map on my phone.

sw.text: Sitapotea tena, nimeweka ramani kwenye simu yangu.
sw.note: si-ta-potea = I won't get lost: -ta- in the negative future.

en.text: Let's go around the old town a bit before dark.

sw.text: Tuzunguke mji wa zamani kidogo kabla ya giza.
sw.note: tu-zunguk-e = let's go around: the -e ending makes let's.

en.text: We went around the whole town looking for a hardware shop.

sw.text: Tulizunguka mji mzima tukitafuta duka la vifaa.
sw.note: tu-ki-tafuta = while we looked for: -ki- also means while.

en.text: My land is surrounded by mango trees.

sw.note: ki-me-zunguk-w-a = it has been surrounded: -w- makes it passive.

en.text: We're almost there, just five minutes left.

sw.note: tu-me-karibia = we have come close: we're almost there.

en.text: Our wedding is getting close, we still have a lot to do.

sw.text: Harusi yetu inakaribia, bado tuna mengi ya kufanya.
sw.note: i-na-karibia = it is coming close: harusi takes i-.

en.text: Don't go near that dog, it bites.

sw.note: u-si-karibi-e = don't go near: -si- and the -e ending.

en.text: I want to walk to Mambrui tomorrow morning.

sw.text: Nataka kutembea mpaka Mambrui kesho asubuhi.
sw.note: nataka ku-tembea = I want to walk.

en.text: I want my parents to come and visit us.

sw.note: ku-tu-tembelea = to visit us: tembelea is the applied form of tembea.

en.text: I don't walk on the beach alone at night.

sw.note: si-tembe-i = I don't walk: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: I've learned ten new words today.

sw.note: ni-me-ji-funza = I have learned: -ji- is self, so it means teach yourself.

en.text: If I learn five words every day, I'll speak well next year.

sw.text: Nikijifunza maneno matano kila siku, nitaongea vizuri mwakani.
sw.note: ni-ki-ji-funza = if I learn: -ki- for if.

en.text: I still haven't learned to count to a thousand.

sw.text: Bado sijajifunza kuhesabu mpaka elfu moja.
sw.note: si-ja-ji-funza = I haven't learned yet: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: My teacher teaches me Kiswahili every Tuesday and Thursday.

sw.text: Mwalimu wangu ananifunza Kiswahili kila Jumanne na Alhamisi.
sw.note: a-na-ni-funza = she teaches me: -ni- is me.

en.text: I've been taught to say shikamoo to elders.

sw.note: ni-me-funz-w-a = I have been taught: passive -w-.

en.text: Teach me to say that in Kiswahili.

sw.note: ni-funz-e = teach me: a request with -ni- inside.

en.text: Where do you teach?

sw.note: u-na-fundish-i-a = you teach at: the -i- ending points at the place.

en.text: When we have children, I'll teach them Kiswahili and English.

sw.text: Tukipata watoto, nitawafundisha Kiswahili na Kiingereza.
sw.note: ni-ta-wa-fundisha = I will teach them: -wa- is them.

en.text: I read a short story in Kiswahili, and I understood almost all of it.

sw.text: Nilisoma hadithi fupi kwa Kiswahili, nikaelewa karibu yote.
sw.note: ni-li-soma = I read; ni-ka-elewa = and then I understood.

en.text: Read this to me, I can't read it yet.

sw.note: ni-som-e-e = read to me: -e- for, the last -e asks; ku-i-soma = to read it.

en.text: How is this word read?

sw.note: li-na-som-w-a = it is read: passive -w-; neno takes li-.

en.text: Every night I write five sentences in my notebook.

sw.text: Kila usiku naandika sentensi tano kwenye daftari langu.
sw.note: na-andika = I write: the short form of ninaandika.

en.text: I'll write you a message in Kiswahili tonight.

sw.text: Nitakuandikia ujumbe kwa Kiswahili leo usiku.
sw.note: ni-ta-ku-andik-i-a = I will write to you: -i- for or to.

en.text: Is this sentence written correctly?

sw.note: i-me-andik-w-a = it has been written: sentensi takes i-.

en.text: If I repeat it out loud three times, I don't forget.

sw.text: Nikirudia kwa sauti mara tatu, sisahau.
sw.note: ni-ki-rudia = if I repeat; si-sahau = I don't forget: loans keep their -u.

en.text: All right, I'll repeat these sentences until I've memorized them.

sw.text: Haya, nitarudia sentensi hizi mpaka nizikariri.
sw.note: ni-ta-rudia = I will repeat; mpaka ni-zi-kariri = until I memorize them.

en.text: Please say that sentence again, I want to record it.

sw.text: Tafadhali rudia sentensi hiyo, nataka kuirekodi.
sw.note: rudia = say it again: the bare verb is a command.

en.text: My teacher explained the meaning of this proverb to me.

sw.text: Mwalimu wangu alinieleza maana ya methali hii.
sw.note: a-li-ni-eleza = she explained to me: -ni- is me.

en.text: Explain it to me in English first, then in Kiswahili.

sw.text: Nielezee kwa Kiingereza kwanza, kisha kwa Kiswahili.
sw.note: ni-elez-e-e = explain to me: -e- for, the last -e asks.

en.text: If you explain it to me slowly, I'll understand.

sw.note: u-ki-ni-eleza = if you explain to me: -ki- for if.

en.text: Is my Kiswahili understandable now?

sw.note: ki-na-elew-ek-a = it can be understood: Kiswahili takes ki-.

en.text: I didn't understand what he said, he spoke really fast.

sw.note: si-ku-elewa = I didn't understand; a-li-cho-sema = what he said.

en.text: One day I'll understand everything, God willing.

sw.text: Siku moja nitaelewa kila kitu, Mungu akipenda.
sw.note: ni-ta-elewa = I will understand; Mungu a-ki-penda = if God wills.

en.text: Am I pronouncing this word right?

sw.note: na-tamka = I'm pronouncing: -na- for right now.

en.text: My teacher corrects me when I pronounce something wrong.

sw.note: ni-ki-tamka = when I pronounce; hu- is for what she always does.

en.text: Do you remember me? We met in Watamu last year.

sw.note: u-na-ni-kumbuka = do you remember me: -ni- is me.

en.text: I don't remember where I parked the motorbike.

sw.note: si-kumbuk-i = I don't remember: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: Our wedding day will be remembered forever.

sw.text: Siku ya harusi yetu itakumbukwa milele.
sw.note: i-ta-kumbuk-w-a = it will be remembered: siku takes i-.

en.text: Don't forget to buy bread on your way back.

sw.note: u-si-sahau = don't forget: a loan verb keeps its -u.

en.text: Yesterday I forgot to lock the gate at the plot.

sw.text: Jana nilisahau kufunga geti la kiwanja.
sw.note: ni-li-sahau = I forgot: the past with -li-.

en.text: I've left the keys inside, and the door has locked itself.

sw.text: Nimesahaulia funguo ndani, na mlango umejifunga.
sw.note: ni-me-sahau-li-a = I've forgotten them in a place: -li- points at where.

en.text: Remind me to call the fundi at nine.

sw.note: ni-kumbush-e = remind me: -ni- me, the -e asks.

en.text: Don't worry, I'll remind you tomorrow morning.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-kumbusha = I will remind you: -ku- is you.

en.text: My phone reminds me to meditate at six in the morning.

sw.text: Simu yangu hunikumbusha kutafakari saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: hu-ni-kumbusha = it reminds me, as a habit: hu- for every day.

en.text: Let me know when you get there safely.

sw.note: ni-ju-lish-e = let me know: -lish- turns jua (know) into inform.

en.text: This restaurant is known for fish in coconut sauce.

sw.text: Mkahawa huu unajulikana kwa samaki wa kupaka.
sw.note: u-na-ju-lik-an-a = it is known: mkahawa takes u-.

en.text: I won't know until I ask my fiancée.

sw.note: si-ta-jua = I won't know; mpaka ni-mw-uliz-e = until I ask her.

en.text: I'm thinking about buying a new motorbike.

sw.note: na-fikiria = I'm thinking about: fikiria is to think something over.

en.text: Let's think it over first before we pay.

sw.note: tu-fikiri-e = let's think it over: the -e ending makes let's.

en.text: If you think about it carefully, you'll see what I mean.

sw.note: u-ki-fikiria = if you think about it; ni-na-cho-maanisha = what I mean.

en.text: What do you think of this colour for the wall?

sw.text: Unafikiri nini kuhusu rangi hii ya ukuta?
sw.note: u-na-fikiri nini = what do you think: -na- for right now.

en.text: I thought today was Saturday!

sw.note: ni-li-fikiri = I thought: loans like fikiri keep their -i.

en.text: I don't think the fundi will come today, the rain is really heavy.

sw.text: Sifikiri fundi atakuja leo, mvua ni kubwa sana.
sw.note: si-fikiri = I don't think: a loan's negative keeps its -i.

en.text: I think my fiancée has forgotten her phone here.

sw.text: Nadhani mchumba wangu amesahau simu yake hapa.
sw.note: na-dhani = I think, I suppose: a little less sure than nafikiri.

en.text: A lot of people assume I'm American, but I'm from Canada.

sw.text: Watu wengi hudhani mimi ni Mmarekani, lakini natoka Kanada.
sw.note: hu-dhani = they usually assume: hu- for what keeps happening.

en.text: I didn't think you'd come this early.

sw.note: si-ku-dhani = I didn't think; u-nge-kuja = you would come.

en.text: Can you translate this message for me?

sw.note: ku-ni-tafsiri-a = to translate for me: a loan adds -a for for.

en.text: All my sentences have been translated into Kiswahili.

sw.text: Sentensi zangu zote zimetafsiriwa kwa Kiswahili.
sw.note: zi-me-tafsiri-w-a = they have been translated: loans take -iwa.

en.text: I don't want to translate in my head, I want to think in Kiswahili.

sw.text: Sitaki kutafsiri kichwani, nataka kufikiri kwa Kiswahili.
sw.note: sitaki ku-tafsiri = I don't want to translate; nataka ku-fikiri = I want to think.

en.text: I want to speak Kiswahili with my fiancée every day.

sw.text: Nataka kuongea Kiswahili na mchumba wangu kila siku.
alt: Ninataka kuongea Kiswahili na mchumba wangu kila siku.
sw.note: nataka ku-ongea = I want to speak: ku- is the to-form.

en.text: If you speak slowly, I understand everything.

sw.text: Ukiongea pole pole, naelewa kila kitu.
sw.note: u-ki-ongea = if you speak: -ki- means if or when.

en.text: What are you guys talking about? Why are you laughing?

sw.note: m-na-ongel-e-a = you (all) are talking about: ongelea is ongea plus about.

en.text: My fiancée says the wedding will be really beautiful.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu anasema harusi itakuwa nzuri sana.
sw.note: a-na-sema = she says; i-ta-kuwa = it will be: harusi takes i-.

en.text: If you need anything, just say.

sw.note: u-ki-hitaji = if you need; sema = say: a command is the bare verb.

en.text: What you said about lime is true.

sw.note: u-li-cho-sema = what you said: -cho- means the thing that.

en.text: Tell me the last price.

sw.note: ni-ambi-e = tell me: a request with an object ends in -e.

en.text: I told the builders to come at eight.

sw.note: ni-li-wa-ambia = I told them; wa-je = that they come; saa mbili = eight o'clock.

en.text: I've been told there's a good fundi in Watamu.

sw.note: ni-me-ambi-w-a = I have been told: the passive adds -w-.

en.text: Listen to me first, then decide.

sw.note: ni-sikiliz-e = listen to me; u-amu-e = then you decide: both are -e requests.

en.text: When I'm at the gym, I listen to Kiswahili on my phone.

sw.text: Nikiwa jimu, nasikiliza Kiswahili kwenye simu yangu.
sw.note: ni-ki-wa = when I am; na-sikiliza = I listen to.

en.text: The fundi doesn't listen, he does what he wants.

sw.note: ha-sikiliz-i = he doesn't listen: the negative ends in -i.

en.text: Sorry, I didn't hear you properly.

sw.note: si-ku-ku-sikia = I didn't hear you: the first -ku- is the past, the second is you.

en.text: I've heard you got a new job, congratulations!

sw.note: ni-me-sikia = I've heard: news you have just heard takes -me-.

en.text: If you hear any news, let me know.

sw.note: u-ki-sikia = if you hear; ni-julish-e = let me know.

en.text: I haven't talked to my parents this week.

sw.text: Sijazungumza na wazazi wangu wiki hii.
sw.note: si-ja-zungumza = I haven't talked: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: We talked about the wedding all night.

sw.note: tu-li-zungumz-i-a = we talked about: the -i- ending adds about.

en.text: Let's talk about the price before we start.

sw.note: tu-zungumz-e = let's talk; kabla ha-tu-ja-anza = before we start: kabla takes the not-yet form.

en.text: Can I ask you something?

sw.note: ni-ku-uliz-e = may I ask you? The -e form asks permission.

en.text: My mom asked about you yesterday.

sw.note: a-li-ku-uliz-i-a = she asked about you: the -i- ending points at the person.

en.text: Today I've been asked three times where I'm from.

sw.text: Leo nimeulizwa mara tatu natoka wapi.
sw.note: ni-me-uliz-w-a = I have been asked: the passive adds -w-.

en.text: If I answer wrong, correct me.

sw.note: ni-ki-jibu = if I answer; ni-rekebish-e = correct me.

en.text: The landlord hasn't answered me yet, I'll call him again.

sw.text: Mwenye nyumba hajanijibu bado, nitampigia tena.
sw.note: ha-ja-ni-jibu = he hasn't answered me yet: -ja- not yet, -ni- me.

en.text: Why have you gone quiet? Are you upset?

sw.note: u-me-nyamaza = you have gone quiet: -me- for a state that holds now.

en.text: I kept quiet because I didn't understand.

sw.note: ni-li-nyamaza = I kept quiet; si-ku-elewa = I didn't understand.

en.text: Call me when you get to the gate.

sw.note: ni-pig-i-e = call me: -i- for, -e asks; u-ki-fika = when you arrive.

en.text: This photo was taken at the beach in Watamu.

sw.note: i-li-pig-w-a = it was taken: kupiga picha is to take a photo, -w- makes the passive.

en.text: I called my mom twice, but she didn't pick up.

sw.text: Nilimpigia mama yangu mara mbili, lakini hakupokea.
sw.note: ni-li-m-pigia = I called her: -m- her; ha-ku-pokea = she didn't pick up.

en.text: Let's keep in touch, my friend.

sw.note: tu-wasilian-e = let's keep in touch: the -e ending makes let's.

en.text: We haven't been in touch for a long time, how are you?

sw.text: Hatujawasiliana kwa muda mrefu, habari yako?
sw.note: ha-tu-ja-wasiliana = we haven't been in touch: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: When I'm in Nairobi, I'll keep in touch with the fundi by phone.

sw.text: Nikiwa Nairobi, nitawasiliana na fundi kwa simu.
sw.note: ni-ki-wa = when I am; ni-ta-wasiliana = I will keep in touch.

en.text: What's this called in Kiswahili?

sw.note: i-na-it-w-a = it is called: kuita is to call, -w- makes the passive.

en.text: The neighbour's kids call me Uncle Ambi.

sw.text: Watoto wa jirani wananiita Mjomba Ambi.
sw.note: wa-na-ni-ita = they call me: -ni- me.

en.text: Call me when my turn comes.

sw.note: ni-it-e = call me: a request ends in -e; i-ki-fika = when it comes.

en.text: Can I charge my phone here?

sw.note: naweza ku-chaji = can I charge: a loan verb like chaji keeps its -i.

en.text: I didn't charge my phone last night, the battery's almost dead.

sw.text: Sikuchaji simu jana usiku, chaji inakaribia kuisha.
sw.note: si-ku-chaji = I didn't charge: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: Charge this phone for me, I'll come back later.

sw.note: ni-chaj-i-e = charge it for me: -i- for, -e asks.

en.text: I turn off my phone when I meditate.

sw.note: na-zima = I turn off; ni-ki-tafakari = when I meditate.

en.text: Don't turn off the computer, I'm still uploading the video.

sw.note: u-si-zim-e = don't turn off: -si- and the -e ending.

en.text: I forgot to turn off the outside light.

sw.note: nimesahau ku-zima = I forgot to turn off: the second verb takes ku-.

en.text: Sit here, I'll turn on the fan for you.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-wash-i-a = I will turn on for you: -ku- you, -i- for.

gloss.g: i will turn on for you

en.text: I can't turn on my laptop.

sw.note: si-wez-i ku-washa = I can't turn on: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: Has the water pump been turned on?

sw.note: i-me-wash-w-a = it has been turned on: pampu takes i-, -w- makes the passive.

en.text: I lost my wallet in Mombasa last year.

sw.text: Nilipoteza pochi yangu Mombasa mwaka jana.
sw.note: ni-li-poteza = I lost: -li- is the past.

en.text: I've lost my phone, can you call it real quick?

sw.text: Nimepoteza simu yangu, unaweza kuipigia haraka?
sw.note: ni-me-poteza = I have lost; ku-i-pigia = to call it: -i- stands for simu.

en.text: I don't want to waste time, I have three videos to finish.

sw.text: Sitaki kupoteza muda, nina video tatu za kumaliza.
sw.note: sitaki ku-poteza muda = I don't want to waste time: kupoteza is to lose or to waste.

en.text: I want to change Canadian dollars into shillings.

sw.text: Nataka kubadilisha dola za Kanada kuwa shilingi.
sw.note: nataka ku-badilisha = I want to change; kuwa here means into.

en.text: I've changed my number, this is the new one.

sw.text: Nimebadilisha namba yangu, hii ndiyo mpya.
sw.note: ni-me-badilisha = I have changed: -me- for what is done now.

en.text: Don't worry, the wedding date hasn't been changed.

sw.note: ha-i-ja-badilish-w-a = it hasn't been changed: -ja- not yet, -w- the passive.

en.text: I don't work for a boss, I do my own work.

sw.text: Sifanyi kazi kwa bosi, nafanya kazi yangu mwenyewe.
sw.note: si-fany-i = I don't do: the negative present ends in -i; na-fanya = I do.

en.text: I'll do it for you tomorrow morning.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-fany-i-a = I will do for you: -ku- you, -i- for.

gloss.g: i will do it for you

en.text: The roof work was done by fundis from Watamu.

sw.text: Kazi ya paa ilifanywa na mafundi wa Watamu.
sw.note: i-li-fany-w-a na = it was done by: the passive adds -w-, the doer comes after na.

en.text: I want to hire someone to help me edit videos.

sw.text: Nataka kuajiri mtu wa kunisaidia kuhariri video.
sw.note: nataka ku-ajiri = I want to hire; mtu wa ku-ni-saidia = someone to help me.

en.text: I hired a fundi from Kilifi, he's really good.

sw.text: Nilimwajiri fundi kutoka Kilifi, ni hodari sana.
sw.note: ni-li-mw-ajiri = I hired him: mw- before a vowel.

en.text: If I hire you, you'll start on Monday.

sw.note: ni-ki-ku-ajiri = if I hire you: -ki- if, -ku- you.

en.text: I haven't started editing yet.

sw.note: si-ja-anza = I haven't started: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: Starting tomorrow, I'll get up at four in the morning.

sw.text: Kuanzia kesho, nitaamka saa kumi alfajiri.
sw.note: ku-anz-i-a = starting from: anza plus -i-; saa kumi alfajiri = four a.m.

en.text: When I start work, I don't want to be disturbed.

sw.note: ni-ki-anza = when I start; ku-sumbu-liw-a = to be disturbed: the -liw- passive.

en.text: I've finished two videos, there's one left.

sw.note: ni-me-maliza = I have finished; i-me-baki = it remains: video takes i-.

en.text: Let me finish up this video real quick, then let's go.

sw.text: Ngoja nimalizie video hii haraka, halafu twende.
sw.note: ngoja ni-maliz-i-e = let me finish up: the -i- form means finishing off.

en.text: When I finish all three videos, I'll go to the gym.

sw.text: Nikimaliza video zote tatu, nitakwenda jimu.
alt: Nikimaliza video zote tatu, nitaenda jimu.
sw.note: ni-ki-maliza = when I finish; ni-ta-kwenda keeps ku- because kwenda is a short verb.

en.text: Is the work on the walls going well?

sw.note: i-na-endelea = it is going on: kazi takes i-.

en.text: I'll keep working until three in the afternoon.

sw.text: Nitaendelea na kazi mpaka saa tisa mchana.
sw.note: ni-ta-endelea na = I will carry on with; saa tisa mchana = three p.m.

en.text: If the rain keeps up, the fundis won't work tomorrow.

sw.text: Mvua ikiendelea, mafundi hawatafanya kazi kesho.
sw.note: i-ki-endelea = if it continues: mvua takes i-; ha-wa-ta-fanya = they won't do.

en.text: I left the laptop uploading the video and went to the gym.

sw.text: Niliacha kompyuta ikipakia video, nikaenda jimu.
sw.note: i-ki-pakia = while it uploads: -ki- also means while; ni-ka-enda = and then I went.

en.text: Please don't leave the work halfway.

sw.note: u-si-ach-e = don't leave: -si- plus the -e ending.

en.text: I'll leave the keys with the guard for you.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-ach-i-a = I will leave for you: -ku- you, -i- for.

en.text: Today I've spent the whole day at the computer.

sw.text: Leo nimeshinda siku nzima kwenye kompyuta.
sw.note: ni-me-shinda = I have spent (the day): kushinda also means to win.

en.text: I tried, but I couldn't fix the sound.

sw.note: ni-li-shind-w-a = I failed, I couldn't: the passive of shinda.

en.text: If our team wins today, the sodas are on me!

sw.text: Timu yetu ikishinda leo, soda ni juu yangu!
sw.note: i-ki-shinda = if it wins: timu takes i-; ni juu yangu = it's on me.

en.text: I passed the Kiswahili test!

sw.note: ni-me-faulu = I have passed: loan verbs keep their final -u.

en.text: If you keep going like this, you'll succeed.

sw.note: u-ki-endelea = if you keep going; u-ta-faulu = you will succeed.

en.text: I haven't succeeded yet, but I won't give up.

sw.note: si-ja-faulu = I haven't succeeded yet; kukata tamaa = to give up (to cut hope).

en.text: I want to record a video at the beach as the sun rises.

sw.text: Nataka kurekodi video ufukweni jua likichomoza.
sw.note: nataka ku-rekodi = I want to record; li-ki-chomoza = as it rises: jua takes li-.

en.text: I didn't record anything yesterday, the wind was too strong.

sw.text: Sikurekodi chochote jana, upepo ulikuwa mkali sana.
sw.note: si-ku-rekodi = I didn't record: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: Sing it again, I'll record it for you.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-rekodi-a = I will record for you: a loan verb adds -a to mean for.

en.text: In the afternoon I edit tomorrow's videos.

sw.note: na-hariri = I edit: loan verbs like hariri keep their final -i.

en.text: I haven't finished editing, give me ten minutes.

sw.note: si-ja-maliza ku-hariri = I haven't finished editing; nipe = give me.

en.text: All the videos have been edited, only the uploading is left.

sw.text: Video zote zimehaririwa, bado kupakia tu.
sw.note: zi-me-harir-iw-a = they have been edited: loans take -iwa, and video zote takes zi-.

en.text: The video's still uploading, the internet is slow.

sw.text: Video bado inapakiwa, intaneti iko polepole.
sw.note: i-na-paki-w-a = it is being uploaded: pakia becomes pakiwa.

en.text: When the internet comes back, I'll upload the video tonight.

sw.text: Intaneti ikirudi, nitapakia video leo usiku.
sw.note: i-ki-rudi = when it comes back; ni-ta-pakia = I will upload.

en.text: The video didn't upload last night, the power went out.

sw.text: Video haikupakiwa jana usiku, stima ilipotea.
sw.note: ha-i-ku-paki-w-a = it wasn't uploaded: -ku- is the negative past, -w- the passive.

en.text: Where can I download this music for free?

sw.text: Naweza kupakua wapi muziki huu bure?
sw.note: naweza ku-pakua = can I download: kupakua is to take down, to download.

en.text: Just serve me a little, I'm full.

sw.note: ni-pakul-i-e = serve me: kupakua also means to dish out food.

en.text: The song has been downloaded, it's on the laptop.

sw.note: u-me-paku-liw-a = it has been downloaded: her -liw- rule; wimbo takes u-.

en.text: My book will be published next year.

sw.note: ki-ta-chapish-w-a = it will be published: kitabu takes ki-.

en.text: Can you print this for me? Two copies.

sw.note: ku-ni-chapish-i-a = to print for me: -ni- me, -i- for.

en.text: I'm making a new video about Malindi.

sw.note: na-tengeneza = I am making: kutengeneza is to make or to fix.

en.text: I'll make you guys a video of your wedding.

sw.note: ni-ta-wa-tengenez-e-a = I will make for you all: -wa- you (all), -e- for.

gloss.g: i will make for you all

en.text: My motorbike hasn't been fixed yet.

sw.note: ha-i-ja-tengenez-w-a = it hasn't been fixed yet: -ja- not yet, -w- the passive.

en.text: The laptop's broken down on me in the middle of a video.

sw.note: i-me-ni-haribik-i-a = it has broken down on me: -ni- me, -i- on.

gloss.g: it has broken down on me

en.text: If the laptop breaks down, all my work will be lost.

sw.text: Kompyuta ikiharibika, kazi yangu yote itapotea.
sw.note: i-ki-haribika = if it breaks down; i-ta-potea = it will be lost.

en.text: My microphone got damaged by sea water.

sw.text: Maikrofoni yangu iliharibika kwa maji ya bahari.
alt: Kipaza sauti changu kiliharibika kwa maji ya bahari.
sw.note: i-li-haribika = it got damaged: -li- is the past, and maikrofoni takes i-.

en.text: Watch this video real quick and tell me what you think.

sw.text: Angalia video hii haraka, uniambie unaonaje.
sw.note: angalia = watch: a command is the bare verb; u-ni-ambi-e = and tell me.

en.text: My video has been watched by ten thousand people!

sw.text: Video yangu imeangaliwa na watu elfu kumi!
sw.note: i-me-angali-w-a = it has been watched: the passive of angalia is angaliwa.

en.text: I don't watch TV, I only watch YouTube.

sw.note: si-angali-i = I don't watch: the final -a becomes -i in the negative.

en.text: Draw me a map to your place.

sw.note: ni-chor-e-e = draw for me: -e- for, and the last -e asks.

en.text: I draw the pictures for my videos myself.

sw.text: Picha za video zangu nazichora mwenyewe.
sw.note: na-zi-chora = I draw them: -zi- stands for picha.

en.text: I'm building my house near Malindi.

sw.text: Najenga nyumba yangu karibu na Malindi.
sw.note: na-jenga = I am building, short for ninajenga.

en.text: The walls are being built with earth, not blocks.

sw.text: Kuta zinajengwa kwa udongo, si kwa matofali.
sw.note: zi-na-jeng-w-a = they are being built: kuta takes zi-.

en.text: When the house is finished, I'll build a courtyard in the middle.

sw.note: i-ki-kamilika = when it is finished; ni-ta-jenga = I will build.

en.text: The fundi is building me a small room for the tools.

sw.text: Fundi ananijengea chumba kidogo cha vifaa.
sw.note: a-na-ni-jeng-e-a = he is building for me: -e- for.

en.text: They didn't dig the well yesterday, the machine broke down.

sw.note: ha-wa-ku-chimba = they didn't dig.

en.text: The foundation has been dug, now we're waiting for the stones.

sw.note: u-me-chimb-w-a = it has been dug: msingi takes u-.

en.text: Dig here, not over there.

sw.note: chimb-eni = dig, all of you: -eni speaks to many.

en.text: We'll plaster the walls with lime, not paint from the shop.

sw.text: Tutapaka kuta chokaa, si rangi ya dukani.
sw.note: tu-ta-paka = we will apply: kupaka chokaa = to plaster with lime.

en.text: The door has been painted blue.

sw.note: u-me-pak-w-a = it has been painted: mlango takes u-.

en.text: Put some lotion on, the sun is strong.

sw.note: ji-pak-e = put it on yourself: -ji- is self.

en.text: Cover the lime, it's going to rain.

sw.note: funika = cover: a command.

en.text: The roof will be covered with makuti.

sw.note: li-ta-funik-w-a = it will be covered: paa takes li-.

en.text: We haven't covered the well yet.

sw.note: ha-tu-ja-funika = we haven't covered it yet.

en.text: The fundi uncovered the pipe and saw it was leaking.

sw.note: a-li-funua = he uncovered; a-ka-ona = and then he saw.

en.text: When the walls are uncovered, you'll see good work.

sw.note: zi-ki-funu-liw-a = when they are uncovered: her -liw- rule; kuta takes zi-.

en.text: Uncover it for me, I want to see.

sw.note: ni-funul-i-e = uncover it for me.

en.text: We won't knock down the old wall, we'll repair it.

sw.note: ha-tu-ta-vunja = we won't break; tu-ta-u-rekebisha = we'll repair it (u- = ukuta).

en.text: A window was broken last night.

sw.note: li-li-vunj-w-a = it was broken: dirisha takes li-.

en.text: Be careful, don't break the tiles.

sw.note: u-si-vunj-e = don't break.

en.text: Don't step on the floor, it's still wet.

sw.note: u-si-kanyag-e = don't step on it.

en.text: Someone stepped on my foot in the matatu.

sw.note: a-li-ni-kanyaga = he stepped on me.

en.text: The grass here has been trampled by the cows.

sw.note: zi-me-kanyag-w-a na = it has been trampled by.

en.text: I've hired a lorry to carry the stones.

sw.note: ni-me-kodi = I have hired.

en.text: I'll hire a tractor for you if you need it.

sw.note: ni-ta-ku-kodi-a = I will hire for you; u-ki-hitaji = if you need.

en.text: I moved away from Canada two years ago.

sw.note: ni-li-hama = I moved away: kuhama is leaving a place.

en.text: We won't move out of this house until ours is ready.

sw.text: Hatutahama nyumba hii mpaka yetu iwe tayari.
sw.note: ha-tu-ta-hama = we won't move out; i-we = it be (after mpaka).

en.text: When we move, I'll give the fridge to the neighbour.

sw.note: tu-ki-hama = when we move; ni-ta-m-pa = I will give him.

en.text: I moved to the coast because of the peace here.

sw.text: Nilihamia pwani kwa sababu ya amani ya huku.
sw.note: ku-ham-i-a = move to: the applied -i- points at the new place.

en.text: We'll move into the new house in March.

sw.note: tu-ta-hamia = we will move into.

en.text: Have you moved in already?

sw.note: m-me-sha-hamia = have you (all) already moved in?

gloss.g: have you all already moved in

en.text: I've lived on the coast for two years now.

sw.text: Nimeishi pwani kwa miaka miwili sasa.
sw.note: ni-me-ishi = I have lived.

en.text: I want to live near the ocean all my life.

sw.text: Nataka kuishi karibu na bahari maisha yangu yote.
sw.note: nataka ku-ishi = I want to live.

en.text: I don't live in Canada anymore.

sw.note: si-ish-i = I don't live: the negative ends in -i.

en.text: Sit here, it's cooler.

sw.note: kaa = sit: the bare verb is a command.

en.text: I'll stay in Nairobi for three days.

sw.note: ni-ta-kaa = I will stay: kukaa is to stay, too.

en.text: This chair is taken.

sw.note: ki-me-ka-liw-a = it has been sat on: the seat is taken.

en.text: Only two days are left before the wedding.

sw.text: Zimebaki siku mbili tu kabla ya harusi.
sw.note: zi-me-baki = they remain: siku takes zi-.

en.text: Stay here, I'll be back quickly.

sw.note: baki = stay (behind): a command.

en.text: I've only got one thousand left.

sw.note: i-me-ni-bak-i-a = it is left over for me: the applied -i-.

en.text: I've got used to the heat now.

sw.note: ni-me-zoea = I have got used to it.

en.text: I haven't got used to the mosquitoes yet.

sw.note: si-ja-zoea = I haven't got used to it yet.

en.text: Once you get used to it, you'll love life here.

sw.note: u-ki-zoea = when you get used to it.

gloss.g: when you get used to it

en.text: The neighbours welcomed me really well.

sw.note: wa-li-ni-karibisha = they welcomed me: -ni- is me.

en.text: We were welcomed with young coconuts.

sw.note: tu-li-karibish-w-a = we were welcomed.

en.text: I'll welcome everyone to the new house.

sw.note: ni-ta-wa-karibisha = I will welcome them.

en.text: God willing, my parents will visit us.

sw.note: wa-ta-tu-tembelea = they will visit us.

en.text: I've never visited Mombasa Old Town.

sw.text: Sijawahi kutembelea Mji wa Kale Mombasa.
sw.note: si-ja-wahi ku-tembelea = I have never visited.

en.text: We were visited by the neighbours yesterday.

sw.note: tu-li-tembele-w-a = we were visited.

en.text: I'm going to plan my week tonight.

sw.note: ni-ta-panga = I will plan.

en.text: Everything has been planned, don't worry.

sw.note: ki-me-pang-w-a = it has been planned: kila kitu takes ki-.

en.text: We're renting a house in Malindi until ours is finished.

sw.text: Tunapanga nyumba Malindi mpaka yetu ikamilike.
sw.note: kupanga nyumba = to rent a house; i-kamilik-e: mpaka takes the -e form.

en.text: I've decided, I'm going to build with lime, not cement.

sw.text: Nimeamua, nitajenga kwa chokaa, si saruji.
sw.note: ni-me-amua = I have decided; ni-ta-jenga = I will build.

en.text: Decide now, the fundi is waiting.

sw.note: amua = decide: the bare verb is a command.

en.text: It was decided that we'd meet on Saturday.

sw.note: i-li-amu-liw-a = it was decided: her -liw- rule.

en.text: Let me try again.

sw.note: ngoja ni-jaribu = let me try: loan verbs keep their -u.

en.text: I tried to call you, but the network was bad.

sw.text: Nilijaribu kukupigia, lakini mtandao ulikuwa mbaya.
sw.note: ni-li-jaribu ku-ku-pigia = I tried to call you.

en.text: If you try it, you'll like it.

sw.note: u-ki-jaribu = if you try.

en.text: I wanted to buy a phone yesterday but I couldn't.

sw.text: Nilitaka kununua simu jana lakini sikuweza.
sw.note: Her sentence: ni-li-taka = I wanted; si-ku-weza = I couldn't.

en.text: I can't come today, but I can tomorrow.

sw.text: Siwezi kuja leo, lakini naweza kesho.
sw.note: si-wez-i = I can't: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: It's possible to finish by Friday.

sw.note: i-na-wez-ek-an-a = it is possible: -ek- makes can-be.

en.text: I won't be able to come to the gym tomorrow.

sw.note: si-ta-weza = I won't be able to.

en.text: You should rest after the session.

sw.note: u-na-paswa ku- = you should.

en.text: I should have told you earlier.

sw.note: ni-li-paswa = I should have: the past of should.

en.text: After the gym I need a lot of water.

sw.text: Baada ya jimu nahitaji maji mengi.
sw.note: na-hitaji = I need, short for ninahitaji.

en.text: Cement isn't needed for these walls.

sw.note: ha-i-hitaj-ik-i = it isn't needed: -ik- makes be-needed.

en.text: I want to finish three videos today.

sw.note: nataka ku- = I want to.

en.text: I don't want to rush, let's do it properly.

sw.note: si-tak-i = I don't want; tu-fany-e = let's do.

en.text: You're supposed to pay before you start.

sw.note: u-na-tak-iw-a = you're wanted to: you're supposed to.

en.text: I wish you a good day.

sw.note: na-ku-tak-i-a = I wish you: -i- for.

en.text: I'm expecting the builders at eight.

sw.note: na-tarajia = I'm expecting; saa mbili = eight o'clock.

en.text: The rain was expected yesterday, but it didn't come.

sw.note: i-li-tarajiw-a = it was expected; ha-i-ku-nyesha = it didn't rain.

en.text: Make sure the door is locked.

sw.note: hakikisha = make sure; u-me-fung-w-a = it has been locked.

en.text: I assure you, it will be done well.

sw.note: na-ku-hakikish-i-a = I assure you: make sure for you.

en.text: I've run five kilometres on the beach this morning.

sw.text: Nimekimbia kilomita tano ufukweni asubuhi hii.
sw.note: ni-me-kimbia = I have run.

en.text: I want to run before the sun comes up.

sw.note: nataka ku-kimbia = I want to run.

en.text: When I run, I don't take my phone.

sw.note: ni-ki-kimbia = when I run; si-beb-i = I don't carry.

en.text: Today I'm going to skip rope for ten minutes.

sw.text: Leo nitaruka kamba kwa dakika kumi.
sw.note: kuruka kamba = to skip rope; ni-ta-ruka = I will jump.

en.text: I can't jump today, my knee hurts.

sw.note: si-wez-i ku-ruka = I can't jump; goti takes li-.

en.text: The boys jumped into the water from the rocks.

sw.text: Vijana walirukia majini kutoka kwenye miamba.
sw.note: wa-li-ruk-i-a = they jumped into: the applied -i- points at where.

en.text: I lifted forty kilos today.

sw.note: ni-me-inua = I have lifted.

en.text: Lift it with your legs, not your back.

sw.text: Kiinue kwa miguu, si kwa mgongo.
sw.note: ki-inu-e = lift it: -ki- for the weight (chuma).

en.text: This bar can't be lifted by one person.

sw.text: Chuma hiki hakiinuliwi na mtu mmoja.
sw.note: ha-ki-inu-liw-i = it isn't lifted: her -liw- rule, in the negative.

en.text: Stretch your legs after the session.

sw.note: nyoosha = stretch: a command.

en.text: I stretch for ten minutes every morning.

sw.text: Mimi hunyoosha mwili dakika kumi kila asubuhi.
sw.note: hu-nyoosha = I stretch, every day.

en.text: When I stretch my back, the pain goes away.

sw.note: ni-ki-nyoosha = when I stretch.

en.text: Help me push the motorbike, it won't start.

sw.note: ni-saidi-e = help me; ku-sukuma = to push.

en.text: Don't push, there's room for everyone.

sw.text: Msisukume, kuna nafasi kwa kila mtu.
sw.note: m-si-sukum-e = don't push, all of you.

en.text: I got pushed in the queue at the bank.

sw.note: ni-li-sukum-w-a = I was pushed.

en.text: Pull the rope slowly.

sw.note: vuta = pull: a command.

en.text: The fishermen pulled the nets up onto the beach.

sw.note: wa-li-vuta = they pulled.

en.text: The boat was pulled out of the water.

sw.note: i-li-vut-w-a = it was pulled.

en.text: Breathe slowly, you're doing well.

sw.note: pumua = breathe: a command.

en.text: After running, I couldn't breathe properly.

sw.text: Baada ya kukimbia, sikuweza kupumua vizuri.
sw.note: si-ku-weza ku-pumua = I couldn't breathe.

en.text: I'm breathing well now, thank God.

sw.note: ni-na-pumua = I am breathing.

en.text: I'll try hard to come every day.

sw.note: ni-ta-ji-tahidi = I will push myself: -ji- is self.

en.text: Push yourself, only five left!

sw.note: ji-tahidi = push yourself.

en.text: I tried hard, but my legs were tired.

sw.note: ni-li-ji-tahidi = I tried hard.

en.text: I feel like I have a bit of a fever.

sw.note: na-hisi = I feel: hisi is a loan verb, so it keeps its -i.

en.text: I'm sick, I won't come to the gym today.

sw.note: na-umwa = I'm sick; si-ta-kuja = I won't come: kuja keeps its ku- after -ta-.

en.text: I'm a bit hurt, but it's all good.

sw.text: Nimeumia kidogo, lakini ni sawa tu.
sw.note: ni-me-umia = I'm hurt: -me- is for the state you are in now.

en.text: I've recovered, I'll be back at the gym on Monday.

sw.note: ni-me-pona = I have recovered; ni-ta-rudi = I will come back.

en.text: Thank you, doctor, I don't feel any pain anymore.

sw.note: si-hisi = I don't feel: a loan verb keeps its -i in the negative too.

en.text: I don't want to get sick before our wedding.

sw.text: Sitaki kuumwa kabla ya harusi yetu.
sw.note: sitaki ku-umwa = I don't want to get sick.

en.text: I was sick last week, but I'm fine now.

sw.text: Niliumwa wiki iliyopita, lakini sasa niko sawa.
sw.note: ni-li-umwa = I was sick; wiki iliyopita = last week, the week that passed.

en.text: I felt dizzy when I woke up.

sw.note: ni-li-hisi = I felt; ni-li-po-amka = when I woke up: -po- means when.

en.text: I fell off the motorbike, but I didn't get badly hurt.

sw.text: Nilianguka na pikipiki, lakini sikuumia sana.
sw.note: ni-li-anguka = I fell; si-ku-umia = I didn't get hurt: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: I felt sick after eating fish last night.

sw.text: Nilijisikia vibaya baada ya kula samaki jana usiku.
sw.note: ni-li-ji-sikia = I felt: -ji- is myself, so I felt myself; vibaya = bad.

en.text: I was treated really well at the clinic in Malindi.

sw.text: Nilitibiwa vizuri sana kwenye kliniki ya Malindi.
sw.note: ni-li-tib-iw-a = I was treated: loan verbs like tibu take -iwa.

en.text: Don't worry, the doctor will treat you.

sw.note: a-ta-ku-tibu = will treat you: -ku- is you, right before the verb.

en.text: My fiancée is feeling unwell, I'm going to take her to the hospital.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu anajisikia vibaya, nitampeleka hospitali.
sw.note: a-na-ji-sikia = she is feeling; ni-ta-m-peleka = I will take her: -m- is her.

en.text: When I get better, we'll go to Watamu together.

sw.note: ni-ki-pona = when I get better: -ki- means when or if.

en.text: When I cough, my chest hurts.

sw.note: ni-ki-kohoa = when I cough; ki-na-ni-uma = it hurts me: kifua takes ki-.

en.text: I hurt my arm carrying bags of lime.

sw.text: Niliumia mkono nikibeba mifuko ya chokaa.
sw.note: ni-li-umia mkono = I hurt my arm; ni-ki-beba = while carrying: -ki- also means while.

en.text: Hold the ladder properly so you don't fall.

sw.note: u-si-anguk-e = so you don't fall: -si- and the -e ending.

en.text: Don't lift that sack on your own, you'll hurt your back.

sw.text: Usiinue gunia hilo peke yako, utaumia mgongo.
sw.note: u-si-inu-e = don't lift; u-ta-umia mgongo = you will hurt your back.

en.text: I treat colds with ginger and honey.

sw.text: Mimi hutibu mafua kwa tangawizi na asali.
sw.note: hu-tibu = I usually treat: hu- is for habits and takes no ni-.

en.text: You're coughing a lot, I've bought you some medicine.

sw.note: ni-me-ku-nunul-i-a = I have bought for you: -ku- you, -i- for.

en.text: I didn't feel well yesterday, that's why I didn't come.

sw.text: Sikujisikia vizuri jana, ndiyo maana sikuja.
sw.note: si-ku-ji-sikia = I didn't feel; si-ku-ja = I didn't come: kuja drops its ku- here.

en.text: I haven't fully recovered, I'm still coughing a little.

sw.note: si-ja-pona = I haven't recovered yet: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: The cold stopped me from going to the gym this week.

sw.text: Mafua yalinizuia kwenda jimu wiki hii.
sw.note: ya-li-ni-zuia = it stopped me: mafua takes ya-, and -ni- is me.

en.text: Can this illness be prevented?

sw.note: ku-zui-w-a = to be prevented: the passive -w-; ugonjwa takes u-.

en.text: A coconut nearly fell on me!

sw.note: nusura takes the -e form; i-ni-anguk-i-e = fall on me: the -i- means on.

en.text: I've really enjoyed today's session.

sw.note: ni-me-furahia = I have enjoyed: what you enjoy comes right after the verb.

en.text: I've meditated, now I'm ready for today.

sw.text: Nimetafakari, sasa niko tayari kwa siku ya leo.
sw.note: ni-me-tafakari = I have meditated: a loan verb, it keeps its final -i.

en.text: I dreamed about you last night.

sw.note: ni-li-ku-ota = I dreamed of you: the person you dream of is the object.

en.text: I believe what the ancient teachers say.

sw.note: na-amini = I believe; wa-na-cho-sema = what they say: -cho- means what.

en.text: The sea is calm today, let's go for a swim.

sw.note: i-me-tulia = it has settled, so it is calm; tu-ka-ogele-e = and let's swim.

en.text: I dreamed I was in Canada, in the snow!

sw.note: ni-li-ota = I dreamed; inside the dream Kiswahili keeps niko, I am.

en.text: Do you mind if I sit here?

sw.note: hu-jal-i = don't you mind: hu- is you in the negative; ni-ki-kaa = if I sit.

en.text: I don't believe it! You've finished the whole wall today?

sw.note: si-amini = I don't believe; m-me-maliza = you all have finished: m- is you, plural.

en.text: I don't long for city life anymore.

sw.note: si-tamani = I don't long for: a loan verb keeps its -i in the negative.

en.text: I was thinking about the wedding all night.

sw.text: Nilikuwa nawaza kuhusu harusi usiku mzima.
sw.note: nilikuwa na-waza = I was thinking: the past of kuwa, then the present.

en.text: My parents really care about me, even though they're far away.

sw.text: Wazazi wangu wananijali sana, ingawa wako mbali.
sw.note: wa-na-ni-jali = they care about me: -ni- is me, right before the verb.

en.text: I've made you some tea, sit down and relax.

sw.note: ni-me-ku-andal-i-a = I have made it for you; u-tuli-e = and relax.

en.text: I didn't dream anything, I slept like a log.

sw.note: si-ku-ota = I didn't dream: -ku- marks the negative past; fofofo = fast asleep.

en.text: Today I'm not going to worry about the breathing, I'll just sit.

sw.text: Leo sitawaza kuhusu pumzi, nitakaa tu.
sw.note: si-ta-waza = I won't think about it: kuwaza is to think, and also to worry.

en.text: I don't care what people will say, I'm going to build with lime.

sw.text: Sijali watu watasema nini, nitajenga kwa chokaa.
sw.note: si-jal-i = I don't care; ni-ta-jenga = I will build.

en.text: I want to meditate at the same time every day, even when we travel.

sw.text: Nataka kutafakari wakati uleule kila siku, hata tukisafiri.
sw.note: nataka ku-tafakari = I want to meditate; tu-ki-safiri = when we travel.

en.text: I won't rest until the house is finished.

sw.note: si-ta-tulia = I won't rest; after mpaka the verb takes -e: i-ish-e.

en.text: I haven't meditated yet, let's talk in forty minutes.

sw.text: Sijatafakari bado, tuongee baada ya dakika arobaini.
sw.note: si-ja-tafakari = I haven't meditated yet; tu-onge-e = let's talk.

en.text: When I meditate, my phone is switched off.

sw.note: ni-ki-tafakari = when I meditate; i-me-zim-w-a = it has been switched off.

en.text: If you go to Watamu just once, you'll long to go back.

sw.text: Ukienda Watamu mara moja tu, utatamani kurudi.
sw.note: u-ki-enda = if you go: kwenda drops its ku- after -ki-; u-ta-tamani = you will long.

en.text: If we wake up early, we'll enjoy the sun coming up.

sw.note: tu-ki-amka = if we wake up; li-ki-chomoza = as it comes up: jua takes li-.

en.text: My fiancée has cooked me pilau, I'm really enjoying it.

sw.text: Mchumba wangu amenipikia pilau, naifurahia sana.
sw.note: a-me-ni-pik-i-a = she has cooked for me; na-i-furahia = I'm enjoying it: -i- is the pilau.

en.text: I'd love my parents to come to the wedding.

sw.text: Natamani wazazi wangu waje kwenye harusi.
sw.note: na-tamani = I long for; wa-j-e = that they come: kuja drops ku- in the -e form.

en.text: This fundi is trusted by everyone here.

sw.text: Fundi huyu anaaminiwa na kila mtu hapa.
sw.note: a-na-amin-iw-a = he is trusted: loan verbs take -iwa; na = by.

en.text: I am grateful because of these blessings.

sw.text: Nashukuru kwa sababu ya hizi baraka.
sw.note: Her sentence: na-shukuru = I'm grateful, the short form of ninashukuru.

en.text: I thank God for this day.

sw.note: na-m-shukuru = I thank him: God takes the object -m-.

en.text: I didn't thank him for the food, I'll call him.

sw.note: si-ku-m-shukuru = I didn't thank him.

en.text: We've been blessed with rain this week.

sw.note: tu-me-barik-iw-a = we have been blessed: loans take -iwa.

en.text: God bless you, my friend.

sw.note: a-ku-bariki = may he bless you: a wish uses the subjunctive.

en.text: May God bless your family.

sw.note: a-i-bariki: familia is an N noun, so its object marker is -i-.

en.text: I'm praying for you.

sw.note: na-ku-omb-e-a = I pray for you: -e- means for.

en.text: Pray for me, I'm travelling tomorrow.

sw.note: u-ni-omb-e-e = pray for me: a request in the -e form.

en.text: I asked the fundi to lower the price.

sw.note: ni-li-mw-omba = I asked him; a-punguz-e = that he lower it.

en.text: Where do people worship around here?

sw.note: hu-abudu = they worship (hu- for what people usually do).

en.text: On Sunday I'm going to worship with my friend.

sw.text: Jumapili nitakwenda kuabudu na rafiki yangu.
sw.note: ni-ta-kwenda ku-abudu = I will go to worship.

en.text: Here God is worshipped in Kiswahili and Arabic.

sw.text: Hapa Mungu anaabudiwa kwa Kiswahili na Kiarabu.
sw.note: a-na-abud-iw-a = he is worshipped: loans take -iwa.

en.text: My neighbour prays five times a day.

sw.text: Jirani yangu husali mara tano kwa siku.
sw.note: hu-sali = prays, as a habit.

en.text: Wait for me, they're still praying at the mosque.

sw.note: wa-na-sali = they are praying; ni-subiri = wait for me.

en.text: We don't eat before we pray.

sw.note: ha-tu-l-i = we don't eat: kula loses ku- in the negative.

en.text: My friend sings in the church choir.

sw.text: Rafiki yangu anaimba kwenye kwaya ya kanisa.
sw.note: a-na-imba = sings: a- is he or she.

en.text: I want to learn to sing that song in Kiswahili.

sw.text: Nataka kujifunza kuimba wimbo huo kwa Kiswahili.
sw.note: nataka ku-jifunza ku-imba = I want to learn to sing.

en.text: That song was sung at our friend's wedding.

sw.text: Wimbo huo uliimbwa kwenye harusi ya rafiki yetu.
sw.note: u-li-imb-w-a = it was sung: wimbo takes u-.

en.text: Sing it for me again!

sw.note: ni-imb-i-e = sing for me: -i- for, -e asks.

en.text: Forgive me, I was late.

sw.note: ni-samehe = forgive me: loans keep their -e.

en.text: I've forgiven him, it's all good.

sw.note: ni-me-m-samehe = I have forgiven him.

en.text: You'll be forgiven if you apologise.

sw.note: u-ta-samehe-w-a = you will be forgiven: the loan keeps its -e and adds -wa.

en.text: I respect the elders here a lot.

sw.note: na-wa-heshimu = I respect them: -wa- them.

en.text: Here in Kenya, elders are very respected.

sw.note: hu-heshim-iw-a = they are respected, as a rule.

en.text: I'm scared of the neighbour's dog.

sw.note: na-ogopa = I'm scared of: what you fear comes straight after the verb.

en.text: Smile, I'm taking your picture!

sw.note: tabasamu = smile: a loan's command is the bare verb; na-ku-piga picha = I'm taking your picture.

en.text: When you're happy, I'm happy too.

sw.note: u-ki-furahi = when you're happy; nami = na mimi, me too.

en.text: I don't get angry quickly.

sw.note: si-kasirik-i = I don't get angry: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: I'm not crying, it's just dust in my eyes!

sw.note: si-li-i = I'm not crying: lia becomes lii in the negative present.

en.text: Your words have really comforted me.

sw.note: ya-me-ni-fariji = they have comforted me: maneno takes ya-, and -ni- is me.

en.text: My parents will be happy to hear this news.

sw.text: Wazazi wangu watafurahi kusikia habari hii.
sw.note: wa-ta-furahi = they will be happy; ku-sikia = to hear.

en.text: She just smiled, she didn't say anything.

sw.note: a-li-tabasamu = she smiled; ha-ku-sema = she didn't say: -ku- marks the negative past.

en.text: We laughed until we cried!

sw.note: tu-li-cheka = we laughed; mpaka tu-ka-lia = until we ended up crying.

en.text: I got really scared when I saw a snake on the plot.

sw.note: ni-li-ogopa = I got scared; ni-li-po-ona = when I saw: -po- means when.

en.text: I won't be afraid to speak Kiswahili anymore.

sw.note: si-ta-ogopa = I won't be afraid: si- with -ta- makes the negative future.

en.text: Don't laugh at me, it's my first time!

sw.text: Usinicheke, ni mara yangu ya kwanza!
sw.note: u-si-ni-chek-e = don't laugh at me: kucheka mtu is to laugh at someone.

en.text: You'll be amazed to see our earth wall.

sw.text: Utashangaa kuona ukuta wetu wa udongo.
sw.note: u-ta-shangaa = you will be amazed; ukuta wa udongo = a wall of earth.

en.text: I'm so happy, my video has been watched by ten thousand people!

sw.text: Nimefurahi sana, video yangu imeangaliwa na watu elfu kumi!
sw.note: ni-me-furahi = I'm happy; i-me-angali-w-a = it has been watched: video takes i-.

en.text: Don't be sad, we'll see each other again next month.

sw.note: u-si-huzunik-e = don't be sad; tu-ta-on-an-a = we'll see each other: -an- is each other.

en.text: I don't want to cry at the wedding, but I know I'll cry!

sw.text: Sitaki kulia harusini, lakini najua nitalia!
sw.note: sitaki ku-lia = I don't want to cry; ni-ta-lia = I will cry.

en.text: Are you angry with me?

sw.note: u-me-ni-kasirik-i-a = have you got angry with me: the -i- ending points at me.

en.text: People are surprised when they hear me speak Kiswahili.

sw.note: hu-shangaa = they are usually surprised; wa-ki-sikia = when they hear.

en.text: My fiancée smiled at me when I walked in.

sw.note: a-li-ni-tabasami-a = she smiled at me: the applied ending points at me.

en.text: The fundis were surprised when I cooked chapati for them.

sw.note: ni-li-po-wa-pik-i-a = when I cooked for them: -po- when, -wa- them, -i- for.

en.text: The fundi got angry when I told him we should knock the wall down.

sw.note: ni-li-po-mw-ambia = when I told him; tu-vunj-e = that we knock it down.

en.text: Every time I walk past, the neighbour's baby laughs at me.

sw.text: Kila nikipita, mtoto wa jirani ananichekea.
sw.note: a-na-ni-chek-e-a = she laughs at me: the -e- ending points at me; ni-ki-pita = I pass.

en.text: I was sad to see the old house being pulled down.

sw.text: Nilihuzunika kuona nyumba ya zamani ikivunjwa.
sw.note: ni-li-huzunika = I was sad; i-ki-vunj-w-a = while it was being pulled down.

en.text: My friend cried with joy when I told her I'm getting married.

sw.text: Rafiki yangu alilia kwa furaha nilipomwambia nitaoa.
sw.note: a-li-lia = she cried; ni-li-po-mw-ambia = when I told her; ni-ta-oa = I will marry.

en.text: I'm going to go and comfort my friend, he's lost his father.

sw.text: Nitakwenda kumfariji rafiki yangu, amefiwa na baba yake.
alt: Nitaenda kumfariji rafiki yangu, amefiwa na baba yake.
sw.note: ku-m-fariji = to comfort him; a-me-fi-w-a na baba = he has lost his father.

en.text: I love you more every day.

sw.note: na-ku-penda = I love you: -ku- is you.

en.text: Do you like the ring?

sw.note: u-me-i-penda = have you liked it: -i- for pete (N).

en.text: I love her for her kindness.

sw.note: na-m-pend-e-a = I love her for: the applied -e- gives the reason.

en.text: I'm going to marry her, and I'll love her forever.

sw.note: ni-ta-mw-oa = I will marry her: kuoa is said of the man.

en.text: When she's married, she'll move to my place.

sw.note: a-ki-o-lew-a = when she is married: kuolewa is said of the woman.

en.text: My friend has never been married.

sw.note: ha-ja-wahi ku-oa = he has never married: kuoa is said of the man.

en.text: We're getting married soon.

sw.note: tu-ta-o-an-a = we will marry each other: -ana is each other.

en.text: They got married in the church near the beach.

sw.text: Walioana katika kanisa karibu na ufukwe.
sw.note: wa-li-o-ana = they married each other.

en.text: How long have you been married?

sw.note: m-me-o-ana = you (two) have married each other.

en.text: Where did you two meet?

sw.note: m-li-kutana = you (all) met: m- is you, many.

en.text: Let's meet at the beach at five.

sw.text: Tukutane ufukweni saa kumi na moja.
sw.note: tu-kutan-e = let's meet; saa kumi na moja = five o'clock.

en.text: When I meet her father, I'll greet him properly.

sw.text: Nikikutana na baba yake, nitamsalimia vizuri.
sw.note: ni-ki-kutana na = when I meet; ni-ta-m-salimia = I will greet him.

en.text: See you tomorrow, my love.

sw.note: tu-on-an-e = let's see each other.

en.text: We haven't seen each other in two weeks.

sw.note: ha-tu-ja-onana = we haven't seen each other yet.

en.text: We'll see each other when I get back from Nairobi.

sw.note: tu-ta-onana = we will see each other; ni-ki-rudi = when I get back.

en.text: I'll invite my parents to the wedding.

sw.note: ni-ta-wa-alika = I will invite them.

en.text: Were you invited to the engagement party?

sw.note: u-li-alik-w-a = were you invited?

en.text: I want to invite all my friends from the gym.

sw.text: Nataka kuwaalika rafiki zangu wote wa jimu.
sw.note: nataka ku-wa-alika = I want to invite them.

en.text: We'll celebrate at her parents' home.

sw.note: tu-ta-sherehekea = we will celebrate.

en.text: We celebrated our engagement with a small party.

sw.text: Tulisherehekea uchumba wetu kwa sherehe ndogo.
sw.note: tu-li-sherehekea = we celebrated.

en.text: Let's not celebrate before everything is ready.

sw.note: tu-si-sherehek-e-e = let's not celebrate.

en.text: Everyone congratulated us.

sw.note: a-li-tu-pongeza = he congratulated us: -tu- us.

en.text: I congratulate the two of you.

sw.note: na-wa-pongeza = I congratulate you (all): -wa- is also you all.

en.text: We were congratulated by all our friends.

sw.note: tu-li-pongez-w-a na = we were congratulated by.

en.text: My parents raised me in Canada.

sw.note: wa-li-ni-lea = they raised me.

en.text: We want to raise our children near the ocean.

sw.text: Tunataka kulea watoto wetu karibu na bahari.
sw.note: tu-na-taka ku-lea = we want to raise.

en.text: Children who grow up on the coast learn to swim early.

sw.text: Watoto wanaolelewa pwani hujifunza kuogelea mapema.
sw.note: wa-na-o-le-lew-a = who are raised: her -lew- rule.

en.text: Where were you born?

sw.note: u-li-za-liw-a = you were born: the passive of kuzaa.

en.text: The neighbour's cow gave birth last night.

sw.text: Ng'ombe wa jirani alizaa jana usiku.
sw.note: a-li-zaa = she gave birth: animals take a-.

en.text: When were you born?

sw.note: u-li-za-liw-a = you were born.

en.text: The neighbour's wife has had a baby girl.

sw.text: Mke wa jirani amejifungua mtoto wa kike.
sw.note: a-me-ji-fungua = she has given birth: said of a woman.

en.text: When she gives birth, we'll go to the hospital to see her.

sw.note: a-ki-ji-fungua = when she gives birth; ku-mw-ona = to see her.

en.text: She hasn't given birth yet, maybe next week.

sw.note: ha-ja-ji-fungua = she hasn't given birth yet.

en.text: I grew up in Canada, but my parents grew up in Jamaica.

sw.text: Nilikulia Kanada, lakini wazazi wangu walikulia Jamaika.
sw.note: ku-kul-i-a = grow up in: the applied -i- points at the place.

en.text: The children are growing fast.

sw.note: wa-na-kua = they are growing.

en.text: When our children grow up, they'll speak Kiswahili.

sw.note: wa-ki-kua = when they grow up.

en.text: I'll look after my parents when they get old.

sw.note: ni-ta-wa-tunza = I will look after them.

en.text: The garden is well looked after.

sw.note: i-na-tunz-w-a = it is looked after: her -w- rule.

en.text: Please look after my motorbike while I'm away.

sw.text: Tafadhali tunza pikipiki yangu nikiwa safarini.
sw.note: tunza = look after; ni-ki-wa = while I am.

en.text: The guard protects the house at night.

sw.note: a-na-linda = he protects.

en.text: The children must be protected from the sun.

sw.text: Watoto lazima walindwe dhidi ya jua.
sw.note: wa-lind-w-e = that they be protected: lazima takes the -e form.

en.text: May God protect you on the journey.

sw.note: a-ku-lind-e = may he protect you.

en.text: The kids play football on the beach every evening.

sw.text: Watoto hucheza mpira ufukweni kila jioni.
sw.note: hu-cheza = they play, every day.

en.text: Let's go and dance at the wedding!

sw.note: tu-ka-chez-e = and let's dance: kucheza is to play and to dance.

en.text: I used to play basketball in Canada.

sw.text: Nilikuwa nikicheza mpira wa kikapu Kanada.
sw.note: ni-li-kuwa ni-ki-cheza = I used to play.

en.text: The fan died last night, it won't come on.

sw.note: i-li-kufa = it died: one-syllable kufa keeps ku- in the past.

en.text: I'm sorry you lost your father.

sw.text: Pole kwa kufiwa na baba yako.
sw.note: kufiwa = to lose someone to death: said with pole.

en.text: The plants will die if they don't get water.

sw.note: i-ta-kufa = they will die; i-si-po-pata = if they don't get.

en.text: I want to farm a small part of my land.

sw.text: Nataka kulima sehemu ndogo ya kiwanja changu.
sw.note: nataka ku-lima = I want to farm.

en.text: The field has been ploughed, now we'll plant.

sw.note: li-me-lim-w-a = it has been ploughed: shamba takes li-.

en.text: The fundi will dig the garden for me.

sw.note: a-ta-ni-lim-i-a = he will dig for me.

en.text: I water the trees every evening.

sw.note: hu-mwagilia = I water, every day.

en.text: Have you watered the mango trees?

sw.note: u-me-mwagilia = have you watered?

en.text: The plants weren't watered yesterday.

sw.note: ha-i-ku-mwagili-w-a = they weren't watered: mimea takes i-.

en.text: We'll harvest the mangoes in December.

sw.note: tu-ta-vuna = we will harvest.

en.text: When we harvest, I'll give the neighbours some.

sw.note: tu-ki-vuna = when we harvest; ni-ta-wa-pa = I will give them.

en.text: The coconuts have already been harvested.

sw.note: zi-me-sha-vun-w-a = they have already been harvested.

en.text: I'm going to keep chickens on my land.

sw.note: ni-ta-fuga = I will keep (animals).

en.text: Do you keep goats?

sw.note: u-na-fuga = do you keep?

en.text: These cows are kept for milk.

sw.text: Ng'ombe hawa wanafugwa kwa ajili ya maziwa.
sw.note: wa-na-fug-w-a = they are kept: cows take wa-.

en.text: Pick me some mangoes from the tree.

sw.note: ni-chum-i-e = pick for me.

en.text: The children picked all the ripe mangoes.

sw.note: wa-li-chuma = they picked; ya-li-yo-iva = that were ripe.

en.text: Don't pick them yet, they're not ripe.

sw.note: u-si-ya-chum-e = don't pick them: -ya- for maembe.

en.text: The ground has dried out, we need rain.

sw.note: i-me-kauka = it has dried: ardhi takes i-.

en.text: The trees will dry up if it doesn't rain.

sw.note: i-ta-kauka = they will dry up; i-si-po-nyesha = if it doesn't rain.

en.text: When the lime dries, we'll paint.

sw.note: i-ki-kauka = when it dries.

en.text: It rained a lot last night.

sw.note: i-li-nyesha = it rained.

en.text: It hasn't rained for a whole month.

sw.note: ha-i-ja-nyesha = it hasn't rained yet.

en.text: The rain caught me on the road.

sw.note: i-li-ni-nyesh-e-a = it rained on me: the applied -e- points at me.

en.text: Every morning I pick up the coconuts that have fallen.

sw.text: Kila asubuhi mimi huokota nazi zilizoanguka.
sw.note: hu-okota = I pick up, every day.

en.text: Pick up the rubbish before the guests arrive.

sw.note: okota = pick up; ha-wa-ja-fika = before they arrive.

en.text: Help me pick up the stones.

sw.note: ni-saidi-e = help me; ku-okota = to pick up.

en.text: I swim in the ocean every Saturday.

sw.note: na-ogelea = I swim.

en.text: I want to swim before the sun gets hot.

sw.text: Nataka kuogelea kabla jua halijawa kali.
sw.note: kabla jua ha-li-ja-wa kali = before the sun gets strong.

en.text: I was warned not to swim when the tide is high.

sw.note: ni-li-ony-w-a = I was warned; ni-si-ogele-e = that I don't swim.

en.text: The wind is blowing hard today.

sw.note: u-na-vuma = it is blowing: upepo takes u-.

en.text: When the wind blows at night, the fan isn't needed.

sw.note: u-ki-vuma = when it blows; ha-i-hitaj-ik-i = it isn't needed.

en.text: There's been no wind for three days, it's very hot.

sw.text: Upepo haujavuma kwa siku tatu, kuna joto sana.
sw.note: ha-u-ja-vuma = it hasn't blown yet.

en.text: The sun is really strong, let's sit in the shade.

sw.note: li-na-waka = it is burning: jua takes li-; tu-ka-e = let's sit.

en.text: The lights aren't on, the power has been cut.

sw.note: ha-zi-wak-i = they aren't on: taa takes zi-; i-me-kat-w-a = it has been cut.

en.text: The motorbike won't start.

sw.note: ha-i-wak-i = it doesn't start: kuwaka is also an engine starting.

en.text: The sun sets at around half past six.

sw.text: Jua huzama saa kumi na mbili na nusu hivi.
sw.note: hu-zama = it sets, every day.

en.text: Be careful, a lot of people have drowned here.

sw.text: Kuwa mwangalifu, watu wengi wamezama hapa.
sw.note: wa-me-zama = they have drowned.

en.text: The fishermen dive for octopus here.

sw.note: hu-zam-i-a = they dive for: the applied -i- means for.

en.text: I got soaked on my way back home.

sw.note: ni-li-lowa = I got soaked; ni-ki-rudi = while I was coming back.

en.text: Don't get wet, you'll catch a cold.

sw.note: u-si-low-e = don't get wet.

en.text: My clothes are soaked from the rain.

sw.note: zi-me-lowa = they are soaked: nguo takes zi-.

en.text: The sun rose at six this morning.

sw.text: Jua lilichomoza saa kumi na mbili asubuhi ya leo.
sw.note: li-li-chomoza = it rose: jua takes li-.

en.text: When the sun comes up, I'm usually on the beach already.

sw.text: Jua likichomoza, mimi huwa niko ufukweni tayari.
sw.note: li-ki-chomoza = when it rises; huwa = usually am.

en.text: Wake me up before the sun rises.

sw.note: ni-amsh-e = wake me; ha-li-ja-chomoza = it hasn't risen yet.

en.text: You look tired today.

sw.note: u-na-onekana = you look (you seem).

en.text: The island can be seen from the beach.

sw.note: ki-na-onekana = it can be seen: kisiwa takes ki-.

en.text: It looks like it's going to rain.

sw.note: i-na-onekana = it seems.

en.text: What happened at the beach yesterday?

sw.note: ki-li-tokea = it happened: nini takes ki-.

en.text: If anything happens, call me.

sw.note: ki-ki-tokea = if it happens; ni-pig-i-e = call me.

en.text: A big wave came out of nowhere.

sw.note: li-li-tokea = it appeared: wimbi takes li-.

en.text: If you can't help me, it's all good.

sw.text: Kama huwezi kunisaidia, ni sawa tu.
sw.note: hu-wez-i = you can't; ku-ni-saidia = to help me: -ni- is me.

en.text: I've been helped so much by the people here.

sw.text: Nimesaidiwa sana na watu wa hapa.
sw.note: ni-me-saidi-w-a = I have been helped: -w- makes it passive, and na = by.

en.text: If you help me carry these, I'll buy you a soda.

sw.note: u-ki-ni-saidia = if you help me; ni-ta-ku-nunul-i-a = I will buy for you.

en.text: If there's anything I can help you with, let me know.

sw.text: Kama kuna chochote ninachoweza kukusaidia, nijulishe.
sw.note: ni-na-cho-weza = that I can: -cho- points back to chochote; ni-julish-e = let me know.

en.text: Are we allowed to swim here?

sw.note: tu-na-ruhus-iw-a = we are allowed: a loan verb takes -iwa in the passive.

en.text: If my fiancée lets me, I'll come.

sw.note: a-ki-ni-ruhusu = if she lets me: -ki- is if, -ni- is me.

en.text: They won't let us in without a ticket.

sw.note: ha-wa-ta-tu-ruhusu = they won't let us: ha- makes the future negative.

en.text: I haven't said no, I'm still thinking about it.

sw.note: si-ja-kataa = I haven't said no: -ja- means not yet.

en.text: My motorbike won't start this morning.

sw.text: Pikipiki yangu imekataa kuwaka asubuhi hii.
sw.note: i-me-kataa kuwaka = it won't start: a machine that won't work has refused.

en.text: I didn't want to turn him down, so I said yes.

sw.note: ku-m-katal-i-a = to turn him down: the -i- ending aims the no at a person.

en.text: If you agree, we'll start training tomorrow at five in the morning.

sw.text: Ukikubali, tutaanza mazoezi kesho saa kumi na moja alfajiri.
sw.note: u-ki-kubali = if you agree; saa kumi na moja alfajiri = five a.m.

en.text: When I asked her to marry me, she said yes.

sw.note: ni-li-po-mw-omba = when I asked her; tu-oan-e = that we marry each other.

en.text: The fundi has agreed to let me pay him half now and half later.

sw.text: Fundi amenikubalia nimlipe nusu sasa na nusu baadaye.
sw.note: a-me-ni-kubali-a = he has agreed for me: the added -a on a loan verb means for.

en.text: The doctor has banned me from carrying heavy things for two weeks.

sw.text: Daktari amenikataza kubeba vitu vizito kwa wiki mbili.
sw.note: a-me-ni-kataza = he has forbidden me; vitu vizito: vi- on both words.

en.text: The guard forbade me from going in without ID.

sw.note: a-li-ni-kataza = he forbade me: -ni- is me.

en.text: We'll see, it depends on the rain.

sw.note: i-na-tegemea = it depends on: i- stands for it, the plan.

en.text: Don't worry, you can count on me.

sw.note: ku-ni-tegemea = to depend on me: -ni- sits right before the verb.

en.text: I was counting on you today, why didn't you come?

sw.text: Nilikuwa nakutegemea leo, kwa nini hukuja?
sw.note: nilikuwa na-ku-tegemea = I was counting on you; hu-ku-ja = you didn't come.

en.text: I'm warning you, this pepper is really hot!

sw.text: Nakuonya, pilipili hii ni kali sana!
sw.note: na-ku-onya = I'm warning you: -ku- is you.

en.text: I warned you, that road is bad when it rains.

sw.text: Nilikuonya, barabara hiyo ni mbaya mvua ikinyesha.
sw.note: ni-li-ku-onya = I warned you; mvua i-ki-nyesha = when it rains.

en.text: I was warned not to ride a motorbike at night.

sw.note: ni-li-ony-w-a = I was warned (passive -w-); ni-si-endesh-e = that I don't ride.

en.text: No worries, it doesn't bother me at all.

sw.note: ha-i-ni-sumbu-i = it doesn't bother me: the negative ends in -i.

en.text: You do your thing, I don't want to bother you.

sw.note: sitaki ku-ku-sumbua = I don't want to bother you.

en.text: When I'm meditating, I don't like being disturbed.

sw.note: ku-sumbu-liw-a = to be disturbed: her -liw- rule for -ua verbs.

en.text: Every morning I greet the vegetable lady in Kiswahili.

sw.text: Kila asubuhi namsalimia mama mboga kwa Kiswahili.
sw.note: na-m-salimia = I greet her: -m- is her or him.

en.text: We greeted each other, and then I told him I'm from Canada.

sw.note: tu-li-salimi-an-a = we greeted each other: -an- means each other.

en.text: You've got greetings from my parents.

sw.note: u-me-salimi-w-a = you have been greeted: the Kenyan way to pass on a hello.

en.text: I didn't say bye to them, I was in a hurry.

sw.note: si-ku-wa-aga = I didn't say goodbye to them: -wa- is them.

gloss.g: i didn't say bye to them

en.text: I've come to say goodbye to you, I'm travelling to Canada tomorrow.

sw.text: Nimekuja kukuaga, nasafiri kwenda Kanada kesho.
sw.note: ku-ku-aga = to say goodbye to you: -ku- is you.

en.text: All right, let me say bye to you all, I have to get up at four in the morning.

sw.text: Haya, ngoja niwaage, lazima niamke saa kumi alfajiri.
sw.note: ngoja ni-wa-ag-e = let me say bye to you all; saa kumi alfajiri = four a.m.

en.text: I joined this gym last month.

sw.text: Nilijiunga na jimu hii mwezi uliopita.
sw.note: ni-li-jiunga na = I joined: kujiunga always takes na.

en.text: Have you joined our WhatsApp group yet?

sw.text: Umeshajiunga na kikundi chetu cha WhatsApp?
sw.note: u-me-sha-jiunga = have you already joined: -sha- adds already.

en.text: You're welcome to join us at the beach tomorrow morning.

sw.text: Karibu ujiunge nasi ufukweni kesho asubuhi.
sw.note: karibu u-jiung-e = you're welcome to join: karibu takes the -e form.

en.text: I want to take part in the beach clean-up on Saturday.

sw.text: Nataka kushiriki usafi wa ufukwe Jumamosi.
sw.note: nataka ku-shiriki = I want to take part: a loan verb keeps its -i.

en.text: Ten people took part in my morning workout today.

sw.text: Watu kumi walishiriki mazoezi yangu ya asubuhi leo.
sw.note: wa-li-shiriki = they took part; mazoezi is a MA noun, so yangu, ya.

en.text: Lots of friends have contributed to our wedding.

sw.note: wa-me-changia = they have contributed: marafiki are people, so wa-.

en.text: If everyone contributes a hundred shillings, we'll get ten thousand.

sw.text: Kila mtu akichangia shilingi mia moja, tutapata elfu kumi.
sw.note: a-ki-changia = if he contributes: kila mtu takes a-.

en.text: Before we finish, would anyone like to contribute?

sw.text: Kabla hatujamaliza, kuna mtu angependa kuchangia?
sw.note: a-nge-penda = he would like: -nge- is polite; kabla takes the not-yet form.

en.text: I attend a Kiswahili class twice a week.
