sw.text: Nahudhuria darasa la Kiswahili mara mbili kwa wiki.
sw.note: na-hudhuria = I attend; mara mbili kwa wiki = twice a week.

en.text: We attended her sister's graduation yesterday.

sw.text: Tulihudhuria mahafali ya dada yake jana.
sw.note: tu-li-hudhuria = we attended; mahafali = a graduation ceremony.

en.text: I won't be able to attend the funeral tomorrow, I'll be in Mombasa.

sw.text: Sitaweza kuhudhuria mazishi kesho, nitakuwa Mombasa.
sw.note: si-ta-weza = I won't be able to; ni-ta-kuwa: kuwa keeps ku- after -ta-.

en.text: I've seen you here a lot, where in Kenya are you from?

sw.text: Nimekuona hapa mara nyingi, unatoka sehemu gani ya Kenya?
sw.note: ni-me-ku-ona = I have seen you: -ku- is you.

en.text: If you see the fundi, tell him to call me.

sw.note: u-ki-mw-ona = if you see him: m- becomes mw- before a vowel.

en.text: I feel sorry for the fishermen, the sea is rough today.

sw.text: Nawaonea huruma wavuvi, bahari imechafuka leo.
sw.note: na-wa-on-e-a huruma = I feel sorry for them: kuonea is see for, feel for.

en.text: I'm going to lead the beach workout on Saturday at six in the morning.

sw.text: Nitaongoza mazoezi ya ufukweni Jumamosi saa kumi na mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: ni-ta-ongoza = I will lead; saa kumi na mbili asubuhi = six a.m.

en.text: I'm not leading the workout today, my shoulder hurts.

sw.note: si-ongoz-i = I'm not leading: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: We were guided by a local at the Gede ruins.

sw.text: Tuliongozwa na mwenyeji kwenye magofu ya Gede.
sw.note: tu-li-ongoz-w-a = we were guided: -w- makes it passive, and na = by.

en.text: I don't want the phone to rule me.

sw.note: i-ni-tawal-e = that it rules me: after sitaki plus a thing, the verb ends in -e.

en.text: Jamaica was also ruled by the British, like Kenya.

sw.text: Jamaika pia ilitawaliwa na Waingereza, kama Kenya.
sw.note: i-li-tawal-iw-a = it was ruled: her -iw- rule for verbs ending in -la.

en.text: Come in, come in, you're welcome.

sw.note: ingia = come in: a command is the bare verb.

en.text: Did you get my message?

sw.note: u-me-pata = have you got it? -me- for what is done now.

en.text: Can you open the gate for me? I'm outside.

sw.note: ku-ni-fungul-i-a = to open for me: -ni- me, -i- for.

en.text: What time does the shop open?

sw.note: li-na-fungu-liw-a = it is opened: her -liw- passive rule.

en.text: Don't open the window, the mosquitoes will come in.

sw.note: u-si-fungu-e = don't open: -si- and the -e ending.

en.text: I'll lock the gate before I sleep.

sw.note: kabla si-ja-lala = before I sleep: kabla takes the not-yet form.

en.text: Close the door for me, dust is coming in.

sw.note: ni-fung-i-e = close it for me: -i- for, -e asks.

en.text: I didn't close the door because my mother said so.

sw.text: Sikufunga mlango kwa sababu mamangu alisema hivyo.
sw.note: Her sentence: si-ku-funga = I didn't close; mamangu is short for mama yangu.

en.text: The doors are always closed when I try to get inside.

sw.text: Milango huwa zimefungwa nikijaribu kuingia ndani.
alt: Milango huwa imefungwa nikijaribu kuingia ndani.
sw.note: Her sentence: milango is M-MI, so the standard is imefungwa (i-); zimefungwa is heard in Kenya.

en.text: Water got into my phone at the beach.

sw.text: Maji yaliingia kwenye simu yangu ufukweni.
sw.note: ya-li-ingia: maji is a MA noun, so ya-.

en.text: When I get inside, I'll switch on the fan.

sw.note: ni-ki-ingia = when I go in.

en.text: I leave the house at five in the morning every day.

sw.text: Natoka nyumbani saa kumi na moja alfajiri kila siku.
sw.note: na-toka = I go out; saa kumi na moja alfajiri = five a.m.

en.text: I don't want to go out today, the sun is too strong.

sw.text: Sitaki kutoka leo, jua ni kali sana.
sw.note: sitaki ku-toka = I don't want to go out.

en.text: I didn't go out yesterday, it rained all day.

sw.text: Sikutoka jana, mvua ilinyesha siku nzima.
sw.note: si-ku-toka = I didn't go out.

en.text: I hid the key under the stone.

sw.note: ni-li-ficha = I hid.

en.text: Where were the keys hidden?

sw.note: zi-li-fich-w-a = they were hidden: funguo takes zi-, passive -w-.

en.text: Don't hide anything from me.

sw.note: u-si-ni-fich-e = don't hide from me: the person is the object.

en.text: If I get a chance, I'll come to the beach.

sw.note: ni-ki-pata = if I get: -ki- for if and when.

en.text: Fresh fish is available at the market in the morning.

sw.note: wa-na-pat-ik-an-a = they can be got: -ik- makes it possible.

en.text: I had my phone stolen yesterday.

sw.note: ni-li-ib-iw-a simu = I had my phone stolen: the person is the subject.

en.text: Someone has stolen my helmet from the bike.

sw.note: a-me-ni-ib-i-a = has stolen from me: -i- here means from.

en.text: Nobody steals here, the guard is good.

sw.text: Hapa hakuna anayeiba, mlinzi ni mzuri.
sw.note: a-na-ye-iba = who steals: -ye- is the person who.

en.text: A fisherman saved a child at the beach yesterday.

sw.note: a-li-mw-okoa = he saved him: mw- before a vowel.

en.text: God is good, they were all saved.

sw.note: wa-li-oko-lew-a = they were saved: her -lew- rule for o verbs.

en.text: If you take a boda, you'll save time.

sw.note: u-ta-okoa muda = you will save time.

en.text: Can I use your charger for ten minutes?

sw.text: Naweza kutumia chaja yako kwa dakika kumi?
sw.note: naweza ku-tumia = can I use: a question needs only the question mark.

en.text: Use just a little water, it's almost finished.

sw.note: tumi-eni = use, all of you: -eni speaks to a group; maji takes ya-.

en.text: I've used up all the data uploading one video.

sw.text: Nimetumia data yote kupakia video moja.
sw.note: ni-me-tumia = I have used; data yote: data is an N noun, so yote.

en.text: I gave away my winter clothes before moving to Kenya.

sw.text: Niligawa nguo zangu za baridi kabla ya kuhamia Kenya.
sw.note: ni-li-gawa = I gave away, I shared out; nguo za baridi = clothes for the cold.

en.text: If we share it out well, the food will be enough for everyone.

sw.text: Tukigawa vizuri, chakula kitatosha kila mtu.
sw.note: tu-ki-gawa = if we share out; chakula takes ki-: ki-ta-tosha.

en.text: We were handed gloves and bags before cleaning the beach.

sw.text: Tuligawiwa glavu na mifuko kabla ya kusafisha ufukwe.
sw.note: tu-li-gaw-iw-a = we were handed out things: her -iw- rule, gawa to gawiwa.

en.text: I'll be at the gym until nine in the morning.

sw.text: Nitakuwa jimu mpaka saa tatu asubuhi.
sw.note: ni-ta-kuwa: kuwa keeps ku- after -ta-; saa tatu asubuhi = nine a.m.

en.text: I wasn't home when you came, sorry.

sw.note: si-ku-wa = I wasn't: kuwa drops ku- in the negative; u-li-po-kuja = when you came.

en.text: Be patient, the fundi is on his way.

sw.text: Uwe na subira, fundi yuko njiani.
sw.note: u-we = be (you): the -e form of kuwa; uwe na subira = have patience.

en.text: When the rains are over, we'll start building the walls.

sw.note: zi-ki-isha = when they end: the rains, many of them, take zi-.

en.text: I want to buy the lime before the money runs out.

sw.text: Nataka kununua chokaa kabla pesa hazijaisha.
sw.note: kabla ha-zi-ja-isha = before it runs out: kabla takes the not-yet form.

en.text: I've run out of data, let me buy some more.

sw.note: i-me-ni-ish-i-a = it has run out on me: the thing is the subject, you are -ni-.

en.text: That's enough, thanks, I'm full.

sw.note: i-na-tosha = it is enough; ni-me-shiba = I'm full: -me- for a state now.

en.text: Ten bags won't be enough, we need twenty.

sw.note: ha-i-ta-tosha = they won't be enough: mifuko is M-MI, so i-.

en.text: Today forty minutes weren't enough for me.

sw.note: ha-zi-ku-ni-tosha = they weren't enough for me: dakika takes zi-.

en.text: Sorry, I've missed three of your calls, I was at the gym.

sw.text: Samahani, nimekosa simu zako tatu, nilikuwa jimu.
sw.note: ni-me-kosa = I have missed; simu zako tatu: simu takes zi- words, zako.

en.text: I haven't missed meditating once this month.

sw.text: Sijakosa kutafakari hata mara moja mwezi huu.
sw.note: si-ja-kosa = I haven't missed; hata mara moja = not even once.

en.text: Don't miss our wedding!

sw.note: u-si-kos-e = don't miss: -si- and the -e ending.

en.text: I've been waiting for the fundi since eight in the morning.

sw.text: Namsubiri fundi tangu saa mbili asubuhi.
sw.note: na-m-subiri tangu = I've been waiting for him since: -na- with tangu.

en.text: Don't wait for me, I'll be a bit late.

sw.note: u-si-ni-subiri = don't wait for me: a loan verb keeps its -i after -si-.

en.text: Sorry, I have to go, I'm expected at home.

sw.note: ni-na-subiri-w-a = I am being waited for: -w- makes it passive.

en.text: Hold on, let me finish my call.

sw.note: ngoja = wait: the bare verb is a command; ni-maliz-e = let me finish.

en.text: I can't wait any longer, I'm going to leave.

sw.note: si-wez-i ku-ngoja = I can't wait: the negative present ends in -i.

en.text: I've waited for you for a whole hour!

sw.note: ni-me-ku-ngoj-e-a = I have waited for you: -e- turns wait into wait for.

proverbs.literal: little by little fills the measure

meaning.en: Small steady efforts add up to something big.

proverbs.literal: chip by chip finishes the log

meaning.en: Keep chipping away and even the big job gets done.

proverbs.text: Chovya chovya humaliza buyu la asali.
proverbs.literal: a dip and a dip finishes the honey gourd

meaning.en: Little by little, small repeated actions finish the whole thing.

proverbs.literal: the beginning of a hundred is one

meaning.en: Everything big starts with the first single step.

proverbs.literal: poor work is not good play

meaning.en: Even humble work beats time spent playing.

proverbs.literal: long steps shorten the journey

meaning.en: Real effort today shortens the road ahead.

proverbs.literal: one who won't accept defeat is not a competitor

meaning.en: A real contender can take a loss and keep going.

proverbs.literal: God does not throw away a person's sweat

meaning.en: Honest work never goes to waste.

proverbs.literal: the one who blisters on the hoe handle does not die of hunger

meaning.en: The one who does the hard work will always eat.

proverbs.literal: one who wants what is under the bed must bend down

meaning.en: If you want something good, you must stoop and work for it.

proverbs.literal: going for nothing is not sitting for nothing

meaning.en: Trying and getting nothing still beats sitting still.

proverbs.literal: when you see them floating, they were built

meaning.en: What looks easy was built by somebody's long, unseen work.

proverbs.literal: one who picks and chooses a hoe is not a farmer

meaning.en: A bad workman blames his tools; a real worker just starts.

proverbs.text: Kila ndege huruka kwa bawa lake.
proverbs.literal: every bird flies with its own wing

meaning.en: Everyone gets there by their own effort, in their own way.

proverbs.literal: every beginning is heavy

meaning.en: The start of anything is the hardest part. Keep going.

proverbs.literal: one who plants carelessly eats carelessly

meaning.en: You harvest exactly the care you put in.

proverbs.literal: nine is close to ten

meaning.en: Don't quit when you are almost finished.

proverbs.literal: hurry hurry has no blessing

meaning.en: Rushing spoils the work. Slow down and it comes out right.

proverbs.literal: slowly slowly is the way to travel

meaning.en: Steady and gentle is how you actually get there.

proverbs.literal: the tortoise's slow pace takes it far

meaning.en: Slow and steady covers a lot of ground.

proverbs.literal: be late but arrive

meaning.en: Better to take your time and get there than rush and fail.

proverbs.literal: patience pulls in good fortune

meaning.en: Patience brings the good thing to you.

proverbs.literal: patience is the key of comfort

meaning.en: Patience is the key that opens relief.

proverbs.literal: the patient one eats the ripe fruit

meaning.en: The one who waits gets the sweet, ready thing.

proverbs.literal: one who stores the unripe eats the ripe

meaning.en: Put something away early, wait, and it ripens for you.

proverbs.literal: spilled water cannot be gathered up

meaning.en: Some things cannot be undone. Think before you act.

proverbs.literal: the hasty one never gets to eat the sweet

meaning.en: In too much of a hurry to taste anything good.

proverbs.literal: the sign of rain is clouds

meaning.en: Watch for the early signs; big things show themselves first.

proverbs.literal: 'wait, wait' hurts the stomach

meaning.en: Putting things off again and again hurts you in the end.

proverbs.literal: after hardship, relief

meaning.en: Hard times don't last; relief comes after them.

proverbs.literal: there is nothing so long that it has no end

meaning.en: Everything, however long, has an end.

proverbs.literal: there is no bad patience

meaning.en: Patience is never the wrong choice.

proverbs.literal: one who won't listen to an elder breaks a leg

meaning.en: Ignore wise advice and you will get hurt.

proverbs.literal: to ask is not stupidity

meaning.en: Asking questions is not foolish; it is how you learn.

proverbs.literal: the one who asks has knowledge

meaning.en: The person who asks ends up being the one who knows.

proverbs.literal: sweet words draw a snake out of its hole

meaning.en: Kind, gentle words can win over even a hard person.

proverbs.literal: one who does not ask has nothing he learns

meaning.en: No questions, no learning.

proverbs.literal: to lose the road is to learn the road

meaning.en: Getting it wrong is how you learn to get it right.

proverbs.literal: bend the fish while it is still fresh

meaning.en: Teach and shape a child while they are young.

proverbs.literal: sense is wealth

meaning.en: Your mind is your riches; what you know can feed you.

proverbs.literal: every door with its own key

meaning.en: Every problem has its own answer. Find the right one.

proverbs.text: Asiyefunzwa na mamaye hufunzwa na ulimwengu.
proverbs.literal: one not taught by his mother is taught by the world

meaning.en: If you won't be taught gently, life will teach you hard.

proverbs.literal: to live much is to see much

meaning.en: The longer you live, the more you have seen.

proverbs.text: Akili ni nywele, kila mtu ana zake.
proverbs.literal: sense is like hair, everyone has their own

meaning.en: Everyone thinks their own way. Respect that.

proverbs.literal: a promise is a debt

meaning.en: What you promised, you owe. Keep your word.

proverbs.literal: the liar's road is short

meaning.en: Lies do not go far. Honesty lasts.

proverbs.literal: a person is people

meaning.en: You are nothing on your own; people make you.

proverbs.literal: unity is strength

meaning.en: Together you are strong.

proverbs.literal: one finger does not crush a louse

meaning.en: One person alone cannot do it; you need another hand.

proverbs.literal: one hearthstone does not hold the pot

meaning.en: One support is not enough; it takes three to hold the pot.

proverbs.literal: where there are many, there is much

meaning.en: Many people means many opinions — and much gets done.

proverbs.literal: let the guest come so the host may be relieved

meaning.en: A guest coming is a blessing on the house.

proverbs.literal: blood is heavier than water

meaning.en: Family ties hold when nothing else does.

proverbs.literal: don't drop your old mat for a passing prayer mat

meaning.en: Don't drop an old friend for a shiny new one.

proverbs.literal: if you don't seal the crack you will build a wall

meaning.en: Fix the small problem now or rebuild the whole thing later.

proverbs.literal: don't wake the sleeper, if you wake him you will sleep

meaning.en: Leave a resting thing alone, or the trouble becomes yours.

proverbs.literal: a sick person is not asked about porridge

meaning.en: When someone is ill, just care for them. Don't ask, do.

proverbs.literal: if you fall ill, have patience

meaning.en: When you're sick, be patient — healing takes its time.

proverbs.literal: one who sleeps early wakes early

meaning.en: Sleep early and the morning is yours.

proverbs.literal: a loudly sounding drum does not last

meaning.en: What roars loudest burns out fastest.
